articles.title: Two youths arrested for possessing narcotics in Vellore
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The police said the duo were on their way to the railway station to go to Chennai, where they planned to sell the drugs
Two youths were arrested by Vellore South police for possession of 1300 narcotic tablets (Tapentadol) near the fort complex in Vellore town on Saturday.
The police identified them as R. Vinoth, 23, and his friend B. Manimaran, 23. They were residents of Vellore town.

Initial inquiry revealed that based on a tip-off to Vellore SP N.U. Sivaraman, special teams were formed to conduct surprise checks in public places in the district. During a surprise check near the fort complex, the team apprehended the suspects.

They checked the duo and their bags, where they found a huge quantity of pharmaceutical drugs in them. Investigation found that the gang had placed an order for tablets with pharmacies online. The tablets were sent by couriers to them.

The police said the duo were on their way to the railway station to go to Chennai, where they planned to sell the drugs. A case was registered and arrested persons were lodged in Central Prison in Vellore. A probe is under way.

articles.title: T.N. may be heading towards a water crisis, unless northeast monsoon comes to the rescue
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: As of now, the aggregate storage in the major 15 irrigation reservoirs is about a third of the combined capacity of the reservoirs. In the corresponding period last year, the combined storage was around 92%
Tamil Nadu may be in for a spell of water crisis and lower rice production this time if the current Northeast monsoon does not come to its rescue.

As of now, the aggregate storage in the major 15 irrigation reservoirs is about a third of the combined capacity of the reservoirs. In the corresponding period last year, the situation was completely different with the combined storage being around 92%.

The State’s largest dam, Mettur, has about 23 thousand million cubic feet (tmcft) but this is hardly enough for the authorities to maintain sustained release of water to farmers, beyond a week, in the Cauvery delta.

The rainfall during the Northeast monsoon has been moderate as the State has received around 240 mm of rainfall against the anticipated 236 mm. It should get at least 260 mm more to be considered comfortable, the most of which should materialise in November. Ordinarily, December yields only about 20% of the total rainfall of the monsoon.

In fact, the existing pattern of rainfall registered by the State so far during the season appears to be more in tune with the forecast made by the Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU), which, in late September, predicted that the State would get 438 mm during the entire monsoon against the normal 434 mm, a deviation of one per cent. The Meteorological department, in its outlook at the beginning of October for the season, referred to the southern peninsular region of the country in general and stated that the expected rainfall “ is most likely to be normal (88-112%) of the Long Period Average (LPA).”

The TNAU, which was more specific in its forecast than the Meteorological department, had anticipated only a normal rainfall for the core districts of the Cauvery delta – Thanjavur, Tiruvarur, Nagapattinam and Mayiladuthurai. Despite the water availability at Mettur not being comfortable and the expectation of a subdued rainfall, farmers have gone in for raising paddy during the samba-thaladi cultivation season to the tune of around 3.62 lakh hectares. Of this, nearly 50% falls under “direct sown“ category of cultivation, which means that seeds are directly sown instead of transplantation. This method is followed in times of water shortage.

But, the problem with water availability seems to be higher in the remaining areas of the State, a reflection of which can be seen in the way the farmers have taken to paddy this time. The paddy coverage in the non-delta areas of the State is about 1.3 lakh hectares shorter than what it was last year. As compared to the previous year’s share (39%) of direct sowing in the overall paddy coverage, this time the method’s share is about 57%. In 2025-26, rice production in the State was 77.5 lakh tonnes, about one lakh tonnes lower than the previous high of 79.07 lakh tonnes during 2021-22.

As part of its efforts for protecting the crop in the Cauvery delta, the State government, at meetings of the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee (CWRC) and the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) on Friday, demanded that Karnataka release around 20. 7 tmcft including the backlog of about 16.9 tmc ft. However, the Authority ratified the decision of the Committee, which had recommended that Karnataka release 3.88 tmcft to Tamil Nadu through 3,000 cubic feet per second (cusecs) per day for 15 days from Saturday (November 7, 2026).

articles.title: T.N. government to withdraw G.O. promoting Dr. Ambedkar Law University Registrar as temporary Director of Legal Studies
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan record the submission that the vacancy would now be filled up as per regular process

Tamil Nadu Government has informed the Madras High Court of its decision to withdraw a Government Order (G.O.) issued on September 8, 2026, temporarily promoting Tamil Nadu Dr. Ambedkar Law University Registrar Gowri Ramesh as the Director of Legal Studies (DLS). It said, the vacancy shall be filled up through a regular process as contemplated under the Special Rules for the Tamil Nadu Collegiate Educational Service.

Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan recorded the submission made by Advocate General Vijay Narayan and disposed of a writ appeal filed against a single judge’s October 1, 2026 order granting an interim stay of the G.O. The Bench also closed the writ petition pending before the single judge since nothing survived in it pursuant to the government’s decision to withdraw the G.O.

Vellore Government Law College principal M. Rajeswaran had initially filed a writ petition in the High Court in June 2026 challenging a Government Order issued on March 3, 2026 allocating full additional charge of the post of DLS to Ms. Gowri. Then, he had contended that a full-time Registrar of the Law University could not be given additional charge of the full time post of DLS too and that it was against the service rules.

The petitioner contended that the vacancy in the post of DLS could be filled up only through direct recruitment, transfer or by promoting those holding the post of principal in any of the government law colleges spread across the State. Stating that he was senior to Ms. Gowri, the petitioner had wondered how could she attend the Syndicate meetings in her ex-officio capacity as the Registrar of the university and also as the DLS.

Justice P.T. Asha had entertained that writ petition on June 30, 2026 and stayed the operation of the March 3, 2026 G.O. When that stay order was taken on appeal by the State, the A-G told the first Division Bench that the State government intends to commence the regular process of appointing the DLS in accordance with Rule 2(a) of the Special Rules and complete it within a period of two months.

The Bench disposed of the writ appeal on July 23, 2026 after taking note that the government had also issued a G.O. on July 21, 2026 giving full additional charge of the post of DLS to a joint secretary in the Law department instead of Ms. Gowri.

Thereafter, the September 8, 2026 G.O. was issued temporarily promoting Ms. Gowri as the DLS by invoking the emergency powers conferred on the government under Section 47(1) of Tamil Nadu Government Servants (Conditions of Service) Act, 2016. Hence, Mr. Rajeswaran had filed yet another writ petition in the High Court on September 29, 2026 challenging the latest G.O.

This time, Justice Mummineni Sudheer Kumar stayed the September 8, 2026 G.O. on the ground that the government ought not to have invoked Section 47(1) of the 2016 Act after having given an undertaking before the Division Bench in July 2026 that the post of DLS would be appointed in accordance with Rule 2(a) of the Special Rules.

When a State appeal against this stay order came up before the first Bench, the latter recorded A-G’s submission that the latest G.O. shall be withdrawn. “The State shall pursue with the promotion process in accordance with law. The statement of Advocate General that in the meantime, the State will take steps to fill up the post temporarily, as was done when the earlier writ appeal was disposed of, is recorded,” the Bench said.

articles.title: Locals burn effigy of Christian priests at Basanti in WB
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: A group of locals at Basanti in West Bengal’s South 24 Parganas on Thursday (November 5, 2026) burnt effigy of local Christian priests and submitted a memorandum to the police station against the local priests. Basanti has been on the boil since November 1 after a newly constructed church was vandalised by a mob claiming their allegiance to a Hindutva outfit.

The protest on Thursday (November 5, 2026) was organised by Adivasi Eilya Parishad, a local organisation whose representatives said that Adivasis are being lured for conversion on the promise of curing disease, which should not be allowed.
The West Bengal chapter of National Christian Council (NCC) in a press statement added that effigy of local priests were set on fire at Chowmatha crossing in Basanti.

“Later in the evening, during the Friday prayer service, a group of approximately 20–25 people allegedly surrounded women attending the service. According to the complaints received, the women were forced to break their traditional conch-shell bangles (Shakha) and wipe off their vermilion (Sindoor),” the press statement said.

Father Parimal Kanji, the priest-in-charge at Basanti, stated that the alleged perpetrators were outsiders and not local residents and confirmed that a written complaint had been submitted to the police.

Arpan Rana, State General Secretary of the National Christian Council said that Christian communities in West Bengal do not seek confrontation but justice, equal protection and the rule of law. “The Chief Minister is speaking about religious freedom, yet the practical experience of some minority communities raises serious questions about their safety and protection,” Mr. Rana said.

Herod Mullick, the founding State Secretary of Bangiya Chrisityo Pariseba said that the government and administration’s silence has emboldened attackers, who have shifted from targeting small independent congregations to raiding older, established churches.

“While the police are well aware of the situation and continue to accept written complaints, no legal action is mysteriously being taken against anyone, making the government’s ongoing silence both baffling and suspicious,” he said.
According to Basanti Police Station, an FIR has been registered in connection with the incident of attack on the Church and notices have been issued to some accused.

There has been an increase in attacks on churches and Christian gatherings after the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) came to power. According to Christian organisations, U.S.-based research project, India Hate Lab, has documented at least 60 incidents of hate crimes and targeted attacks against Christians in West Bengal across 13 districts between May 13 and September 20 this year.

articles.title: Rajnath Singh warns of evolving threats, calls for highest military readiness
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Addressing personnel at key airbase near China frontier, Defence Minister warns of adversaries exploiting ‘vulnerabilities’; he also reviews Army’s LAC infrastructure, operational preparedness and lauds initiatives aimed at strengthening ties with local communities

Defence Minister Rajnath Singh visited members of the armed forces at multiple locations in West Bengal on Saturday (November 7, 2026) and highlighted a changing nature of warfare while describing the northeast as India’s “first edge” rather than its “last edge”.

The security landscape around the country has become increasingly complex and the armed forces must maintain the highest level of operational readiness to effectively counter any threats to national security, he told personnel at the Bagdogra Air Force station. Delivering his message on the eve of Deepavali from the key airbase near the frontier with China in the Eastern sector, Mr. Singh, without naming any country, said the adversary now avoids direct confrontation but seeks to exploit certain "vulnerabilities".

He called upon the armed forces to keep special focus on strengthening domain awareness, cyber resilience, and information integrity to effectively counter emerging security threats, according to the Defence Ministry. Chief of the Air Staff Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, Air Officer Commanding, Air Force Station, Bagdogra Air Commodore Manish Sharma, and other senior officials of the IAF were present on the occasion.

Describing Bagdogra as a strategically important region and a crucial link in India's security framework, Mr. Singh commended the courage and dedication of the defence personnel towards safeguarding national interests. He stated that the Air Force personnel deployed in the region serve as a robust shield for the security of the eastern sector, and their preparedness is fundamental to maintaining stability in the region.

The Defence Minister later reviewed the operational preparedness of the Army’s Trishakti Corps at Sukna, with a focus on infrastructure development along the Line of Actual Control (LAC), deployment of advanced military equipment, and adoption of emerging technologies to enhance combat effectiveness.

Mr. Singh expressed satisfaction with the operational preparedness of the corps and appreciated its contribution to infrastructure development and community welfare initiatives in border areas aimed at strengthening ties with local communities.
Army Chief General Dhiraj Seth, Eastern Army Commander Lt. Gen. VMB Krishnan and Trishakti Corps Commander Lt. Gen. Man Raj Singh Mann were present during the review.

Addressing personnel during a ‘ barakhana ’ on the eve of Deepawali, Mr. Singh commended their courage, professionalism, and dedication in safeguarding the country’s frontiers under challenging operational conditions.

Highlighting the changing nature of warfare, he said security challenges were no longer confined to conventional exchanges of gunfire and artillery but increasingly involved hybrid warfare, proxy wars, cyberattacks, drone incursions, and information warfare.

He cautioned that adversaries were using social media to spread rumours, deploying drones to monitor sensitive locations, and attempting to compromise military systems through cyberattacks. He exhorted personnel to remain vigilant and prepared to tackle emerging threats across all domains.

articles.title: Ten of 11 stations on Kochi metro’s Pink Line to have entry/exit from both sides of road
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Terminal station at Smart City to have entry/exit only on the right hand side; foot overbridge mulled for members of the public to access the station

With about 70% of the viaduct of the Kochi metro’s 11.20-km Kakkanad extension (Pink Line) complete and the laying of tracks set to begin, pending works on all 11 stations in the corridor are set to gather momentum after an initial lull. This is in keeping with the revised deadline of August 2027, which has been set to complete the works on the extension, official sources said.

Contrary to the perception that a few stations will have entry/exit only from one side of the road, 10 of the 11 stations will have entry/exit from both sides of the road beneath the upcoming metro extension. The terminal station, whose work is set to begin on the Smart City premises, will have entry/exit only on the right hand side, while a foot overbridge will provide a link for members of the public to access the station, they added.

The structural work on the entry/exit of the Chittetukara station is over on both the left hand side and the right hand side of the road, while that of the left-hand side of the KINFRA Park station is over. Work on the right hand side of the Vazhakkala station is over, and architectural work has begun. Structural works on the left hand side entry/exit of the stations at Civil Station Junction and Cochin SEZ are scheduled to be completed by the first week of December.
The foundation works of the entry/exit of the Chembumukku station whose land acquisition suffered delay is over, and rest of the works is set to gather pace on both sides of the road, it is learnt.

Metro sources attributed the delay in commencing work on the right hand side entry/exit of Palarivattom Junction and Padamugal stations to hassles associated with land acquisition. The requisite plots of land for the two stations will be acquired by the end of December. The pending works on most metro stations will gather pace in the coming weeks, since the requisite pre-fabricated structures are ready at the casting yard. They will be transported in lorries and launched at the stations concerned. This will be followed by architectural works, laying of tracks, and installation of signals and telecommunication equipment, lifts and escalators, to name a few.

The first station on the Pink Line is at Palarivattom Junction, followed by stations at Alinchuvadu, Chembumukku, Vazhakkala, Padamugal, Civil Station Junction, Cochin SEZ, Chittettukara, KINFRA Park, Infopark, and Smart City.

articles.title: Trump says he wants UFC chief Dana White for White House press secretary
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Mr. White, ⁠chief executive of ⁠the Ultimate Fighting Championship, is a “violent Fighter and Warrior,” Mr. Trump wrote in ​a Truth ‌Social post

Facing an incoming Democratic Congress, U.S. President Donald Trump struck a combative tone Saturday (November 7, 2026), offering friend and “violent fighter” Dana White the White House press secretary job and ordering the Justice Department to investigate his opponents.

Democrats handed Mr. Trump’s Republicans a blowout defeat in the midterm elections this week and will take control of both chambers of Congress in January. They promise robust investigations into Mr. Trump and his administration.
Mr. Trump, however, showed no signs of being chastened.
He offered the press secretary post to Mr. White, a loyal supporter and head of the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) mixed martial arts organisation.
“Dana, please take the job!” Mr. Trump posted on social media, describing White as a “violent Fighter and Warrior.”

Speaking to reporters following a boxing event in London late Saturday (November 7, 2026), Mr. White said he was flying to Washington “right now” and will meet with Mr. Trump on Monday (November 9, 2026).
Mr. White had earlier shared a photo -- possibly AI-generated -- showing him behind the lectern in the White House press briefing room, captioned “On to the next chapter.”
Mr. Trump on Saturday (November 7, 2026) also ordered the Justice Department to investigate Democrats for “extortion at the highest level.”
“The Democrats are going around threatening a lot of people,” he wrote, adding that he was ordering the Justice Department to “look into this criminal act.”
Denying that anyone in his administration had committed impeachable offenses, Trump called for prison time for “these EXTORTIONISTS.”

articles.title: Israeli President picks Gadi Eisenkot, Netanyahu rival, to try to form government
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Mr. Eisenkot, a former military chief, has declined to join forces with Arab parties, with whose support he ‌would have a majority of seats in parliament

Israel’s president on Saturday (November 7, 2026) chose Gadi Eisenkot , Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s strongest rival, to try ‌to form a new government following a deadlocked election that left neither man with ​a clear path to power.

Mr. Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving leader, is fighting to stay in ⁠office after his religious-nationalist coalition lost its majority in an October 27 election but still emerged as the largest bloc in parliament.

Mr. Eisenkot, a former military chief, has declined to join forces with Arab parties, with whose support he ‌would have a majority of seats in parliament. But Arab leaders, incensed by what they view as the racist policies of Mr. Netanyahu and his far-right allies, still nominated Mr. Eisenkot ‌to try to form a government first — giving him the most endorsements.

“President Herzog has invited ‌Gadi ⁠Eisenkot to the President’s Residence, where he will be tasked with forming the government tomorrow,” ⁠said the spokesperson of President Isaac Herzog, whose largely ceremonial role involves nominating a candidate to form a coalition after elections.
Weeks of protracted negotiations are expected to follow Mr. Eisenkot’s nomination. He has 28 days ​to try to forge a government, with a ‌possible 14-day extension.

His potential pathways to power include trying to form a minority government with Arab support from the outside; forming a coalition with ultra-Orthodox parties that he and his allies have shunned in the past; or forging a unity government with Mr. Netanyahu.

Analysts say that all three options ‌are unlikely to take shape. If Mr. Eisenkot fails, another candidate can try to form ​a government and if that candidate fails, parliament can nominate another. There is a deadline for the process of around 100 days. If no one succeeds, another election ⁠is held.
Likud won the most seats of any single party with 27 in the 120-seat Knesset, but Mr. Netanyahu’s wider religious-nationalist coalition garnered only 53 in total, short of a 61-seat majority.

Mr. Eisenkot’s Yashar party emerged as ‌the second-largest party with 21 seats, while his coalition, spanning four centre-left to right-wing Jewish-led parties, won just 48 seats. Two parties representing Israel’s Arab minority won an unprecedented 19 seats.
A son of Moroccan immigrants, Mr. Eisenkot, 66, would be the country’s first Prime Minister from Israel’s Mizrahi community, Jews who trace their roots to West Asia and North Africa.

fullParagraphs: Mr. Yadav said that Mr. Ragi used the abusive language against Yadav community on behest of Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) leader and Rajya Sabha member Sanjay Yadav wrote a letter to President Draupadi Murmu, requesting her to order strict action against Delhi University Professor Sangeet Ragi for allegedly insulting the Yadav community.

Mr. Yadav said that he used the abusive language on behest of Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). He mentioned that action is necessary so that it serves as an exemplary punishment, ensuring that in a diverse country like India, no one dares to insult any society, class or community in the name of freedom of expression, and thus hurting unity and integrity of the nation.
The three-page letter dated November 6, 2026, was shared with media on Saturday (November 7, 2026).

“I am writing to you in my capacity as a Member of Parliament (Rajyasabha) to express my serious concern regarding the alleged caste-based derogatory remarks made by Professor Sangeet Ragi of the University of Delhi against India’s largest community (Yadav/Ahir) during a televised public debate,” Mr. Yadav stated.

He added, “The controversy surrounding the Professor’s remarks has generated considerable public resentment. According to media reports, the remarks reportedly included the use of expressions such as “gawar” in conjunction with the term “Ahir”. The subsequent controversy has raised serious concerns about the use of caste identity, community genealogy and social stereotypes as instruments of public insult and humiliation.”
Mr. Yadav asserted that the matter is particularly disturbing because the individual concerned occupies a responsible academic position at one of India’s most prestigious public universities.

He further said a university professor, especially one associated with political science, is expected to uphold constitutional morality, democratic values, social equality and respect for the dignity of every community.

“A teacher who must be educating his students against societal stereotypes is here himself strengthening unacceptable caste based derogatory stereotypes. Prof. Ragi has been notorious for habitually making indecent and unacceptable remarks and expletives against women folk, dalit community and whole bahujan community from time to time in TV debates,” Mr. Yadav said,
He mentioned that Mr. Ragi’s remarks have caused considerable resentment among members of the affected communities, students and various civil society organisations.

RJD MP explained that the Yadav/Ahir community has a long and complex social, historical and cultural genealogy adding that its identity, like that of every other community, deserves recognition and respect rather than being subjected to ridicule, social stereotyping or derogatory characterisation.

articles.title: 42 days of SRFTI protest; classes suspended till December 11
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Students send message of resistance and fight for justice on Deepavali

The agitation at the Satyajit Ray Film & Television Institute (SRFTI) continued for 42 days as class suspension was extended till December 11, affecting academic life. Students of the film institute on Saturday (November 7, 2026) said that “This Diwali we choose to resist”, while authorities said they were “keen" to resume classes.

“Diwali has always been a special occasion at SRFTI... But this year, the familiar celebrations are overshadowed by fear, uncertainty and an ongoing struggle for justice,” an official post by the SRFTI student union said on Saturday (November 7, 2026), a day before Deepavali. They also said that the day they are served justice will be Deepavali for them.

“While the faculty and administration are ready to resume classes, a section of students continues to remain disengaged from academics and disrupt the functioning of the Institute through repeated violations of its rules and orders,” Registrar Deepak Kumar told The Hindu on Saturday (November 7, 2026). He further added that they are asking students to come forward for constructive dialogue.

As of November 7, at least 25 students have received show cause notices, with 11 of them receiving them last Thursday (November 5, 2026). Six students have faced rustication, and one FIR has been registered against student union Vice-President Shubham.

Shubham is one of the six students who got the rustication notice for allegedly vandalising the Vice-Chancellor Santosh Ajmeera’s office and manhandling him. However, all of these allegations have been denied by the students.
According to the students, two contractual faculty members, and five resource persons of SRFTI have also been terminated from their jobs for showing solidarity with the students.

As the classes remained suspended, the hostels and mess were also closed for students. Many students have been living under a makeshift tent during the protest, as many of them are from States outside West Bengal.

The impasse at the campus started on September 27 after violence broke out on the film institute’s campus as a right-wing RSS-affiliated Akhil Bharatiya Grahak Panchayat (ABGP) held an event on the campus and clashed with students. Several students were left injured in the clashes.

Since then, students have demanded accountability from the authorities for failing to protect them inside their own campus. However, six of them were served a rustication notice two weeks later, on October 15, for manhandling the VC.
The students are also demanding the VC’s resignation for failing to take action against the violence, which left many students injured.

The Presidency University has expelled two students for allegedly defacing Swami Vivekananda posters inside the campus, official sources said. The Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad had alleged that Left student factions had vandalised the poster and had filed a police complaint on October 14.

The two female students have been barred from taking admission in any course at the university in the future. The university had formed a committee to investigate the matter and has checked CCTV footage of the campus and heard from various stakeholders to come to a decision. One of them is a current student and the other was an ex-student who had finished her post-graduate course a few months back.

“Two students have been expelled from the studentship/post-studentship academic activities. It has also been decided that they won’t be allowed admission to any future degree program in this university,” official sources said.

“Presidency University always stood for dignified academic discourse and debate on different scientific/socio-political issues. The university is not in a position to tolerate any abuse to any thinkers/ideas/organizations,” Presidency University registrar Debajyoti Konar said.

The Students’ Federation of India (SFI) condemned the expulsion on Saturday (November 7, 2026). “By imposing an expulsion that threatens to destroy the academic lives of these two students, the administration has established a deeply dangerous precedent,” their statement from the SFI Presidency unit added. They also said that students must be punished if they took part in vandalism, but asked for corrective steps and rehabilitation, rather than punitive or retaliatory measures.
Meanwhile, the ABVP student wing welcomed the expulsion and said that such “anti-India” sentiments and anti-national conspiracies do not have a place in the educational institutes.

“If such incidents are repeated in the future, the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) will once again stand firmly against them. Our message is clear: ABVP possesses the only vaccine capable of eliminating the Chinese virus of anti-national ideology,” Ananta Barui, State Media In-charge, ABVP told T he Hindu on Saturday (November 7, 2026).

The ABVP student wing had previously alleged that the Left student wings were conducting the vandalism of their posters. However, the Left student wings of Presidency had issued a statement and denied the allegations.
“ABVP has started the work of cleaning the Tukde-Tukde gang from Jadavpur and Presidency. This work must be continued,” Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said.

This comes as both Jadavpur University and Presidency University, two of the top-ranking educational institutes of the State, remained embroiled in repeated controversies and face-offs with the right-wing student group. A massive fight had erupted at JU in August as left- and right-wing student groups clashed.

articles.title: A bridge between past and present
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: A German publication ranked Bihar Museum among the best in the world. Mayank Kumar visits to understand what went into the making of the museum and what visitors think of its contribution to the development of Indian civilization

On November 3, Soumya Pathak, 23, a final-year medical student studying at a medical college in Ambala, Haryana, is exploring exhibits showcasing relics from prehistoric times at the Bihar Museum in Patna. Pathak belongs to Muzaffarpur in Bihar, and is looking at some coins from the Mauryan (321–185 B.C.E) and Gupta ages (early 4th to mid-6th Century C.E.).

She passes through interactive galleries which highlight Bihar’s pivotal role in shaping two major world religions: Jainism and Buddhism. “I have been thinking of coming here for a long time, but after reading on social media that the museum is ranked the best in Asia, I decided to spend a day here,” she says. Pathak is enroute to Muzaffarpur for the Deepavali holidays and came to the museum directly from Patna’s Jay Prakash Narayan airport, about four kilometres away. Pathak is proud of her State that is often in the news for poverty and violence.
Political & National Report: A bridge between past and present. This development is a key milestone in India's ongoing legislative, judicial, and constitutional governance framework.

articles.title: Ahead of Deepavali, Chhath festivals, migrants reach Bihar in hordes covering thousands of kilometers
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Four young men on Saturday (November 7, 2026), from Bengaluru, travelled about 2,200 km riding on an old auto-rickshaw to reach Areraj town, in East Champaran

Ahead of Deepavali and the four-day Chhath festival, migrants are visiting different places of Bihar in hordes. With the flight fares skyrocketing and train ticket charts shown full, migrants are reaching their destination by buses and even riding on old auto-rickshaws covering thousands of kilometres.

Four young men on Saturday (November 7, 2026), from Bengaluru, travelled about 2,200 km riding on an old auto-rickshaw to reach Areraj town, near Someshwarnath Dham temple in Motihari of East Champaran district in Bihar.

Reaching their destination in three days, they told local media persons that it was their “desire to celebrate Deepavali and Chhath festival along with family members” and the air ticket fares had gone beyond their capacity. With train ticket charts shown chock-a-bloc they, eventually, decided to travel to their village in Areraj by riding on the old auto-rickshaw, which one of them runs in Bengaluru for a living. The other three who accompanied him in the auto-rickshaw do other causal work in the city for their survival.

The railway department, though, has announced to run special trains for Bihar and other places for the migrants to return to their homes ahead of these two festivals but the returning migrants say there was “no-room available” in the trains.

Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, meanwhile, has directed police officials to be vigilant round-the-clock for the safe return of migrants to their homes. In view of these two major festivals all the leaves for police officials have been cancelled till November 17, a senior official said. The Chhath festival this year begins on November 13 and will continue till November 16.

In neighbouring Jharkhand, private bus operators are plying extra buses for the local people to reach their destinations. From the industrial town of Jamshedpur, the number of buses plying daily for Bihar has increased from 85 to 105 but the owners said, “the demand remains unfulfilled in view of the no-room availability in Bihar bound trains”.

“The demand for additional busses are strong for places like Patna, Chhapra, Siwan, Ara, Muzaffarpur, Bhagalpur, Nawada and Nalanda”, they added. “The sharp rise in demand for more buses is likely to be increased in days to come as the auspicious Chhath festival nears. Many passengers are booking their tickets in advance, through the fare remains unchanged”, said Uday Sharma, a Jamshedpur based bus operator. For several passengers, buses have now become the only option to travel to their destination to celebrate the festival as they claimed, “train reservations have exhausted”.

Rajesh Kumar, a software engineer, though, said he was lucky to have booked air tickets three months ago to reach Patna from Delhi. “Even at that time, the air-fare was almost three times of the normal fare”, he rued. He has spent ₹60,000 only on tickets for his family of four, he said.

“As far as I remember, every year, during this festival time of Diwali and Chhath the ticket prices in flights go manifold and train charts show no-room availability... it’s been going on for long with the same scene of crowded trains and buses reaching the State capital, but no government could do anything on this, except announcing more trains on some routes”, said Sanjay Kumar, a Patna based government employee.

articles.title: FSSAI seizes 3,280 tonne food items, cancels 52 licences in nationwide inspection drive
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The regulator said it inspected 56,431 food establishments during its nationwide enforcement drive between September 1 and November 5, and seized non-compliant food products, including paneer, ghee, milk and sweets

Food Safety and Standards Authority of India has seized 3,280 tonnes of 'banned and non-compliant' food products worth ₹82 crore during its nationwide inspection drive, which began on September 1 to check adulteration during the festive season.
Acting against food safety violations, the FSSAI cancelled 52 licences, suspended 1,133 licences, and sealed 314 establishments.
In a social media post on Saturday (November 7, 2026), the FSSAI said that it has stepped up vigilance in view of festivals.

The regulator said it inspected 56,431 food establishments during its nationwide enforcement drive between September 1 and November 5, and seized non-compliant food products, including paneer, ghee, milk and sweets.

FSSAI led an intensive nationwide inspection drive across States and UTs. Through rigorous checks on over 56,000 food establishments, authorities took decisive action against substandard practices-issuing over 10000 improvement notices and suspending more than 1,100 licences 1(2) https://t.co/Ov7iIZcmdA
A total of 3,279.57 tonnes of 'banned and non-compliant' food products worth ₹81.80 crore were seized, it said.
Additionally, the regulator issued 10,047 improvement notices to food business operators.
This calendar year, the FSSAI has stepped up enforcement actions against food business operators and e-commerce companies to ensure safe food for consumers.

articles.title: Singapore-based senior IT executive shot dead over parking dispute in Faridabad
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The accused fired several rounds at the victim and his son; the victim succumbed to injuries and the son escaped unhurt

A 42-year-old senior executive of a Singapore-based IT services and solutions company was shot dead following a dispute over parking in Faridabad on Friday (November 6, 2026) evening. The police have arrested the accused, identified as Mohan Sharma, a real estate agent who lived on the third floor of the same multi-storey building in Sector 21C where the victim resided with his family.
The victim, Paramjith Dhankhar, had returned from Singapore two days ago to attend a family wedding and celebrate Deepavali with his family.

According to the complaint filed by his 19-year-old son, Shaurya, the accused rang the doorbell of their flat around 8.30 p.m. and asked Mr. Dhankhar, who had returned from the gym a few minutes earlier, to come downstairs and move his car. Shaurya also accompanied his father to the parking area.

An argument reportedly broke out between the two men, following which Mr. Sharma allegedly pulled out a pistol and fired several rounds at Mr. Dhankhar. He also fired at Shaurya, who managed to escape unhurt by taking cover behind parked cars. The accused then fled the spot in his vehicle. Mr. Dhankhar succumbed to his bullet injuries.

“About 14-15 rounds were fired, of which eight or nine reportedly hit the victim. His son, who was present at the spot, escaped unhurt,” said Surajkund police station SHO Inspector Pahlad. The SHO said the two men had differences earlier as well and the accused allegedly used to create disturbances after consuming alcohol.

A case was registered at the Surajkund police station under charges of murder, attempt to murder and criminal conspiracy. The accused was subsequently arrested by the Sector 30 Crime Branch team on Saturday (November 7, 2026).

A 42-year-old senior executive of a Singapore-based IT services and solutions company was shot dead following a dispute over parking in Faridabad on Friday (November 6, 2026) evening. The police have arrested the accused, identified as Mohan Sharma, a real estate agent who lived on the third floor of the same multi-storey building in Sector 21C where the victim resided with his family.

The victim, Paramjith Dhankhar, had returned from Singapore two days ago to attend a family wedding and celebrate Deepavali with his family.

According to the complaint filed by his 19-year-old son, Shaurya, the accused rang the doorbell of their flat around 8.30 p.m. and asked Mr. Dhankhar, who had returned from the gym a few minutes earlier, to come downstairs and move his car. Shaurya also accompanied his father to the parking area.

An argument reportedly broke out between the two men, following which Mr. Sharma allegedly pulled out a pistol and fired several rounds at Mr. Dhankhar. He also fired at Shaurya, who managed to escape unhurt by taking cover behind parked cars. The accused then fled the spot in his vehicle. Mr. Dhankhar succumbed to his bullet injuries.

“About 14-15 rounds were fired, of which eight or nine reportedly hit the victim. His son, who was present at the spot, escaped unhurt,” said Surajkund police station SHO Inspector Pahlad. The SHO said the two men had differences earlier as well and the accused allegedly used to create disturbances after consuming alcohol.

A case was registered at the Surajkund police station under charges of murder, attempt to murder and criminal conspiracy. The accused was subsequently arrested by the Sector 30 Crime Branch team on Saturday (November 7, 2026).

articles.title: Paraguay's ousted President charged with crimes linked to collapse of major bank
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: In a farewell message released shortly before he was ousted on Friday (November 6), Mr. Peña expressed hope his departure would spare Paraguay further harm

Prosecutors in Paraguay on Saturday (November 7, 2026) charged recently deposed former President Santiago Peña with two crimes linked to the collapse of a major bank that has jeopardised the savings of hundreds of thousands of account holders and unleashed the nation's biggest political crisis in a decade.

In a press conference on Saturday (November 7), Nancy Salomón, the South American nation's chief prosecutor for corruption and economic crimes, said Mr. Peña would be investigated for the crimes of breach of trust and administration for personal gain.

Mr. Peña's removal marks a major crisis for Paraguay, which returned to democratic rule in 1989. Since then, the nation of six million people has been mostly governed by the conservative Colorado Party, of which Mr. Peña was a member.

Prosecutors said the former President could face up to 20 years in prison if he is found guilty of both crimes and have asked a judge to freeze Mr. Peña's assets and send him to prison while investigations continue.

Later on Saturday (November 7), Paraguayan Judge Humberto Otazu complied with that request and said Mr. Peña will be held at a military base as investigations continue, in order to “guarantee his compliance” with the anti-corruption probe.

On Tuesday (November 3), regulators in Paraguay intervened in Ueno Bank, freezing the accounts of nearly three million customers and triggering a political crisis that led to Peña's removal by Congress on Friday (November 6) night.

Earlier on Saturday (November 7), Mr. Peña was questioned by prosecutors at the Attorney General's compound, in the capital Asuncion. The former President was not in handcuffs but was escorted by police.

Lawmakers accused Mr. Peña of using his political influence to steer hundreds of millions of dollars in public funds into Ueno while regulators overlooked risky insider lending. Mr. Peña has denied wrongdoing.

Paraguayan prosecutors on Friday (November 6) ordered the arrest of Mr. Peña and former Central Bank chief Carlos Carvallo as part of a criminal investigation into alleged breach of trust and other offenses tied to the collapse of Ueno Bank. Peña was transferred to a military base late Friday (November 6) as hundreds of protesters gathered outside his home.

The arrest order was issued soon after the Senate removed Mr. Peña from office in a unanimous vote. He was replaced by Vice-President Pedro Alliana, who began naming a new Cabinet on Saturday (November 7). The Central Bank said Saturday that 1.2 million Ueno customers had received partial or full reimbursement of their deposits. Under Paraguayan law, deposits of up to $37,000 are insured.

articles.title: Strong earthquake with preliminary magnitude of 5.7 strikes Japan
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: A wide area near Aichi Prefecture was affected, including the city of Hamamatsu, the ancient capitals of Kyoto and Nara and nearby prefectures of Yamanashi, where Mount Fuji is located, as well as Gifu

A strong earthquake shook central Japan early on Sunday (November 8, 2026), shattering store windows, causing people to flee buildings and leaving at least 22 people injured, according to local media.
Japan’s Meteorological Agency put the quake’s magnitude at 5.7, while the U.S. Geological Survey reported it at magnitude 5.5. Smaller aftershocks were reported.

A wide area near Aichi Prefecture was affected, including the city of Hamamatsu, the ancient capitals of Kyoto and Nara and nearby prefectures of Yamanashi, where Mount Fuji is located, as well as Gifu.

Japanese TV footage showed shattered store windows and scattered shards of glass on the streets. A bookstore was left with mounds of books that had flown off the shelves. The injuries included people who fell from stairs while they were trying to flee.

The quake, which struck at 1:04 a.m., was located about 40 kilometres below the earth’s surface in Shizuoka Prefecture. Aichi and Shizuoka are neighbouring regions. They are far enough from Tokyo that the quake was not felt there. The most violent shaking was felt in Aichi, according to official seismic assessments.
The meteorological agency warned people to brace for possible strong quakes in the coming week, especially the next two to three days.
“Please be on the lookout for mudslides, falling rocks and the possible effects from rainfall,” Ayataka Ebita, an agency official, told reporters.
He said no apparent change was detected so far to the Nankai Trough plate, where scientists say a megaquake can possibly hit.
The Shinkansen bullet trains were running at slower speeds in the affected areas as a precautionary measure. Sometimes quakes can damage the railways the trains run on.

Japan is located in an area that is prone to earthquakes. Authorities frequently instruct people to stock up on bottled water, food and batteries, have plans ready to hide under tables and keep comfortable walking shoes at hand.

articles.title: Kerala Water Authority intensifies action against encroachments on Pipeline Road
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Pipeline Road is important for the KWA as the transmission main carrying water from Aruvikkara to the capital city passes through it

The Kerala Water Authority (KWA) has kicked off a major drive to rid the Pipeline Road on the Peroorkada-Aruvikkara stretch of encroachments and unauthorised constructions. The water utility said on Saturday that it has intensified action against encroachers.

As part of the drive, illegal structures were removed at the Vazhayila junction on Friday. The effort will continue in the weeks ahead, the KWA said on Saturday. “These measures are being taken to protect the Pipeline Road and the allied KWA assets and to ensure access for carrying out repairs and maintenance works,” the KWA said.
The Pipeline Road is important for the KWA as the transmission main carrying water from Aruvikkara to the capital city passes through it.

The water utility has requested encroachers to vacate the premises voluntarily, so as to avoid action. KWA officials are also serving notices to encroachers under provisions of the KWA (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupation and Removal of Unauthorised Constructions) Regulations, 2014.

If the encroachers fail to vacate the premises within the timeframe stipulated in the notice, the Executive Engineer concerned will issue the final speaking order. Failure to vacate within the 30-day deadline prescribed in that order will attract eviction measures with the assistance of the police, according to KWA.

In August this year, the KWA had ordered that all permanent, semi-permanent and other encroachments be removed from the Pipeline Road in Kochi. The drive in Kochi was held as part of the preliminary measures for the laying of pipelines to the city from a proposed 190-mld water treatment plant.

articles.title: Revanth challenges KCR for debate on Kaleshwaram, El Niño and Godavari waters in the special Assembly session
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy alleged that the previous government had neglected drinking and irrigation water requirements in the region while prioritising the Kaleshwaram project over the Pranahita project

Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy challenged BRS president and former Chief Minister K. Chandrasekhar Rao to participate in a two-day discussion in the Assembly in December on the Kaleshwaram project, Godavari waters and the anticipated El Niño impact.

Interacting with progressive farmers and agricultural scientists after inaugurating the Mega Rythu Mela and Industrial Expo at Hakimpet village in Dudyala mandal of Vikarabad district, Mr. Reddy appealed to Assembly Speaker Gaddam Prasad Kumar to allow the discussion and said Mr. Rao and his family members should attend so that the facts surrounding the irrigation projects and their implementation could be brought out.

Accusing the previous BRS government of failing to complete even one major irrigation project in undivided Mahabubnagar district during its 10-year tenure, he said people had expected the completion of the Kalwakurthy, Bhima, Nettampadu, Koilsagar and Makthal-Narayanpet-Kodangal lift irrigation projects. Had the Congress formed the government in 2014, these projects would have been completed and the aspirations of the region’s people fulfilled, he claimed.

Mr. Reddy alleged that the previous government had neglected drinking and irrigation water requirements in the region while prioritising the Kaleshwaram project over the Pranahita project, despite the Centre’s offer to accord national project status to the latter.

The Chief Minister said then Irrigation Minister T Harish Rao was reluctant to discuss Medigadda while he claimed himself as ‘Kaleshwar Rao’ claiming himself as the man behind its completion. “After it collapsed he is not even mentioning Medigadda,” charged Mr. Reddy
He also accused Mr. Rao of approaching Prime Minister Narendra Modi to delay the CBI investigation ordered by the State government into the alleged irregularities.

Responding to criticism over the functioning of the Kaleshwaram project and demands to operate the Kannnepalli pump houses, the Chief Minister questioned the purpose of constructing Medigadda if water could be lifted through the pumps independently.
Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy interacting with farmers and officials at the Rythu Mela in Hakimpet village in Vikarabad districct on November 7, 2026.

articles.title: Bombay High Court allows BNS Section 75 charge where complainant identifies as woman
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The judge rejected the argument that Section 75 cannot apply because the complainant is a transgender and not a woman

The Bombay High Court has refused to discharge Vishal Ingle and held that Section 75 of the Bharatiya Nyay Sanhita can apply when the complainant is a transgender who identifies as a woman. Justice Mehroz Pathan passed the order on November 3.

The judge rejected the argument that Section 75 cannot apply because the complainant is a transgender and not a woman. The judge said the complainant identifies as a woman and has taken medicines for hormone changes.

The FIR contains allegations against the applicant of outraging the modesty of the complainant. The complainant identifies as a woman and has undergone treatment for hormone changes. The judge said the FIR contains allegations against the applicant of outraging the modesty of the complainant, who identifies as a woman after hormone therapy. The judge said Section 75 appears to be made out.
The judge said allegations of assault and outraging the modesty of a woman can be sustained when the victim is a transgender who identifies as a woman.
Mr. Ingle served as an Agniveer. The police registered an offence under Section 75 and Section 296 of the BNS and under the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019.

The judge rejected the argument that Section 18(D) of the Act of 2019 is not made out because the complainant did not have a certificate of identity under the Act. The judge said Section 2(k) shows a person may identify as a transgender even without a certificate of identity. Section 5 provides a route to apply to the District Magistrate for a certificate.

The complainant received a certificate of identity on February 12, 2026. The assault took place on October 28, 2025 and October 30, 2025. The judge said the absence of a certificate at the time of the offence does not bar use of the Act of 2019. The judge said the FIR shows Section 18(D) was invoked and the allegations attract the provisions invoked against the applicant.

articles.title: PM Modi to celebrate Deepavali with forces in Bastar that was once den of Maoists
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Prime Minister said Bastar is an area where Maoism once held sway but now, development is flourishing

Prime Minister Narendra Modi will celebrate Deepavali on Sunday (November 8, 2026) along with security personnel in Chhattisgarh's Bastar, which was freed from the clutches of Maoists after several decades.
"Heading to Bastar to celebrate Diwali with our brave security forces," Mr. Modi said in a post on 'X'.
The Prime Minister said Bastar is an area where Maoism once held sway but now, development is flourishing.
"I am going to salute our brave security personnel for their sacrifices, selfless service and unwavering devotion to the nation," he said.
The Central Armed Police Forces and personnel of the Chhattisgarh Police have been deployed in Bastar. They were deeply involved in the anti-Maoist operations.
On March 31 this year, the government had announced that the country was free from the menace of Maoism after the elimination of many leaders and cadres and the surrender of hundreds of others.

While conveying Deepavali greetings on Saturday (November 7, 2026), the Prime Minister said that like the previous year, this time also, he would celebrate the festival along with the brave soldiers of the country.
In a video message posted on his social media handles, Mr. Modi had said that like everyone, he will also celebrate Deepavali with great enthusiasm.
"My heartiest greetings to all of you for Deepavali. I wish for peace, prosperity and happiness for all of you in the coming days. I also celebrate Deepavali like you with great enthusiasm," he said.
The Prime Minister said everyone knows that every year he celebrates Deepavali with the brave soldiers of the country.

articles.title: News in Frames: Many twists in the monsoon’s tale

fullParagraphs: Andhra Pradesh swung from drought to deluge, with two back-to-back cyclones causing an estimated ₹6,500 cr. in damage and leaving at least 17 dead; crops were flattened and coconut trees uprooted, with farmers in the Godavari belt facing at least two years of recovery

A ndhra Pradesh is witnessing two extremes this year: drought and deluge. During the initial monsoon months of June and July, the State declared drought in 388 of its 688 mandals across 28 districts. By the end of October, however, extremely heavy rainfall had battered many of these mandals, except those in Rayalaseema.

Between October 28 and November 3, Andhra Pradesh was hit by two back-to-back cyclones — Very Severe Cyclonic Storm ‘Arnab’ and Severe Cyclonic Storm ‘Murasu’ — leaving the coastal districts in ruins.

With wind speeds reaching 140 kmph during Arnab and 110 kmph during Murasu, the two cyclones are estimated to have caused damage worth approximately ₹6,500 crore. They also left at least 17 people dead, uprooted hundreds of electricity poles and damaged roads across the State. Arnab wreaked havoc in the twin Godavari districts of East and West Godavari and in the north coastal region, including Visakhapatnam.

The destruction was immense, with thousands of coconut trees uprooted and paddy, cotton and chilli crops flattened in West Godavari, East Godavari, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema, Bapatla, Guntur and Palnadu districts. Visakhapatnam, Eluru and East Godavari recorded extremely heavy rainfall of around 260 mm.

Coconut growers in the Godavari belt say it may at least take two years for them to recover the losses. While experts debate whether climate change played a role in these weather events, farmers and fishermen continue to bear the brunt of every disaster.
A similar situation last occurred in 2013, when cyclones Helen and Lehar battered the Andhra Pradesh coast. Before that, the State witnessed similar events in 1987 and 1976.

Rough ride: A motorist navigates a storm-battered street at Mangamaripeta in Visakhapatnam on October 28, a day after Cyclone Arnab brought heavy rain.
Road to recovery: Disaster response personnel work to restore a stretch of road washed away by waves at Uppada coastal village in Kakinada district after Cyclone Arnab.

articles.title: Trump offers UFC boss press secretary post, urges criminal probes of Democrats
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Dana White had earlier shared a photo -- possibly AI-generated -- showing him behind the lectern in the White House press briefing room, captioned “On to the next chapter.”

Facing an incoming Democratic Congress, U.S. President Donald Trump struck a combative tone Saturday (November 7, 2026), offering friend and “violent fighter” Dana White the White House press secretary job and ordering the Justice Department to investigate his opponents.

Democrats handed Mr. Trump’s Republicans a blowout defeat in the midterm elections this week and will take control of both chambers of Congress in January. They promise robust investigations into Mr. Trump and his administration.
Mr. Trump, however, showed no signs of being chastened.
He offered the press secretary post to Mr. White, a loyal supporter and head of the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) mixed martial arts organisation.
“Dana, please take the job!” Mr. Trump posted on social media, describing White as a “violent Fighter and Warrior.”

Speaking to reporters following a boxing event in London late Saturday (November 7, 2026), Mr. White said he was flying to Washington “right now” and will meet with Mr. Trump on Monday (November 9, 2026).
Mr. White had earlier shared a photo -- possibly AI-generated -- showing him behind the lectern in the White House press briefing room, captioned “On to the next chapter.”
Mr. Trump on Saturday (November 7, 2026) also ordered the Justice Department to investigate Democrats for “extortion at the highest level.”
“The Democrats are going around threatening a lot of people,” he wrote, adding that he was ordering the Justice Department to “look into this criminal act.”
Denying that anyone in his administration had committed impeachable offenses, Trump called for prison time for “these EXTORTIONISTS.”

articles.title: Iran says two tankers caught fire in Hormuz after hitting mines
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Since the outbreak of the Iran war in late February, Tehran has severely restricted traffic through the strategic waterway, insisting vessels use routes authorised by the Islamic republic
Two oil tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz after hitting mines, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on Sunday (November 8, 2026), according to state news agency IRNA .
Since the outbreak of the Iran war in late February, Tehran has severely restricted traffic through the strategic waterway, insisting vessels use routes authorised by the Islamic republic.
The United States has in response imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports and helped tankers travel the strait, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption.

"Two oil tankers violating regulations — one in the eastern part of the Strait of Hormuz and the other within the strait — caught fire and are currently engulfed in intense flames after striking naval mines while attempting to cross through unauthorised routes," the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, the ideological arm of Iran's military, said in a statement.

"The two tankers had reportedly committed multiple violations, including switching off their navigation and positioning systems, as they attempted to transit through an unauthorised route," the statement added.
The Guards did not specify the name or nationality of the tankers.
Tehran has made multiple announcements in recent weeks saying that ships have caught fire in the Hormuz strait.

U.S. Central Command said last month that it had helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil via Hormuz since the summer and has recently said that all mines have been cleared from the waterway.
The IRNA separately reported late on Saturday (November 7) that sounds of explosions were heard in parts of the country.
"Sounds resembling explosions were heard in Qeshm, Sirik, Jask, and Bandar Abbas. The cause of the sounds remains unknown," the news agency wrote on Telegram.

articles.title: Body of Punjab anti-drug activist Jhota brought to Mansa for last rites
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Jhota was shot dead in broad daylight at a medical store in a busy marketplace in Mansa town on October 13
The mortal remains of s lain anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota, whose murder last month triggered protests and a political row, were brought to his native place here on Sunday for last rites.
Following a post-mortem at PGIMER in Chandigarh on Saturday (November 7, 2026), Jhota's body was taken to his native place, where last rites would be conducted.

Jhota was shot dead in broad daylight at a medical store in a busy marketplace in Mansa town on October 13. The store owner, who had fired at Jhota after the activist confronted him over the sale of addictive drugs to an elderly man, was subsequently arrested.
A large number of people turned up at his home to pay their last respects before the cremation was held.
On Saturday (November 7, 2026), a member of the joint action committee had said Jhota's cremation would take place at his native place in Mansa on Sunday.
The joint action committee (JAC), also known as the Parminder Singh Jhota Insaaf Action Committee, is a coalition of various social organisations and activists formed in Punjab after Jhota's murder.
The cremation will be held at Jhota's fields on Chakerian Road in Mansa. Jhota's father, Bhim Singh, on Saturday (November 7, 2026) called upon the youth of Punjab to pledge against drug abuse.

"We will take the body to our residence first and thereafter, between 12 and 1 pm, Jhota will be cremated on Diwali Day," said Singh while speaking to reporters in Chandigarh on Saturday (November 7, 2026).

Jhota's body was brought to PGIMER Chandigarh from the mortuary of Civil Hospital in Mansa in the early hours of Friday, after his family ended their 22-day agitation and agreed to a post-mortem following a meeting with Punjab government representatives.
On Friday (November 6, 2026), Jhota's father said he would go on a fast demanding the immediate transfer of Mansa Senior Superintendent of Police Vaibhav Chaudhary.

The mortal remains of s lain anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota, whose murder last month triggered protests and a political row, were brought to his native place here on Sunday for last rites.

Following a post-mortem at PGIMER in Chandigarh on Saturday (November 7, 2026), Jhota's body was taken to his native place, where last rites would be conducted.

Jhota was shot dead in broad daylight at a medical store in a busy marketplace in Mansa town on October 13. The store owner, who had fired at Jhota after the activist confronted him over the sale of addictive drugs to an elderly man, was subsequently arrested.

A large number of people turned up at his home to pay their last respects before the cremation was held.

On Saturday (November 7, 2026), a member of the joint action committee had said Jhota's cremation would take place at his native place in Mansa on Sunday.

The joint action committee (JAC), also known as the Parminder Singh Jhota Insaaf Action Committee, is a coalition of various social organisations and activists formed in Punjab after Jhota's murder.

The cremation will be held at Jhota's fields on Chakerian Road in Mansa. Jhota's father, Bhim Singh, on Saturday (November 7, 2026) called upon the youth of Punjab to pledge against drug abuse.

"We will take the body to our residence first and thereafter, between 12 and 1 pm, Jhota will be cremated on Diwali Day," said Singh while speaking to reporters in Chandigarh on Saturday (November 7, 2026).

Jhota's body was brought to PGIMER Chandigarh from the mortuary of Civil Hospital in Mansa in the early hours of Friday, after his family ended their 22-day agitation and agreed to a post-mortem following a meeting with Punjab government representatives.

On Friday (November 6, 2026), Jhota's father said he would go on a fast demanding the immediate transfer of Mansa Senior Superintendent of Police Vaibhav Chaudhary.

articles.title: Congress donations fall nearly 75%, sharpest decline in a decade
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Congress had received ₹517.39 crore in such contributions in 2024-25, according to its 2024-25 contribution report submitted to the Election Commission of India

The Congress party's receipts from donations above ₹20,000 plunged nearly 75% to ₹130.69 crore in 2025-26, the steepest annual fall in such contributions in a decade, an analysis of the party's filings with the Election Commission shows.
The party had received ₹517.39 crore in such contributions in 2024-25, according to its 2024-25 contribution report submitted to the commission.
A comparison with the preceding 12 financial years shows that the last steeper fall was in 2015-16, when Congress' disclosed donations dropped roughly 86% from ₹141.46 crore the previous year.

The latest decline follows two years of higher collections. Congress received ₹281.48 crore in disclosed donations in 2023-24, rising to ₹517.39 crore in 2024-25, the year Lok Sabha elections were held.

BJP received ₹6,074.02 crore in donations exceeding ₹20,000 in 2024-25, nearly 12 times Congress's collection. BJP's corresponding figure for 2025-26 is not available as the party's contribution report has not been made public by the ECI yet.
The BJP collected more than the Congress in each of the 12 financial years examined.

Funding through Prudent Electoral Trust accounted for a substantial part of Congress' latest decline. The trust's contribution fell from ₹216.34 crore in 2024-25 to ₹25 crore in 2025-26, a drop of about 88%.
Prudent was the only electoral trust listed in the party's latest contribution report.
Among other large contributors were Star Cement, which gave ₹5 crore, Sajjan Bhajanka, who contributed ₹4 crore, and Prem Kumar Bhajanka, who donated ₹2 crore.
The Congress' 2025-26 fund collection, though sharply lower than the previous year, was not its lowest over the period examined.

articles.title: Lawrence Bishnoi gang member Hari Boxer detained in U.S., extradition process underway
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Rajasthan Anti-Gangster Task Force (AGTF) secured the detention through sustained coordination with international agencies, including the CBI and Interpol, police said

Lawrence Bishnoi gang member Harichand Jat alias Hari Boxer has been detained in the U.S. by the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), and efforts are underway to bring him to India, Rajasthan Police said on Sunday (November 8, 2026).
The Rajasthan Anti-Gangster Task Force (AGTF) secured the detention through sustained coordination with international agencies, including the CBI and Interpol, police said.

Hari Boxer (40), a resident of Chatarpura village in Kotputli-Behror district of Rajasthan, was allegedly operating criminal activities in India from abroad and played a key role in supplying weapons to the Lawrence Bishnoi-Rohit Godara gang.
He was involved in extortion threats and firing incidents in Rajasthan, Haryana, Punjab, Delhi, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra, including Mumbai and Pune, AGTF ADG Dinesh MN said.
The accused allegedly threatened wealthy businessmen through WhatsApp and Signal-based VoIP calls and resorted to firing at individuals or their family members if extortion demands were not met.

He was also wanted in connection with several firing incidents, including the shooting outside Bollywood director Rohit Shetty's Mumbai residence, following which he allegedly claimed responsibility through a social media post.
More than 22 cases, including attempts to murder, extortion, Arms Act violations and organised crime, are registered against him in various police stations in Rajasthan.

Hari Boxer allegedly fled India in April 2023 using his own passport and travelled through Dubai, the Dominican Republic and Guyana before reaching the U.S. through Mexico via an illegal migration route, police said.
A Red Corner Notice was issued against him through Interpol on November 14, 2024, following coordination with the CBI.

AGTF subsequently shared intelligence and technical inputs with international agencies, including nine Interpol notices to the US between December 2024 and July 2026. A provisional arrest request, updated dossier and fingerprints were also forwarded, police said.

articles.title: Nithya Raman | The urban planner
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Before entering U.S. politics, L.A.’s first South Asian Mayor-elect worked among the urban poor in Chennai, where she used data to expose gaps in slum resettlement and public facilities

After defeating Karen Bass, the incumbent Mayor of the second most populous city of the U.S., Nithya Raman wrote on X, “Los Angeles, I am deeply honored to be your next mayor.” A member of the city council since 2020, Ms. Raman has a track record of civic activism, advocating for affordable and increased housing. Entering the electoral race at the very last minute, she is now L.A.’s the first South Asian Mayor-elect as well as the first candidate to defeat an incumbent Mayor of the city since 2005.

Born in Keralam, Ms. Raman spent a part of her early childhood between Thiruvananthapuram and Thrissur. Her father, Venkataraman, used to work for Keltron, and her mother, Sudha, was a former employee of the Indian Overseas Bank. The family migrated to the U.S. when Ms. Raman was six. She graduated from Harvard University in 2003, and then got a master’s degree in urban planning from MIT. She became a U.S. citizen at 22.

articles.title: Jon Ossoff | Ambition without ambition
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: While headlines scream Ossoff looks more presidential after his Senate win, he remains focused on his State while attacking Donald Trump and his family

There is something of an investigative journalist in Jon Ossoff, who served as managing director and chief executive officer of Insight: The World Investigates, a London-based investigative television production company. During his Senate campaign as Democratic candidate in Georgia and even before, he had been mounting a blistering campaign against corruption. It resonated with the voters struggling with rising food prices and unaffordable fuel.

Mr. Ossoff won the November 3 election against Republican Mike Collins, becoming the only incumbent Senate Democrat to defend a seat in a State President Donald Trump carried in 2024. Ever since his win in the 2021 Senate race in Georgia, the charismatic Mr. Ossoff has been making the lists of possible candidates for the Democratic ticket in the 2028 Presidential election. But, like Barack Obama before his 2004 Senate win and scores of others before him, Mr. Ossoff, now 39, who in 2021 became the youngest U.S. Senator since 1980, has been vehemently denying any such aspiration. The media, however, has been quick in spotting in him similarities with Mr. Obama, especially the former President’s speech delivery.

articles.title: New Zealanders won’t know for weeks who won election as neither side secures clear victory
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The tightest vote in years delivered a stinging rebuke to the major parties which have long dominated New Zealand politics, Christopher Luxon’s centre-right National party and centre-left Labour led by Chris Hipkins

New Zealanders will wait for weeks to discover who will lead the country after Saturday's (November 7, 2026) election failed to deliver a decisive win for the right or the left, leaving fraught negotiations for a wafer-thin governing majority the only apparent path to victory for either side.

The tightest vote in years delivered a stinging rebuke to the major parties which have long dominated New Zealand politics, Christopher Luxon's centre-right National party and centre-left Labour led by Chris Hipkins, as voters threw more support behind minor parties on the ideological flanks than before.
On Saturday's (November 7) numbers, minor parties would enter negotiations for a governing deal with leverage to extract deeper policy concessions from a weakened National or Labour.

The near-deadlock was partly produced because voters, apparently weary of New Zealand's economic woes and apathetic about both Luxon and Hipkins, chose to propel a new entrant group to Parliament for the first time in years.
Opportunity, led by 38-year-old business consultant and political newcomer Qiulae Wong, is unaligned with either bloc and Ms. Wong has said she could work with either side to form a government.

Ms. Wong's pledges of evidence-based centrism and an end to partisan bickering had on Saturday's (November 7) results secured seven seats for Opportunity — enough to frustrate both left and right in a simple path to power.
It was a staggering ascension for a party that made three failed attempts at Parliament before Ms. Wong became leader less than a year ago.

Other winners were harder to identify and on Sunday (November 8), “who won the election 2026” was the top trending Google search in New Zealand. So unclear was the result that parties won't begin negotiations to form a government until final tallies are released on November 27, confirming the exact number of seats they've won.

With 2.8 million ballots counted on election night, the conservative incumbent government led by Luxon's National party appeared close to the slimmest possible return to power — by just one seat. However, Mr. Luxon didn't claim victory, instead striking a note of cautious optimism that he could negotiate a second term in power.

Speaking to reporters Sunday (November 8), Luxon blamed public dissatisfaction on global shocks which have buffeted New Zealand's trade-based economy, noting that other incumbent governments worldwide have faced voters' rancor over living costs.
