articles.title: Europe will be represented at U.S.-mediated Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi: France
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Although Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has made it clear that he wants involvement from European allies in the process, Russia has suggested there would be no place for European representatives at the table
Europe will be represented at the upcoming U.S.-mediated talks with Moscow and Kyiv in Abu Dhabi aimed at ending the Ukraine war, France said on Sunday (November 8, 2026).
"The Europeans will be represented and France will be in Abu Dhabi to participate in these talks," French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot told RTL radio .
His comment came after President Donald Trump stoked fears of a U.S. pivot toward the Kremlin by predicting a "very big" deal with Russia involving not only the Ukraine war but "all of Europe".

Up to now, the talks scheduled for Tuesday (November 10, 2026) and Wednesday (November 11, 2026) had been framed as a trilateral format at the level of officials, not leaders, from Ukraine, Russia and the United States.
The identities of who would take part have not been made public.

Although Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has made it clear that he wants involvement from European allies in the process, Russia has suggested there would be no place for European representatives at the table.
Mr. Barrot said that, in the past, "there have been discussions, sometimes without the Europeans and sometimes with," but "this time they will participate".
He said, "France will be there and will ensure that Europe's voice is heard."
On Thursday (November 5, 2026), U.S., European, Ukrainian and NATO officials met in Brussels ahead of the Abu Dhabi talks.
A NATO spokeswoman said they "sought to advance a just and sustainable end to the war in Ukraine".

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Europe will be represented at the upcoming U.S.-mediated talks with Moscow and Kyiv in Abu Dhabi aimed at ending the Ukraine war, France said on Sunday (November 8, 2026).

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: A NATO spokeswoman said they "sought to advance a just and sustainable end to the war in Ukraine".

articles.title: Agasthyamalai conservation case: SC directs temporary and non-resident silk cotton cultivators not eligible for protection under FRA Act
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Supreme Court directed on Friday that individuals with temporary residence in the Agasthyamalai biosphere or those living entirely outside the forest boundaries cannot be classified as traditional forest dwellers merely for cultivating silk cotton within the forest.

“Persons falling in Category II and Category III, as classified in the additional affidavit of September 6 filed by Department of Revenue, State of Tamil Nadu, shall be excluded from consideration as forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers for the purposes of the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 or FRA Act,” a Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta directed.

According to Tamil Nadu’s own affidavit, 232 persons are cultivating the forest area with temporary residence while 2,767 persons who occupy 2,867.70 hectares land are residing outside the forest boundary and are managing silk cotton cultivation.

The order was passed in furtherance of a May 2026 judgment, which had issued various directions for a structured and time-bound process of eviction, rehabilitation and ecological restoration in the forest areas. The court had ordered the preparation of a division-wise eviction plan, removal of encroachments, and action against identified government servants.

It had imposed a prohibition on approval or commencement of new non-forestry activities or diversion proposals within the Agasthyamalai landscape, and directed continued monitoring of the area by the Central Empowered Committee (CEC).

Justice Mehta, who authored the order, held the State government “primarily responsible” for delaying the receipt of claims under the 2006 Act. Noting that so far only around 40 gram sabhas had become functional to commence the process of inviting claims, the government gave a last opportunity of 30 days to the State government to complete the formation of the remaining gram sabhas. The process of adjudication of the claims would be concluded within a period of five months from the date of constitution of the gram sabhas.

The court further constituted a ‘special committee’ chaired by former Chief Justice of India B.R. Gavai to supervise the expeditious disposal of claims and scrutinise the orders passed by the competent authorities under the 2006 Act.

The Supreme Court directed the CEC to furnish an opinion regarding the government’s view that silk cotton was a ‘minor forest produce’. This is significant for the biosphere. Presently, 3,637.83.2 hectares of the 5,072.64.3 hectares of forest land is under silk cotton cultivation.

Giving a prima facie view against the State’s claim of historical cultivation of silk cotton, the court said “what emerges from the government affidavits is the promotion and sponsored cultivation of silk cotton as a commercial crop”.

“The concept of planned cultivation of commercial crops is totally contrary to the very concept of a naturally occurring minor forest produce. If commercial crops are permitted to be cultivated in the forest areas, the very nature of the forest is bound to change… The fact that large swathes of forest are being destroyed under the garb of cultivation of silk cotton,” the court observed.

articles.title: Did all the murders happen in the small house on the terrace?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Seven murders in Bengaluru have raised law and order concerns. Here’s a look at accused Indushekhar’s whereabouts and criminal history

Indushekhar lived with his wife Sunita and daughter in a small house, barely 500 sq. ft, on the terrace of a two-storey building, nestled among several commercial establishments, 50 metres from the famous Bhashyam Circle, Rajajinagar.

The building has commercial establishments on the ground floor, including a watch repair shop, a tea stall and a small condiments shop. The entire first floor was occupied by a small political party. Indushekar’s house is on the second floor, which also serves as the terrace.
Household appliances were crammed into the space, with several other household items scattered around. A board on the wall read, “Police Voice”.

Reaching the second floor itself through a very narrow staircase itself is a task. This has raised questions as to whether all seven murders were committed here in the house. However, the accused claimed that the murders took place inside his house. The location has raised several questions, as the building has very little space to move around.
However, the police investigation indicates a high probability that the murders took place there. “He may have cleaned the entire scene, but residues were found at the crime scene,” the officer said.

How did he transport the bodies down to the road into his car is a question that has left the police puzzled. He couldn’t have done it alone and that is where police suspect the role of the minor daughter. Given the lane mostly has commercial establishments, the police suspect that he could have shifted the bodies only during night time.

articles.title: Bamboo shelters, cool roofs to climate-proof Telangana cities
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The State is drawing up a ₹20,000-crore project pipeline and a series of policy measures to prepare its cities for rising temperatures and erratic rainfall. Speaking to media persons in Kanakapura, he wondered why the BJP leaders were tying to take publicity for this event though they had nothing to do with it.
“We are developing metro network by borrowing money. I will present some of these issues before the Prime Minister on November 13,” he said.

The Governor instructed all Vice-Chancellors to prepare and submit a detailed report on the same. “This report should cover the current status of their respective universities, key achievements, challenges, shortcomings, and specific measures proposed for improvement,” she stated.

Addressing the Vice-Chancellors of various universities and officials from the Karnataka State Higher Education Council at Lok Bhavan, the Governor emphasised the need to strengthen the quality, transparency, accountability and overall performance of universities across the State.

“Emphasis must be placed on the effective implementation of the National Education Policy and the State Education Policy, strong coordination between industries and universities, as well as skill development, research, innovation and employability,” she said.
The Governor called upon all Vice-Chancellors and the Karnataka State Higher Education Council to work in coordination and collaboration to strengthen the higher education system in Karnataka.

articles.title: Periyar Arivulagam books row: political leaders raise concern over allegations, call for action
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Kamal Haasan demands the immediate withdrawal of the fake books from all libraries. M.H. Jawahirullah wants the formation of an independent committee to examine all books procured for the public library. Others, including Anbumani Ramadoss and K. Annamalai, want the government to take up a thorough investigation of the allegations

After writer Perumal Murugan wrote about alleged irregularities in the procurement of books for Periyar Arivulagam, a newly inaugurated public library in Coimbatore, Makkal Needhi Maiam (MNM) founder and Rajya Sabha Member Kamal Haasan said on Friday that “there can be no greater disgrace to the Tamil language than this”.

He pointed out that books containing fabricated information could cause immense damage in the long run. In a statement, he said the reputation of Tamil language would be irreparably damaged if people read, took notes, and incorporated the contents of (fabricated books) into speeches, written works, and research.

“Whoever is responsible for this has betrayed the Tamil language. I urge the Government of Tamil Nadu to immediately withdraw these fake books from all libraries and have them dumped on the streets and burnt. The publishing houses responsible for this must be sealed. We owe a debt of gratitude to writer Mr. Murugan for exposing this fraud,” Mr. Haasan said.
Manithaneya Makkal Katchi president and MLA M.H. Jawahirullah said allegations raised by Mr. Murugan had caused considerable shock and concern.
Manithaneya Makkal Katchi president M.H. Jawahirullah. | Photo Credit: B. VELANKANNI RAJ

He said: “It has come to light that 1,800 books published under the name of a publishing house called Akalvilakku Publications have been procured and placed on the library’s fourth floor. This publishing house, which is unfamiliar to serious readers, has raised suspicions that it may have been established specifically to supply books to the library. Furthermore, Mr. Murugan has alleged that books were produced with the assistance of artificial intelligence, without the proper application of technical expertise; that the authors’ names are either pseudonyms or fictitious; that the International Standard Book Numbers (ISBNs) mentioned in the books cannot be found when checked online; and that the publisher’s address also appears to be unreliable,” he said.

Mr. Jawahirullah said, “An independent committee must be constituted to examine all books procured for the Periyar Arivulagam to date, including their publishers, authors, ISBNs, and pricing details, and a thorough inquiry must be conducted into the registration, addresses, owners, and activities of the suspicious publishing houses, including Agal Vilakku Publications.”

Tamil Nadu Congress Committee (TNCC) president and Virudhunagar MP B. Manickam Tagore alleged: “Everyone knows that the DMK government was replete with enormous corruption. No scheme was devoid of corruption. If there has been this level of corruption in the procurement of books, it is scary to think how much corruption would have been there in the construction of the building. The Tamil Nadu government should order an investigation.”
TNCC president B. Manickam Tagore. | Photo Credit: B. JOTHI RAMALINGAM
He added that all the books kept in Periyar Arivulagam should be audited and fabricated books should be removed.

articles.title: Trump replaces Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller as chief of staff after GOP’s midterm defeat
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: On his social media site, Donald Trump praised Susie Wiles and said she’d continue working for his political organisation

President Donald Trump said Friday (November 6, 2026) that Stephen Miller was replacing Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff, mere days after Republicans lost control of Congress in the midterm elections.
On his social media site, Mr. Trump praised Ms. Wiles and said she’d continue working for his political organisation. Ms. Wiles also released a social media statement on Friday (November 6, 2026).

"Serving President Trump in the White House has been the honour of a lifetime. I’m so proud to have been a part of what we’ve accomplished together, from securing our border and cutting taxes to strengthening our economy and putting America First,” Wiles said in a social media post shortly after Trump’s announcement. She added that her commitment to “the President and the mission” will not change.
Mr. Miller, long a key member of Mr. Trump’s inner circle, is a key architect of the administration’s hard-line immigration policies.
Ms. Wiles, the steely political operator and longtime adviser to Mr. Trump, was the first woman to ever serve in that post.
Ms. Wiles' departure comes almost immediately after the GOP's midterm thrashing on Tuesday (November 3, 2026). She will be replaced by Stephen Miller, a longtime trusted aide to Mr. Trump.

The departure also came months after Ms. Wiles indicated she no longer showed evidence of breast cancer after she underwent months of treatment for the disease, a diagnosis she went public with in March 2026.
Ms. Wiles is the longest-serving White House chief of staff for Mr. Trump, who cycled through four of them during his first four-year term.

Mr. Miller is one of Mr. Trump’s closest and longest-serving advisers, having jumped on board during his long-shot 2016 presidential campaign as a speechwriter. He currently serves as White House deputy chief of staff, and though he has a wide-ranging portfolio, Mr. Miller is most closely aligned with Mr. Trump’s immigration policy and rhetoric on immigration.
Mr. Miller is a former aide to hardliner former Sen. Jeff Sessions, R-Ala., who would go on to serve as Mr. Trump’s first Attorney General.

articles.title: West Bengal election is not legally valid: Former CEC S.Y. Quraishi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The former top poll official also reinstated that the Election Commission of India is supposed to make decisions based on a majority

Former Chief Election Commissioner S.Y. Quraishi alleged that the West Bengal elections were not legally valid. He reinstated that the decisions at the Election Commission of India should be based on a majority.

“Were the West Bengal elections legally valid? In my opinion, it was not. I have said this several times; I will say it again. Now it is in front of the Supreme Court; I am hoping they will take the right decision,” Mr. Quraishi said. He further added that some parts of it may have been valid but also said that in places where there was suspicious of majority Muslim voters being removed must be rechecked and go for re-polls if needed.

“This government has been in power for 6-7 months. People are happy. But some people are raising questions, maybe because they did not get the outcome that they desired,” Minister Dilip Ghosh said on Friday (November 6, 2026), reacting to Mr. Quraishi’s allegations. He also warned that accepting the people’s verdict and choice of government is the right decision; otherwise the people opposing it have a “tough” road ahead.

This comes after the former CEC raised allegations against the SIR process and discrepancies at the West Bengal elections while delivering the keynote address at the Hashim Abdul Halim Memorial Lecture on Thursday (November 5, 2026) in Kolkata.

“The CEC is not the Election Commission. The rules first call for unanimous decisions. If that is not possible, there must be a majority-based decision among the three members of the ECI,” Mr. Quraishi said. He added that the CEC is not the ECI on their own, and their decision alone cannot be final.

The former CEC said this in reference to The Indian Express report, which had claimed that election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised at least 14 objections to the various decisions allegedly taken unilaterally by CEC Gyanesh Kumar.

Meanwhile, Mr. Quraishi also said that the voter is not supposed to beg for their voting rights; rather, tradition in the past ensured that voter cards were delivered to the homes of each voter, and they did not have to negotiate to be included in the voter lists. He accused the special intensive revision (SIR) was used as a process to do backdoor checks for citizenships.

“It was neither smooth nor transparent. So many questions were raised that are currently being heard in the Supreme Court. Now, things will come out clearly once their judgment arrives, regarding what went wrong and what was correct,” Mr. Quraishi added.

articles.title: Pakistan says willing to issue visa to Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann for visit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: On October 23, Bhagwant Mann had said that he had been invited to attend the World Punjabi Conference in Lahore on November 27 questioning whether he would be allowed to travel to Pakistan
Pakistan on Friday (November 6, 2026) said it would consider issuing a visa to Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann if the Indian politician wished to visit the country.
Pakistan Foreign Office Spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan made the remarks during his weekly media briefing in response to a question about the possible visit of the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) leader.

The Pakistani government would “consider issuing him a visa if he wished to visit the country”, Mr. Khan said, clarifying that whether the Indian government permits Mr. Mann to travel to Pakistan was an entirely separate matter.
On October 23, Mr. Mann had said that he had been invited to attend the World Punjabi Conference in Lahore on November 27.
However, he questioned whether he would be allowed to travel to Pakistan. “Our culture is the same. Many poets from here will go there,” he had said.
Mr. Mann had also expressed his desire that all legislators of the Punjab Legislative Assembly visit Kartarpur Sahib in Pakistan if the Kartarpur Corridor reopened.

The corridor, which connects Dera Baba Nanak in India's Punjab with the historic Gurdwara Darbar Sahib in Kartarpur, Pakistan, was established to facilitate Sikh pilgrims travelling to the shrine associated with Guru Nanak Dev, the founder of Sikhism.
It allows Indian pilgrims to visit the gurdwara without requiring a visa for Pakistan, subject to the applicable arrangements.

The corridor has remained closed to pilgrim movement from the Indian side since May 7, 2025, when India launched pre-dawn missile strikes on nine terror targets in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir following the Pahalgam terror attack.
Pakistan said it remained ready to facilitate pilgrims once the restrictions were lifted.

articles.title: A missing persons complaint that unravelled Bengaluru’s seven murders
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Senior police officers said that Sunita, the accused’s wife, and Roopavathi, his mother-in-law, were the first to be murdered.

It was not until the mother of Nalini, one of the seven allegedly killed by cab driver-turned-YouTuber Indushekhar , lodged a missing person complaint that the police found the first clue to the murders. While the murders allegedly took place between October 16 and October 31, the last two bodies were disposed of on November 1 or 2.

Senior police officers said that Sunita, the accused’s wife, and Roopavathi, his mother-in-law, were the first to be murdered. Sunita and Indushekhar had been married for 20 years, and an officer said they had been having regular arguments throughout their marriage. Sunita worked as a typist for an advocate, while Indushekhar was a cab driver. Their respective jobs were often a point of contention between them.
“Indushekhar claimed that he was verbally abused and harassed by his wife and her family, while her brothers also encouraged her to fight with him,” a senior officer said.
Prima facie , the police have found that Indushekhar had been planning the murders for over a year. The growing friction and pent-up anger allegedly came to a head following a recent meeting.

“The accused claimed that Roopavathi had visited his house on October 14, when she and Sunita reportedly verbally abused him. This became a trigger point, and he wanted to eliminate them,” the officer said.

According to the police, Sunita and Roopavathi were murdered first. Subsequently, the accused invited Sunita’s younger brother Shivakumar and his wife Divya to his house on the pretext of hosting a dinner party. The couple were then killed along with their seven-year-old son Puneeth. On October 30, the accused allegedly invited Shankar, another brother of Sunita, and his wife Nalini, and allegedly murdered them.

On November 3, Tungamma, Nalini’s mother, approached the police, stating that her daughter’s phone was switched off and that their house in Srirampura was also locked. Tungamma subsequently went to Indushekar’s house to check on him but found that his house was locked as well.

Sensing that something was amiss, she contacted Divya’s mother Kalavathi, who also said that her daughter and son-in-law were missing. Tungamma then lodged a missing person complaint with the Srirampura police.

Karthik, a shopkeeper near Indushekhar’s house, said a police team visited the house on November 3 and made inquiries about Indushekhar among the neighbourhood residents. “They also came the next day and questioned people because Indushekhar’s house was locked,” he said.

A senior officer told The Hindu that the police grew suspicious and began tracking Indushekhar. Several technical inputs indicated that he was on the move. “Finally, when he was in the city, we tracked him and intercepted his car,” he said.

articles.title: Amid price rise, Centre mandates rice, paddy stock declaration
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: To prevent hoarding, Union government allows five southern States to impose stock limits

With rice prices rising due to a deficient and uneven monsoon, the Centre on Friday (November 7, 2026) directed traders, retailers, wholesalers, processors and millers across the country to declare their rice and paddy stocks and allowed five southern States to impose stock limits to prevent hoarding.

Under a November 6 order, all traders and wholesalers, retailers, large retail chains and processors and millers in all States and Union Territories must declare stocks under six categories — Basmati rice, non-Basmati premium rice, non-Basmati rice, parboiled rice, broken rice and paddy.
Every unit holding stocks will have to update details on the Food Stock Portal (foodstock.dfpd.gov.in) every Friday, the Food Ministry said in a statement.
Units that are not registered on the portal or that violate stock limits will face action under Sections 6 and 7 of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955.

In a separate letter, also dated November 6, the Centre has given its consent to Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Telangana to impose stock limits on paddy and rice through control orders.

The limits will remain in force till January 31, 2027. The Centre and States will monitor implementation to ensure adequate availability and prevent hoarding and black marketing, an official statement said.

To improve availability, the Centre is allocating additional rice stocks to NAFED, NCCF and Kendriya Bhandar for sale as Bharat Rice, and has asked them to explore all possible distribution channels, especially in the southern States.

The Centre has also doubled the target for rice sales through e-auction under the Open Market Sale Scheme (Domestic) for 2026-27 from 25 lakh tonnes to 50 lakh tonnes. Around 25 lakh tonnes had been sold to private parties by October 31, compared to 11 lakh tonnes in the same period of the last year.
Trade and industry experts said deficient and uneven rainfall had contributed to rice inflation, particularly in premium non-Basmati varieties, and pushed up paddy prices in several markets.
Retail rice inflation rose to 8.25% year-on-year in September from 5.89% in August, with the average retail price at around ₹48.23 per kg, about 12% higher than a year earlier.

📈 Economic, Banking & Finance 📅 07 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 3 Min Read

📰 Amid price rise, Centre mandates rice, paddy stock declaration

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

To prevent hoarding, Union government allows five southern States to impose stock limits

With rice prices rising due to a deficient and uneven monsoon, the Centre on Friday (November 7, 2026) directed traders, retailers, wholesalers, processors and millers across the country to declare their rice and paddy stocks and allowed five southern States to impose stock limits to prevent hoarding.

Under a November 6 order, all traders and wholesalers, retailers, large retail chains and processors and millers in all States and Union Territories must declare stocks under six categories — Basmati rice, non-Basmati premium rice, non-Basmati rice, parboiled rice, broken rice and paddy.

Every unit holding stocks will have to update details on the Food Stock Portal (foodstock.dfpd.gov.in) every Friday, the Food Ministry said in a statement.

Units that are not registered on the portal or that violate stock limits will face action under Sections 6 and 7 of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955.

In a separate letter, also dated November 6, the Centre has given its consent to Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Telangana to impose stock limits on paddy and rice through control orders.

The limits will remain in force till January 31, 2027. The Centre and States will monitor implementation to ensure adequate availability and prevent hoarding and black marketing, an official statement said.

To improve availability, the Centre is allocating additional rice stocks to NAFED, NCCF and Kendriya Bhandar for sale as Bharat Rice, and has asked them to explore all possible distribution channels, especially in the southern States.

The Centre has also doubled the target for rice sales through e-auction under the Open Market Sale Scheme (Domestic) for 2026-27 from 25 lakh tonnes to 50 lakh tonnes. Around 25 lakh tonnes had been sold to private parties by October 31, compared to 11 lakh tonnes in the same period of the last year.

Trade and industry experts said deficient and uneven rainfall had contributed to rice inflation, particularly in premium non-Basmati varieties, and pushed up paddy prices in several markets.

Retail rice inflation rose to 8.25% year-on-year in September from 5.89% in August, with the average retail price at around ₹48.23 per kg, about 12% higher than a year earlier.

articles.title: CPI(M) leader Biman Basu retracts after holding Jyoti Basu responsible for LF government’s industrial policy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on November 5 blamed the policy of forcible land acquisition during the regime of former Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee for decline in industrial prospects of the State.

Senior Communist Party of India (Marxist) (CPI[M]) leader Biman Basu on Friday (November 6, 2026) retracted his remarks, holding the veteran party leader and former West Bengal Chief Minister Jyoti Basu responsible for any issues with the industrial policy of the State during the regime of Left Front.

“The Left Front government’s industrial policy was adopted and announced under the leadership of Comrade Jyoti Basu. If there were any problems with that industrial policy, it was Jyoti Basu’s fault. Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee was given the responsibility to implement that industrial policy,”

Mr. Sau said on Thursday (November 6, 2026). The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government in West Bengal on Thursday (November 5, 2026) came up with an investment promotion policy offering incentives to new industries that will be set up in the State.

Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Thursday (November 5, 2026) blamed the policy of forcible land acquisition during the regime of former Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee for the decline in industrial prospects of the State. The remark by the senior CPI(M) leader on Thursday sparked speculation on whether Mr. Basu came to the defence of Mr. Bhattacharjee by putting the blame on Jyoti Basu, the longest serving Chief Minister of the State from 1977 to 2000.

On Friday (November 6, 2026), Mr. Basu clarified that he did not talk about any divisions between the regime of the two Chief Ministers of the Left Front government. “The industrial policy was announced in the eighties by the then Chief Minister, Comrade Jyoti Basu. Accordingly, industries have developed. Thermal power plants have been built,” he said.

The CPI(M) leader said that the fact that no industries came to the State during the past 15 years of the Trinamool Congress regime should not be blamed on the Left.”I did not make any differentiation. I said, the industrial policy was not announced by Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee. His predecessor Jyoti Basu announced it,” Mr. Basu added.

Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee, who was the Chief Minister of West Bengal from 2000 to 2011, is considered to have made an earnest attempt to revive the industrial prospects of the State, but fell into the trap of forcible land acquisition, which brought the Trinamool Congress to power in 2011. The political opponents of the CPI(M), including Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, blame militant trade unionism in the State for the flight of capital from the State.
West Bengal / Kolkata / Communist Party of India -Marxist

articles.title: Disallowed Friday prayers, under house detention for 6th day: Mirwaiz
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: On the previous Friday, the Mirwaiz mentioned in his sermon the findings of the International Crisis Group report on Jammu and Kashmir and highlighted the concerns over political prisoners, civil liberties and the need for meaningful political engagement and reconciliation

Kashmir chief cleric Mirwaiz Umar Farooq on Friday (November 6, 2026) said the authorities disallowed him from leading the congregation prayers at Jama Masjid, apparently in response to the sermon delivered on the previous Friday on the Kashmir issue.

“My house detention continues unabated for the past week, with police deployment and barricades in place. Unfortunately, I will not be able to deliver the Friday sermon at Jama Masjid Srinagar to the faithful today,” said the Mirwaiz in a post on X. He also shared videos of the barricading by security forces outside his residence in Srinagar’s Nigeen area.

Terming the move of the authorities as “arbitrary and authoritarian measures”, the Mirwaiz said, “It was aimed to curtail freedom of movement and speech, and also betray the official narrative of ‘normalcy’ in Kashmir”.

On the previous Friday, the Mirwaiz mentioned in his sermon the findings of the International Crisis Group report on Jammu and Kashmir and highlighted the concerns over political prisoners, civil liberties and the need for meaningful political engagement and reconciliation.

“Since then, the Mirwaiz has remained confined to his residence, preventing him from fulfilling his religious responsibilities, including addressing scheduled religious gatherings and leading the Friday congregation at Jama Masjid,” said a spokesman for the Mirwaiz, in a statement.

articles.title: Wave of resignations from U.S. Justice Department after midterms
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The Justice Department under Donald Trump has pursued cases against a number of perceived enemies, and several prosecutors have lost their jobs over their reluctance or inability to bring charges
Several senior U.S. Justice Department officials have resigned, including its civil rights chief and a prosecutor investigating allegations of conspiracy against President Donald Trump.

U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche, a former personal lawyer for Mr. Trump, announced on Thursday (November 5, 2026) that he had accepted the resignation of Assistant Attorney General for Civil Rights Harmeet Dhillon.

In this role, Mr. Dhillon was directly involved in unsuccessful attempts to obtain voter registration lists from some 30 states ahead of this week’s midterm elections that dealt heavy defeats to Mr. Trump’s Republican Party.
In her resignation letter, cited by U.S. media outlets, Mr. Dillon said that she submitted it in October and agreed to remain in her position until the election.

Ms. Blanche also announced on Friday (November 6, 2026) the resignations of Assistant Attorney General for National Security John Eisenberg, and Jason Reding Quinones, U.S. attorney for the Southern District of Florida.
Mr. Quinones oversaw an investigation into former intelligence officials whom Mr. Trump accused of seeking to remove him from power.
The Justice Department under Mr. Trump has pursued cases against a number of perceived enemies, and several prosecutors have lost their jobs over their reluctance or inability to bring charges.
In one high-profile case brought by the department, James Comey, the former director of the FBI, was indicted in April for allegedly threatening Mr. Trump’s life in an Instagram post of seashells.

articles.title: India, EU conclude multi-billion Euro global innovation programme
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: India’s association with the Horizon programme is seen as part of the comprehensive strategic agenda of the two sides for the next five years

India and the European Union have concluded negotiations on New Delhi’s association with a Euro 93.5 billion flagship research and innovation programme, paving the way for expanded collaboration under their broader strategic partnership.
The decision comes weeks before India and the 27-nation bloc are set to seal a landmark free trade agreement — billed as the “mother of all deals” — to create a market of two billion people.
The European Commission and India have successfully concluded negotiations on New Delhi’s association with the Horizon Europe programme, the EU said.
This marks an important step forward for EU-India relations, strengthening scientific cooperation, creating new opportunities in research, and deepening the strategic partnership, it said.
India’s association with the Horizon programme is seen as part of the comprehensive strategic agenda of the two sides for the next five years.

For researchers, businesses and research organisations across Europe, India’s association will open up more opportunities to collaborate with Indian partners and build lasting scientific and technological links, the EU said.

Once the agreement is signed and the necessary procedures are completed on both sides, researchers and organisations in India will be able to receive funding directly from Horizon Europe and lead collaborative projects under its Pillar II: ‘Global Challenges and European Industrial Competitiveness’, it said.

This is the largest part of the programme which funds collaborative, multi-national research and innovation projects tackling societal and technological issues, such as health, digital, industry, space, climate, energy, and bioeconomy.
The EU said the move will create new opportunities for European and Indian partners to pool expertise, develop technologies and address shared challenges.
Association is the closest form of cooperation offered by the EU to non-EU countries under Horizon Europe.

India’s association with the Horizon programme is seen as part of the comprehensive strategic agenda of the two sides for the next five years

India and the European Union have concluded negotiations on New Delhi’s association with a Euro 93.5 billion flagship research and innovation programme, paving the way for expanded collaboration under their broader strategic partnership.

The decision comes weeks before India and the 27-nation bloc are set to seal a landmark free trade agreement — billed as the “mother of all deals” — to create a market of two billion people.

The European Commission and India have successfully concluded negotiations on New Delhi’s association with the Horizon Europe programme, the EU said.

This marks an important step forward for EU-India relations, strengthening scientific cooperation, creating new opportunities in research, and deepening the strategic partnership, it said.

India’s association with the Horizon programme is seen as part of the comprehensive strategic agenda of the two sides for the next five years.

For researchers, businesses and research organisations across Europe, India’s association will open up more opportunities to collaborate with Indian partners and build lasting scientific and technological links, the EU said.

Once the agreement is signed and the necessary procedures are completed on both sides, researchers and organisations in India will be able to receive funding directly from Horizon Europe and lead collaborative projects under its Pillar II: ‘Global Challenges and European Industrial Competitiveness’, it said.

This is the largest part of the programme which funds collaborative, multi-national research and innovation projects tackling societal and technological issues, such as health, digital, industry, space, climate, energy, and bioeconomy.

The EU said the move will create new opportunities for European and Indian partners to pool expertise, develop technologies and address shared challenges.

Association is the closest form of cooperation offered by the EU to non-EU countries under Horizon Europe.

articles.title: Govt. focuses on land for augmenting resources
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Deputy CM directs officials to prepare dashboard containing land details
The State Government appears to have decided to focus on lands for augmenting resources and meeting its financial commitments.

The Government has directed officials to make information such as land details, layout status, plots ready for auction and various other initiatives available on a single digital platform. The dashboard would facilitate better coordination among departments, enable faster decision-making and enhance transparency in the auction process.

Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka favoured development of a dedicated digital dashboard for effective monitoring of government lands, layout development and auction-related activities. He gave the directions during the Cabinet sub-committee meeting on resource mobilisation on Friday.

Officials of various revenue earning departments were directed to work in close coordination and formulate a comprehensive action plan to strengthen the State’s financial resources for achieving revenue targets within the stipulated timelines.

Clear targets, inter-departmental coordination and timely decisions were essential to enhance the State’s revenues. Senior officials should prepare weekly action plans and regularly review the progress to ensure the achievement of the prescribed targets.

The meeting reviewed the possibilities of mobilising revenue through utilisation and regularisation of lands in industrial layouts and old industrial estates. Officials briefed on the revenue already generated and the proposals at various stages of implementation.

Mr. Vikramarka wanted a focused action plan to be prepared to achieve the revenue targets through these initiatives. There was also a need to expedite unit-wise regularisation and approval processes in industrial areas such as Azamabad, Balanagar and Hafeezpet. Proposals relating to B-category and micro industrial units should be examined comprehensively.
Officials were asked to set weekly targets for processing applications within defined timelines and assign clear responsibilities to the concerned officials.

The meeting held detailed discussions on land pooling, availability of land for future requirements and mobilisation of land resources in the rapidly developing areas surrounding Hyderabad, particularly Medchal and Rangareddy districts.

He reviewed the possibilities of generating revenue through the development and auction of lands under the jurisdiction of HMDA and TGIIC. Officials were asked to identify suitable layouts for auction, prioritise locations with good connectivity to major roads and development potential, and initiate the auction process in a phased manner.

articles.title: Zubeen Garg case: Assam CM flags danger to family in threat to besiege his house
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: He told journalists in Guwahati that he would bring the threat to the notice of the Supreme Court and the Gauhati High Court, as it could amount to an attempt to murder
Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Friday (November 6, 2026) said the threat by a group led by an MLA to besiege his house over the Zubeen Garg death case posed a danger to his family.
He told journalists in Guwahati that he would bring the threat to the notice of the Supreme Court and the Gauhati High Court, as it could amount to an attempt to murder.

The Zubeen Garg Nyay Samiti, a group led by Sivasagar MLA Akhil Gogoi, said on Thursday (November 5, 2026) that they would surround the Chief Minister’s residence if Shyamkanu Mahanta and Siddharth Sharma, the two prime accused in the Garg death case, were granted bail.

Garg died while swimming in the sea off an island in Singapore on September 19, 2025. Seven people, including Mr Mahanta and Mr. Sharma, were arrested in connection with the death, which the Singapore authorities said was accidental.
However, the Chief Minister told the 126-member Assembly on November 25, 2025, that Garg’s death was “plain and simple murder”.
On Friday (November 7, 2026), he said what he stated in the Assembly was reflected in the charge sheet filed by the Assam Police’s Special Investigation Team (SIT) formed to probe Garg’s death.

Referring to the bail Gauhati High Court granted to singer Amritprava Mahanta, also an accused in the Garg death case, on October 9, he pointed out that 160 witnesses named her during the SIT investigation but not during the hearing.
“People should question the witnesses, not me. The court should be allowed to do its work,” the Chief Minister said, adding that the threat to besiege his residence was a “serious matter”.

“The call to protest near the Chief Minister’s residence and not his office is a threat to my family and could amount to a direct attempt to murder,” he said, adding that he has instructed the legal department to bring the matter to the notice of the courts.
“The threat, after creating an impression that two accused (Mr Mahanta and Mr Sharma) will be granted bail, is a conspiracy to create unrest in the State,” the Chief Minister said.

articles.title: Epic failures: on electoral roll, welfare
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: The electoral roll cannot be used to determine welfare beneficiaries

Union Panchayati Raj Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh’s statement that voter identity cards, with biometric authentication, will replace Aadhaar as the basis for identifying beneficiaries and making payments under his Ministry’s schemes runs contrary to existing laws and regulations. Essentially, the electoral roll, prepared in several States through the flawed Special Intensive Revision (SIR) by the Election Commission of India (ECI), will become the dataset to vet the identities of beneficiaries. This contradicts the Supreme Court’s May 27 judgment on the Bihar SIR and its observations while hearing petitions against West Bengal’s orders removing people deleted during the SIR from the Public Distribution System and the Annapurna Yojana. The Court held that the ECI may undertake only a “limited enquiry” into citizenship to decide who belongs on the electoral roll, and that “any action taken pursuant thereto is confined to electoral consequences alone”. The consequence of deletion from the rolls, it said, is “correspondingly limited” to a person’s place on the roll and their right to vote. The Court also called the EPIC “a derivative document, issued on the basis of inclusion in the electoral roll”, and held that relying on it to verify that very roll would defeat the exercise. It is ironic that Mr. Singh now wants this “derivative document” to be the determinant of welfare benefits.

Not every citizen is an eligible voter, and tying benefits to the electoral roll is illogical and also cruel. In West Bengal, lakhs were deleted from the rolls , many for dubious “logical discrepancies”. In the appeals heard for reinstatement, 93% resulted in the restoration of names by September 2026, pointing to massive pre-election disenfranchisement. The Court has stated that it is yet to adjudicate on the legality of the ECI’s “logical discrepancies” method. The SIR was designed by the ECI to restrict enrolment through stringent residency criteria; thus, itinerant voters had to prove their eligibility. The Opposition, civil society and even some of the BJP’s allies have objected to this, but the BJP refuses to acknowledge the SIR’s flaws. This is partly because it has benefited from disenfranchisement — as in West Bengal. But the Minister’s remarks suggest another reason. The BJP-led coalition sees the pruned electoral rolls as a way to limit welfare, especially at a time when growth in tax revenues has slowed because of the Centre’s policies. Inordinately delaying the Census, changing the procedure to appoint Election Commissioners, who then run an exercise that disenfranchises millions by design, and now, using the resultant rolls to decide who gets welfare, all cut at the heart of the painstakingly built constitutional welfare state. The sooner the Court decides the petitions against the SIR, and reiterates that its rolls cannot be used to curtail welfare, the better.

✍️ Editorial & Opinion 📅 07 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 4 Min Read

📰 Epic failures: on electoral roll, welfare

🎯 Exam Relevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

The electoral roll cannot be used to determine welfare beneficiaries

Union Panchayati Raj Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh’s statement that voter identity cards, with biometric authentication, will replace Aadhaar as the basis for identifying beneficiaries and making payments under his Ministry’s schemes runs contrary to existing laws and regulations. Essentially, the electoral roll, prepared in several States through the flawed Special Intensive Revision (SIR) by the Election Commission of India (ECI), will become the dataset to vet the identities of beneficiaries. This contradicts the Supreme Court’s May 27 judgment on the Bihar SIR and its observations while hearing petitions against West Bengal’s orders removing people deleted during the SIR from the Public Distribution System and the Annapurna Yojana. The Court held that the ECI may undertake only a “limited enquiry” into citizenship to decide who belongs on the electoral roll, and that “any action taken pursuant thereto is confined to electoral consequences alone”. The consequence of deletion from the rolls, it said, is “correspondingly limited” to a person’s place on the roll and their right to vote. The Court also called the EPIC “a derivative document, issued on the basis of inclusion in the electoral roll”, and held that relying on it to verify that very roll would defeat the exercise. It is ironic that Mr. Singh now wants this “derivative document” to be the determinant of welfare benefits.

Not every citizen is an eligible voter, and tying benefits to the electoral roll is illogical and also cruel. In West Bengal, lakhs were deleted from the rolls , many for dubious “logical discrepancies”. In the appeals heard for reinstatement, 93% resulted in the restoration of names by September 2026, pointing to massive pre-election disenfranchisement. The Court has stated that it is yet to adjudicate on the legality of the ECI’s “logical discrepancies” method. The SIR was designed by the ECI to restrict enrolment through stringent residency criteria; thus, itinerant voters had to prove their eligibility. The Opposition, civil society and even some of the BJP’s allies have objected to this, but the BJP refuses to acknowledge the SIR’s flaws. This is partly because it has benefited from disenfranchisement — as in West Bengal. But the Minister’s remarks suggest another reason. The BJP-led coalition sees the pruned electoral rolls as a way to limit welfare, especially at a time when growth in tax revenues has slowed because of the Centre’s policies. Inordinately delaying the Census, changing the procedure to appoint Election Commissioners, who then run an exercise that disenfranchises millions by design, and now, using the resultant rolls to decide who gets welfare, all cut at the heart of the painstakingly built constitutional welfare state. The sooner the Court decides the petitions against the SIR, and reiterates that its rolls cannot be used to curtail welfare, the better.

articles.title: Sonia Gandhi interview: ‘Great damage done to the fabric of India by BJP’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Ahead of the launch of her book, Sonia Gandhi speaks to The Hindu, answering a number of questions — personal and political

In this wide-ranging interview to The Hindu on her soon-to-be-launched book, Belonging: A Journey of Love , published by HarperCollins India, Sonia Gandhi responds in writing to a number of questions, personal, historical, and political, raised by N. Ram.

The subjects covered include how she came to write her story about belonging; the values she grew up with and came to learn and cherish in India; what she learnt from Rajiv Gandhi and Indira Gandhi and how they shaped her life and outlook; the “great damage … done to the fabric of our country, our democracy and our institutions” by the BJP-RSS dispensation; how she viewed, and now looks back on, the Emergency of 1975-1977; the major political decisions she made to accept the office of Congress President in 1998 and to continue in it, after a challenge by some colleagues, in 1999, and in 2004 to decline the offer to become Prime Minister; the current political situation and the prospects of the Congress and its coalition partners; and the change of publisher in India just weeks before the book’s launch.

‘Others have spent decades telling my “story”,’ you posted on X the other day, ‘now it’s my turn.’ My AI-assisted bibliographical search suggests there are at least 75 books, including several biographies, that attempt or purport to tell your story in substantial measure. Your post hints that you were amused rather than irritated or angry about others presuming to tell your story. Am I right? And did you read those books, or at least some of them, written by biographers and others who spent decades telling your ‘story’?

I had no idea there were so many! But I have never felt like reading books about myself. A long time ago Rajiv and I realised that there was no point in trying to keep up with all that had been written about us. But, as I say in the book, there came a time when I felt that I should tell my own story.

In the Prologue to Belonging , you give us an insight into how you came to write your story, ‘perhaps…a story worth sharing,’ as you put it somewhat self-deprecatingly. Was it the ‘chorus’, which was on your case for years, or something within you, or both that eventually pushed you over the line to give us this intimate and unusually candid story? And may I ask how long it took you to write the book, breaks and all?

It’s been such a long time that I’ve lost track, but it has certainly been more than a decade since I first wrote a bit. I only started writing in earnest about five years ago. It wasn’t an uninterrupted process. There were times when words and thoughts flowed, others when nothing would come out, and I would throw my hands up in frustration.

You describe Belonging as a personal memoir, with politics providing the background or ‘a kind of framework’. But it’s really a love story at its heart and that’s how I read it. The story of an extraordinary, instantly formed magnetic bond of love between Rajiv and Sonia, which gradually grew into something much larger, drawing you into the highest circles of power, then reluctantly into public life and politics, and eventually making you one of the country’s foremost political leaders. Stranger than fiction, isn’t it?

Yes! That’s one reason I had no desire to talk about it for so long. But it is not only a love story between the two of us, it’s also the story of how I grew to love Rajiv’s family and the country to which they belonged, and then I too came to belong in it. And of how this love brought me into public life, when I saw the purpose of all the sacrifices they had made being threatened, and the party was weakening. I felt I had to do something.

The writer R.K. Narayan once observed that, despite the passage of time and physical ageing, ‘the chap inside is the same,’ capturing the enduring sense of self. You grew up in a small town in Italy, in a family and social environment far removed from the world that you would eventually inhabit and make your own. Looking back over more than six decades in India, how much of that young Italian woman survives in the person you are today?

The values that I learnt growing up survive. I have tried my best to be true to them: loyalty to family and friends, sincerity and feeling for others, the idea of being dutiful and responsible. I think I can say that in these I am the same person Rajiv met sixty years ago. But I used to smile and laugh a lot more then!

articles.title: Don’t confuse PM Modi, convince him for open debate with me: Rahul Gandhi to Amit Shah
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge has also said the Prime Minister should come forward and face the questions on vote theft that the nation was posing

Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Friday (November 6, 2026) said Home Minister Amit Shah should not confuse Prime Minister Narendra Modi and instead should convince the PM to have an open debate with him on the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
In a post in Hindi, Mr. Gandhi said, “Amit Shah ji, don’t confuse Modi ji. Just convince him to have an open debate with me. Any platform, any time.”
“Daro Mat (Do not be scared),” the leader of the Opposition (LoP) in the Lok Sabha said.

articles.title: Two sisters injured in shooting at Navi Mumbai home; one arrested, another on the run
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: One sister suffered a bullet injury to her back, while the other was grazed near her ear; police are investigating the motive behind the attack

Two sisters, 22 and 20, were injured after a man allegedly opened fire on them inside their home in Koparkhairane, Navi Mumbai, on Thursday night (November 5, 2026). Police have arrested a 22-year-old suspect in connection with the attack, while another accused remains absconding.

The incident took place around 9.30 p.m. in the SS-3 area of Sector 1, Koparkhairane. According to police, the elder sister sustained a grazing bullet injury near her ear, while the younger sister was shot in the back.
The Koparkhairane police have registered a case of attempted murder and offences relating to the illegal possession and use of a firearm.
The arrested accused has been identified as Arjun Chavan, 22, while his alleged accomplice, Rakesh Chavan, is on the run.
According to Nitin Pradeep Dhobi, the victims’ brother, the two sisters were at home with their mother when the attack occurred. Their father and Nitin were away at the time.
Nitin said a man entered the house, opened fire on his sisters and fled. He said his elder sister, 22, is employed, while his younger sister, 20, is a final-year student at Pillai College.

Following the shooting, both women were rushed to a Navi Mumbai Municipal Corporation (NMMC) hospital for treatment. They were subsequently transferred to Sir JJ Hospital in Mumbai for further medical care.
Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP), Zone 1, Vijay M. Kharat said police had visited the NMMC hospital and spoken to the doctors treating the victims before they were shifted to Mumbai.

“Both injured women were immediately admitted to the NMMC hospital. We visited the hospital, spoke to the doctors and assessed their condition. They have now been shifted to JJ Hospital for further treatment,” Mr. Kharat said.

Police said the arrested accused originally hails from Solapur and lived behind the victims’ residence. Investigators are examining whether he was previously acquainted with the sisters and what may have prompted the shooting.

articles.title: Assam prohibits drone operations near Amur falcon roosting sites
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The order follows reports of content creators and visitors flying drones close to congregations of the migratory raptors, apparently to capture photographs and videos for social media
The Assam government on Friday (November 6, 2026) banned drone operations within and around identified Amur falcon congregation sites.

The order banning such operations followed reports of content creators and visitors flying drones close to congregation and roosting sites of the migratory raptors, apparently to capture photographs and videos for social media.

The order, issued by the office of Assam’s Principal Chief Conservator of Forests and Head of Forest Force, specifically prohibits unauthorised recreational, commercial and non-essential drone flying, photography and videography in and around Amur falcon (Falco amurensis) congregation and roosting sites during their seasonal presence.

It also directs the Divisional Forest Officers concerned to identify and demarcate sensitive roosting areas, ensure effective monitoring and protection, and coordinate with district administrations and police authorities for enforcement. It further emphasises public awareness and sensitisation of tourists, photographers, content creators and local communities.

“Amur falcons are remarkable migratory birds, and their congregation sites in Assam are important stopover locations during their extraordinary annual journey. While photography and videography can play an important role in promoting wildlife appreciation, these activities must never compromise the safety of the birds,” Udayan Borthakur of Aaranyak, a biodiversity conservation group, said.

“Drones equipped with high-speed rotating propellers pose a real risk of injury through accidental collisions and can also cause unnecessary disturbance. We hope this order will be strictly implemented and serve as a clear message that wildlife safety must always take precedence over social media content and personal interests,” he said.

Amur Falcons migrate every year from their breeding grounds in eastern Asia to their wintering grounds in southern Africa. Assam hosts important congregation and roosting sites, notably at Umrangso in Dima Hasao district and Dharamtul in Morigaon district, where the birds gather during their seasonal passage.

articles.title: Deepavali 2026: All you need to know about Supreme Court-permitted time slots, green crackers and other directives
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The Supreme Court permitted the bursting of certified green firecrackers between 6 a.m. and 7 a.m. and between 8 p.m. and 10 p.m. on November 7 and November 8, 2026 in Delhi-NCR

The Supreme Court on November 2, 2026 described bursting of firecrackers during Deepavali as a “religious practice” while permitting the use of green firecrackers for two days, on November 7 and November 8, in Delhi-NCR.

The unregulated use of firecrackers during Deepavali has historically led to a sharp rise in the Air Quality Index (AQI) and pollution levels, including the emission of particulate matter, the court observed. “The right of an individual to engage in a particular practice, which may have a religious colour, is only a qualified one and cannot go beyond the Constitutional restrictions,” the Supreme Court held.

The state had “utterly failed” to comply with the Supreme Court’s orders issued since 2015 to impose restrictions on fireworks, the Bench said. In fact, the situation had not improved even after the reimposition of a complete ban on firecrackers. A significant spike in AQI levels was noticed on Dasara and the following day. The “complete ban” had not only facilitated the illegal sale of firecrackers but had also prevented people from purchasing authorised green crackers, the court said.
The court had earlier suggested that the government enlist celebrities such as cricketer Virat Kohli to spread awareness about the harmful effects of firecrackers.

In October 2025, the apex court had permitted the sale and bursting of green firecrackers in Delhi-NCR during Deepavali, subject to conditions aimed at balancing tradition with environmental and health concerns. The court had then made it clear that the use of green crackers would be restricted to specified hours on the festival day and its eve.

The court permitted the bursting of certified green firecrackers between 6 a.m. and 7 a.m. and between 8 p.m. and 10 p.m. on November 7, 2026 and the day after in the Delhi National Capital Region (Delhi-NCR).

“There shall not be any bursting of fireworks within a 300-metre radius of hospitals, nursing homes, primary and district health centres, old age homes and any notified silence zones. These areas will be declared as ‘no-cracker zones’, and shall be marked on the ground and published,” the court said in its 23-page order. The same restriction would apply to educational institutions.

“We are conscious that the celebration of Deepavali has a religious, social, psychological and emotional connotation amongst people, creating a positive atmosphere of hope, welfare and prosperity. That being said, allowing the environment to degrade, which results in a health hazard to all living beings, defeats the very purpose of the festivities, and the celebrations would be rendered nugatory,” the Bench reasoned.

In a series of directions, the court ordered that only manufacturers certified by CSIR-NEERI (Council of Scientific and Industrial Research-National Environmental Engineering Research Institute) and PESO (Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation) would be permitted to manufacture green crackers between November 2, 2026 and November 6, 2026. The cracker boxes would be sealed and kept separate from unauthorised or conventional firecrackers.

There would be no manufacture or sale of firecrackers joined in series ( ladi s) and garlands. Only firecrackers carrying product-specific QR codes would be allowed to be sold. Cancelled licences of traders would be restored temporarily from November 4, 2026 to November 6, 2026. Manufacturers and traders of firecrackers in Delhi-NCR must furnish a monetary security deposit, the amount of which would be determined by the authorities.

articles.title: China says discussions underway on Xi-Trump-Putin meeting

fullParagraphs: President Trump is expected to travel to Shenzhen to meet President Xi for the third time this year, as the fragile trade truce is set to expire in January
Beijing has confirmed for the first time that it is discussing a historic meeting between Chinese President Xi Jinping, U.S. President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Mao Ning, a spokesperson for the Chinese Foreign Ministry, said at a press briefing this week in Beijing that China "is in communication with relevant parties regarding a meeting between the three heads of state."
Nothing is set, but the three-leader gathering would take place this month on the sidelines of a regional summit in Shenzhen.

If it happens, it would be historic. Experts, however, say the three leaders are unlikely to discuss anything substantive because their interests are at odds, but they would gather for a photo, with China carefully choreographing the meeting.

In a sign that tensions persist, U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, in a Friday (November 6, 2026) video call with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng, urged Beijing to take "concrete actions to fully implement its past commitments, particularly as they relate to agricultural purchases, rare earths, and other critical minerals," according to a statement from Greer's office.

China's official news agency Xinhua reported Saturday (November 7) that both sides held in-depth, constructive exchanges on the call, and that China expressed concerns about Washington's restrictive economic and trade measures against Beijing.

While he's in China, Mr. Trump has said he would be interested in meeting Mr. Xi and Mr. Putin to discuss nuclear arms control, though Mr. Putin is focused on talking about the war in Ukraine without Kyiv at the table.

articles.title: Maharashtra to lease reservoir land for fodder cultivation in 304 drought-hit talukas
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The decision is aimed at improving fodder availability for livestock in areas affected by rainfall deficiency during the 2026 kharif season.

The Maharashtra government has decided to lease exposed cultivable land in reservoirs and tanks across 304 drought-declared talukas to farmers and livestock owners for growing short-duration fodder crops, Soil and Water Conservation Minister Sanjay Rathod said on Friday (November 6, 2026).

The decision is aimed at improving fodder availability for livestock in areas affected by rainfall deficiency during the 2026 kharif season. The Soil and Water Conservation Department issued technical guidelines on November 5, outlining the conditions for cultivation, land allotment and water use.

According to Mr. Rathod, farmers will be permitted to cultivate fodder crops such as maize, sorghum, pearl millet, nutrifeed, berseem and oats on eligible land under the department’s jurisdiction. Maize and sorghum grown for silage production will be given preference.
The guidelines will apply to minor irrigation tanks, storage tanks, percolation tanks, village tanks and former Malguzari tanks, among other water bodies.

However, the government has stipulated that drinking water requirements will take precedence over cultivation. Reservoirs supplying drinking water schemes or used for filling water tankers will be subject to existing drinking water reservations. Areas where repairs, desilting or restoration works are underway or proposed will not be made available for cultivation.
Only cultivable land exposed between a reservoir’s full reservoir level and its actual water level will be eligible for allotment.

To protect reservoir infrastructure, cultivation will be prohibited within 50 metres of the reservoir-side toe of an earthen dam, and within 30 metres of spillways, their approach areas and structures such as outlets, intake wells, jackwells, gauge poles and benchmarks.
The use of chemical fertilisers and pesticides will also be prohibited for cultivation within 200 metres of drinking water source wells or jackwells.

Under the allotment process, officials from the Revenue, Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Soil and Water Conservation departments will conduct joint surveys to identify eligible land. The executive engineer concerned must submit an availability report to a district-level committee within 15 days of the government resolution.

The committee, headed by the district collector, will review the land available under each project, approve allotments, select beneficiaries and determine the maximum area that can be leased to an individual beneficiary.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity 📅 07 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 3 Min Read

📰 Maharashtra to lease reservoir land for fodder cultivation in 304 drought-hit talukas

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

The decision is aimed at improving fodder availability for livestock in areas affected by rainfall deficiency during the 2026 kharif season.

The Maharashtra government has decided to lease exposed cultivable land in reservoirs and tanks across 304 drought-declared talukas to farmers and livestock owners for growing short-duration fodder crops, Soil and Water Conservation Minister Sanjay Rathod said on Friday (November 6, 2026).

The decision is aimed at improving fodder availability for livestock in areas affected by rainfall deficiency during the 2026 kharif season. The Soil and Water Conservation Department issued technical guidelines on November 5, outlining the conditions for cultivation, land allotment and water use.

According to Mr. Rathod, farmers will be permitted to cultivate fodder crops such as maize, sorghum, pearl millet, nutrifeed, berseem and oats on eligible land under the department’s jurisdiction. Maize and sorghum grown for silage production will be given preference.

The guidelines will apply to minor irrigation tanks, storage tanks, percolation tanks, village tanks and former Malguzari tanks, among other water bodies.

However, the government has stipulated that drinking water requirements will take precedence over cultivation. Reservoirs supplying drinking water schemes or used for filling water tankers will be subject to existing drinking water reservations. Areas where repairs, desilting or restoration works are underway or proposed will not be made available for cultivation.

Only cultivable land exposed between a reservoir’s full reservoir level and its actual water level will be eligible for allotment.

To protect reservoir infrastructure, cultivation will be prohibited within 50 metres of the reservoir-side toe of an earthen dam, and within 30 metres of spillways, their approach areas and structures such as outlets, intake wells, jackwells, gauge poles and benchmarks.

The use of chemical fertilisers and pesticides will also be prohibited for cultivation within 200 metres of drinking water source wells or jackwells.

Under the allotment process, officials from the Revenue, Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Soil and Water Conservation departments will conduct joint surveys to identify eligible land. The executive engineer concerned must submit an availability report to a district-level committee within 15 days of the government resolution.

The committee, headed by the district collector, will review the land available under each project, approve allotments, select beneficiaries and determine the maximum area that can be leased to an individual beneficiary.
