fullParagraphs: In Maharashtra’s Hupari town, women artisans drive a ₹1,000-crore silver industry, sustaining a century-old trade. Radheshyam Jadhav reports on how, despite being underpaid and excluded from formal leadership, they forge their own economic autonomy in a deeply traditional landscape

On an afternoon just about a month before Deepavali, Kanchan Katkar, 76, deftly picks up silver ghungroos with a pair of iron tongs that fit into her palm. She attaches them to chain loops. “I have been doing this for decades and will continue to do this as long as I am able,” she says, her voice bearing a gentle tremor. Deep inside her dimly lit house, hidden within the twisting lanes of Hupari town, where rooms line up like wagons on a track, Katkar sits in the shadows.

Back in 1970, Kanchan was one of the few girls who completed school in Hupari. Marriage then was taken for granted, but after her two sisters wed, she decided to stay single to care for her parents, who had actively participated in the Indian freedom struggle.

articles.title: Will do something for Singur, West Bengal CM signals fresh industrial push
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said that the government was in talks with Ashok Leyland for setting up a plant at Singur

West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Thursday (November 5, 2026) said that his government is in talks with multinational vehicle manufacturer Ashok Leyland for setting up a plant at Singur, signalling a fresh push for the site of Tata Nano project abandoned almost 18 years ago.
“We will do something about Singur. Talks are on with Ashok Leyland,” the Chief Minister said.

Speaking to media persons at an event to unveil “The West Bengal Investment Promotion Policy, 2026”, the Chief Minister said the withdrawal of Tatas from Singur in October 2008 over protests against forcible land acquisition is considered one of the defining setbacks of West Bengal’s dreams of an industrial revival. The protest against forcible land acquisition was led by Mamata Banerjee and after she came to power in 2011, Trinamool Congress government returned land to farmers.
Mr. Adhikari had in the past said that the land at Singur now belongs to farmers and for setting up any industry, the land has to be acquired again.

The Chief Minister said that his government will not use police to forcibly acquire land like the Left Front government, and not follow hands-off approach of Trinamool Congress government. “We will purchase lands ourselves. Talks are on with HUDCO, NABARD, ADB for funds to purchase lands. We have handed over land to companies in Panagarh and Haringhata,” Mr Adhikari said.
The 34-page investment promotion policy has no reference of land and according to officials of the State government there will be a separate policy document on acquiring land for industries.

The Chief Minister said that West Bengal government officials were studying land policies in industry-rich states like Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Maharashtra and also Uttar Pradesh for land purchase, pooling and development.

Pointing out that his government over the past five months has handed over land to 33 business groups, including Amul, Vedanta Group, Campa Cola and Reliance, to set up new plants, Mr. Adhikari said that his government was a position to meet the current demand for industrial plots of around Rs 1 lakh crore over the next few months.

The Chief Minister on Thursday (November 5, 2026) also issued a message to industries who are sitting on land allocated by the State government either to start new units in three months or return land back to the government at the price it was acquired. Several prominent captains of industry have met Mr. Adhikari over the past few weeks and promised to start new industries or expand their operations in West Bengal on the land they had acquired in the past.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity 📅 06 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 3 Min Read

Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said that the government was in talks with Ashok Leyland for setting up a plant at Singur

West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Thursday (November 5, 2026) said that his government is in talks with multinational vehicle manufacturer Ashok Leyland for setting up a plant at Singur, signalling a fresh push for the site of Tata Nano project abandoned almost 18 years ago.

“We will do something about Singur. Talks are on with Ashok Leyland,” the Chief Minister said.

Speaking to media persons at an event to unveil “The West Bengal Investment Promotion Policy, 2026”, the Chief Minister said the withdrawal of Tatas from Singur in October 2008 over protests against forcible land acquisition is considered one of the defining setbacks of West Bengal’s dreams of an industrial revival. The protest against forcible land acquisition was led by Mamata Banerjee and after she came to power in 2011, Trinamool Congress government returned land to farmers.

Mr. Adhikari had in the past said that the land at Singur now belongs to farmers and for setting up any industry, the land has to be acquired again.

The Chief Minister said that his government will not use police to forcibly acquire land like the Left Front government, and not follow hands-off approach of Trinamool Congress government. “We will purchase lands ourselves. Talks are on with HUDCO, NABARD, ADB for funds to purchase lands. We have handed over land to companies in Panagarh and Haringhata,” Mr Adhikari said.

The 34-page investment promotion policy has no reference of land and according to officials of the State government there will be a separate policy document on acquiring land for industries.

The Chief Minister said that West Bengal government officials were studying land policies in industry-rich states like Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Maharashtra and also Uttar Pradesh for land purchase, pooling and development.

Pointing out that his government over the past five months has handed over land to 33 business groups, including Amul, Vedanta Group, Campa Cola and Reliance, to set up new plants, Mr. Adhikari said that his government was a position to meet the current demand for industrial plots of around Rs 1 lakh crore over the next few months.

The Chief Minister on Thursday (November 5, 2026) also issued a message to industries who are sitting on land allocated by the State government either to start new units in three months or return land back to the government at the price it was acquired. Several prominent captains of industry have met Mr. Adhikari over the past few weeks and promised to start new industries or expand their operations in West Bengal on the land they had acquired in the past.

articles.title: J&K’s health sector receives a shot in arm as Union Minister J.P. Nadda sets AIIMS deadline for March
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: During a review of the phase-wise construction and handover plan, the Union Minister was informed that Phase-I buildings, including the OPD Registration Block, OPD Block, residential buildings and designated hostels, had been completed

Union Health Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda on Thursday (November 5, 2026) announced that the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) at Awantipora in south Kashmir would be completed by March 2027.

“AIIMS, Awantipora, is a priority project. The concerned agencies should maintain the momentum and complete the remaining construction works by March 2027,” Mr. Nadda said while reviewing the project.

During a review of the phase-wise construction and handover plan, the Union Minister was informed that Phase-I buildings, including the OPD Registration Block, OPD Block, residential buildings and designated hostels, had been completed. Inventory verification and formal handover processes are under way.
“The remaining academic, administrative, hospital, residential and hostel infrastructure is being taken up in a phased manner,” officials said.

Mr. Nadda also directed that all essential procurements required for the commencement of OPD services be completed on priority. Approval has been conveyed for the procurement of 180 medical equipment items worth ₹59.41 crore, of which Notices of Award have been issued for 140 items.
Officials said academic activities, including commencement of MBBS classes, are proposed for the academic session 2027–28, beginning June–July 2027.
J&K Heath Minister Sakima Itoo, who welcomed the Union Minister, praised the Centre for its support in reinforcing the healthcare infrastructure of J&K.

“It was a matter of great happiness that the Union Health Minister, who had earlier announced 50 MBBS seats, today announced that 100 MBBS students will start classes here soon. The start of OPD services at AIIMS Awantipora will make a huge difference for patients in Kashmir, who presently have to travel long distances for advanced treatment,” Ms. Itoo said.
The AIIMS Awantipora is expected to significantly augment the region’s healthcare capacity.

Meanwhile, Opposition Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) leader Iltija Mufti said the AIIMS Awantipora was a dream not only envisaged by Mufti (Muhammad Sayeed) sahab but also fulfilled 10 years later is a testament of his vision for J&K. “Really wish he was alive because it would’ve given him immense happiness to see south Kashmir get top notch healthcare,” said Ms. Mufti.

articles.title: Violence mars third phase of Rajasthan panchayat elections
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Polling in the third phase of panchayat elections for sarpanch and ward panch posts in 27 districts of Rajasthan on Thursday was marred by clashes, stone-pelting, allegations of bogus voting and protests at several places. Supporters of rival candidates clashed in Sikar, Chittorgarh, and Balotra districts.

A dispute between supporters of two sarpanch candidates turned violent at Delsar village in the Nawalgarh area of Jhunjhunu district, with the two sides allegedly attacking each other with sticks and batons. A youth from Punjab’s Hoshiarpur died in the clash, while two others sustained injuries.

The police detained several persons for questioning and seized vehicles. At Bassi in Chittorgarh district, police resorted to a lathi charge after supporters of two candidates clashed over alleged bogus voting. Tension prevailed in Sikar’s Sami village after stones were hurled at a vehicle near a polling station. Sarpanch candidate Arun Pareek was allegedly assaulted by his rival and around 50 supporters at Bhojya Ki Dhani village panchayat.

Voting for the sarpanch post was cancelled at Ludi Jhabar village panchayat in Rajgarh panchayat samiti of Churu district after the nomination of the only candidate was rejected during scrutiny. No election was held in the absence of a candidate.
Polling was held in 3,716 village panchayats under 116 panchayat samitis for 3,716 sarpanch and 34,218 ward panch seats.

articles.title: From ghee masala dosa to Mysore pak, Bengaluru’s favourite foods set to cost more
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Prices of items like ghee masala dosa, kesari bath, upma, pongal, ghee rice, bisibele bath, rotis, naans, parottas and sweets like halwa will also be increased”

Following the increase in the prices of ghee, butter and paneer, hotel associations and sweet shops will also be increasing the prices of sweets and food items in which ghee, butter and paneer are used.

Veerendra Kamat, secretary, Bangalore Hotels Association, said, “Ghee, butter and paneer prices were increased a day ago. Before that, milk and curd prices had increased. Hence, tea and coffee prices in all hotels across the city, from small to big ones, have increased by ₹3 to ₹5. Now prices of items like ghee masala dosa, kesari bath, upma, pongal, ghee rice, bisibele bath, rotis, naans, parottas and sweets like halwa will also be increased.”

Mr. Kamat added, “An average price of ghee masala dosa is ₹120 to ₹130 across most of the hotels, which will be increased up to ₹125 to ₹135. Some premium hotels charge up to ₹200 also. Other items like kesari bath, ghee rice, pongal and bisibele bath will also be increased by ₹5. We cannot increase these prices beyond ₹5 because customers will stop coming and the entire business will be impacted.”

He also clarified that the association cannot set a standard price for all the hotels. “Hoteliers price the dishes as per the location of the hotel, customer footfall, scale of business, and profit and loss, which is calculated at the end of every month,” he added.

Meanwhile, Madhu Iyengar, general secretary, Karnataka Bakeries, Sweets and Cafe Association (KBSCA), said, “When prices of milk and curds had increased, we thought to continue selling sweets on the same scale or price.But the ghee price hike has impacted our budgets too. Since it is the festival season, where we aim to make good business, we have not increased prices of any sweet where milk and ghee are used. However, we will increase the price probably in December during the off-season by 3% to 5%.”

Arjun P., a manager working at a famous sweet outlet that has branches across the city, said, “In our shop, special Mysore Pak made using ghee is priced at ₹473 for 500 grams, and Kaju Katli at ₹700 for 500 grams. Mango barfi and doodh pedha are probably the lowest, priced around ₹419 for 500 grams. Kesar peda is priced at ₹473 for 500 grams. When the prices are hiked in December or during New Year, all these will be increased by ₹5 to ₹10.”

Apart from hotels and sweet shops, households have also felt the heat of the price rise, especially during Deepavali. Prathiba Reddy, a resident of Ramamurthy Nagar, said, “People are yet to recover from the milk and curd price hike, and the government has gone ahead to increase ghee, paneer and butter prices. During the festival, I use ghee for most of the items, either to fry or mix it with maida and wheat flour for making snacks and sweets. A one-litre sachet of Nandini ghee has gone up by almost ₹135.”

Expressing disappointment over the price hike of essential commodities, Manjunath M., a gig worker, said, “Festivals are not for poor people like us who earn less than ₹20,000 a month and have five people in a family to look after. The milk and ghee price hike have impacted a working-class person like me.”

articles.title: Santiago Pena, Paraguay President, steps down as banking crisis sows chaos
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Thousands of Paraguayans gathered outside Congress on Thursday (November 5, 2026) to protest against the President
Paraguayan President Santiago Pena resigned on Thursday (November 5, 2026) after the takeover of a bank linked to the U.S.-allied leader blocked almost half the population from accessing their money.
The Central Bank’s seizure of Ueno Bank two days earlier froze the deposits of some three million people, including pensioners, and sparked angry demonstrations across the country.
Thousands of Paraguayans gathered outside Congress on Thursday (November 5, 2026) to protest against the President, who is still technically in power as his resignation awaits parliamentary approval.
“Give back the money,” AFP journalists heard them yelling. Earlier demonstrations featured clashes with the police, who used tear gas and water cannons on the crowd.
“My family ran out of money, we don’t have any cash. Santi (Pena) is a criminal, he has to go to jail,” 21-year-old student protester Andres Maldonado told AFP.

Lawmakers voted unanimously on Thursday (November 5, 2026) to launch impeachment proceedings against Mr. Pena over the crisis, alleging misconduct and a conflict of interest in dealings with the bank to which he is tied.
The right-wing President said he would attend his impeachment trial, which is set to begin on Friday (November 6, 2026), after earlier apologizing to the people of Paraguay.
“It was never my intention to betray the trust you placed in me,” he said in a video posted on X announcing his resignation.
Mr. Pena’s priority, he added, is “the peace of mind of Paraguayans who entrusted their savings to our financial system.”
Paraguay’s Central Bank said it took over Ueno due to a severe capital shortfall, in order to “protect depositors and preserve the stability of the financial system.”

articles.title: Donald Trump predicts deal with Russia on Ukraine and ‘all of Europe’
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The U.S. president’s comments will fuel European fears that Mr. Trump is pivoting towards the Kremlin and will push Ukraine into an unfavorable deal to end Russia’s invasion

U.S. President Donald Trump on Thursday (November 5, 2026) predicted a “very big” deal with Russia involving not only the Ukraine war but “all of Europe”, after meeting Russian leader Vladimir Putin’s envoy at the White House.
Mr. Trump revealed that he had an unscheduled meeting with Kirill Dmitriev, who was at the White House for talks with Ukrainian officials hosted by U.S. First Lady Melania Trump .
“I can’t tell you what I discussed. But I’m just telling you, it’s going to be an agreement, it’s going to be a big agreement,” Mr. Trump told reporters in the Oval Office.

“It’s going to be very big. It’s going to involve more than Ukraine, and I could even say it might involve all of Europe. It’s going to be a big, beautiful agreement, and everyone’s going to be thrilled.”
Mr. Trump said he had not met with Ukrainian officials who were also at the White House on Thursday (November 5, 2026).
NATO capitals are also watching to see if Trump, who has hinted at withdrawing troops from the continent, will meet Putin’s maximalist demands to reduce U.S. influence in Europe.
But Mr. Trump, who promised to end the Ukraine war within 24 hours of taking office in January 2025, has also repeatedly touted looming peace deals in the past which never materialized.
Ms. Melania Trump had earlier called for a new, “more enduring” ceasefire in Ukraine as she hosted a rare meeting between officials from the war-torn country and Russia at the White House.
Mr. Trump said the meeting and a localized six-day truce in the starvation-hit Ukrainian city of Oleshky that the U.S. First Lady announced last month could be a stepping stone to a wider deal.

fullParagraphs: For over two years, 45 toddy-tapper and 10 Dalit families in Nizamabad’s Tallarampur have allegedly faced a complete social boycott for defying their Village Development Committee’s (VDC) orders. Denied access to groceries, medical aid and social gatherings, they have been pushed to the margins of everyday life. The growing clout of VDCs and nearly 90 complaints of alleged excesses before the Backward Classes Commission bring the larger issue into focus, as Ravi Reddy finds during a ground visit

On a sunny afternoon last year, 40-year-old Kairi Kalyani dressed in her festive best and stepped out of her home with a plate of offerings, including turmeric, kumkum , flowers, coconuts and fruits. It was Sri Rama Navami, and Kalyani, along with a dozen other women from her neighbourhood in Tallarampur village of Nizamabad district, arrived at the local Ramalayam to perform kumkumarchana .

But what was meant to be a day of prayer and celebration quickly turned into an experience of humiliation. Just as the women settled among the other devotees, the temple priest allegedly asked them to leave. The reason? They belonged to the Goud (toddy-tapper) community and were not permitted to perform rituals at the temple!

Just as the women settled among the other devotees, the temple priest allegedly asked them to leave. The reason? They belonged to the Goud (toddy-tapper) community and were not permitted to perform rituals at the temple!

articles.title: Maharashtra Government makes provision for ₹160 crore in 2026-27 Budget for development of primitive tribes
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The package includes 130 crore reserved for primitive tribes, ₹30 crore reserved for the Pardhi community, and also provides for 100% government grant for individual and collective benefit schemes

Under ‘Viksit Maharashtra 2047’, the Maharashtra Government made provision for a special package of ₹160 crore in the 2026-27 Budget for the “holistic development of the primitive tribes” — Katkari, Kolam and Madia — along with the Pardhi community.
The package includes 130 crore reserved for primitive tribes, ₹30 crore reserved for the Pardhi community, and also provides for 100% government grant for individual and collective benefit schemes.

The ₹130 crore will be further divided and allocated as follows: ₹100 crore for basic amenities and ₹30 crore for individual and collective benefit schemes. For the Pardhi community, ₹10 crore will be allocated for basic amenities and ₹20 crore for individual and collective benefit schemes.
The announcement to provide funds through a special package for the holistic development of primitive communities was made in the 2026-27 Budget.
The State Government issued a Government Resolution (GR) on 2 November 2026 to implement the package.
The minimum grant of ₹50,000 will be given for an individual scheme, and up to a maximum of ₹7.5 lakh for a collective scheme of two or more beneficiaries.

“If beneficiaries are deprived of benefits under schemes of other departments because they are unable to pay their own share, then the Tribal Development Department will chip in. Greater encouragement will be given to the formation of women’s Self-Help Groups (SHGs) for women’s empowerment, enabling women to take up collective ventures and achieve economic empowerment of their families, groups will be given grants of up to ₹7.5 lakh,” stated in a CMO statement.

The funds will also be used to organise awareness drives and special camps, providing essential documents like Aadhaar Card, Voter ID Card, Ration Card, Caste Certificate, MGNREGA Job Card, Ayushman Card and Bank Account. Health check-up camps, visits by Anganwadi workers, ASHA workers and nurses, health education and benefits of government health schemes will also be provided.

The package also includes increasing student attendance, bringing out-of-school children into the mainstream of education, and organising residential camps in Ashram Schools during summer for children of migrant families.

articles.title: Sarah Jukaku: First Muslim U.S. senator’s wife has a Karnataka link
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Dr. Sarah is the granddaughter of the late J.H. Shamsuddin Jukaku, a lawyer from Bhatkal who served as Deputy Finance Minister in the erstwhile Mysore State government, led by the then Chief Minister B.D. Jatti, in the late 1950s and early 1960s.

Sarah Jukaku, a doctor and wife of Democrat Abdul EI-Sayed , who is the first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate in the midterm elections, traces her family roots to Bhatkal in Uttara Kannada district, of Karnataka, according to media reports.

Dr. Sarah is the granddaughter of the late J.H. Shamsuddin Jukaku, a lawyer from Bhatkal who served as Deputy Finance Minister in the erstwhile Mysore State government, led by the then Chief Minister B.D. Jatti, in the late 1950s and early 1960s. Shamsuddin was also the Deputy Minister for Electricity in the then government led by then Chief Minister S. Nijalingappa, reports said.
It is said that following the death of Shamsuddin, his family members shifted to different parts of India, including to Bengaluru.
Reports said that Dr. Sarah is the daughter of Jukaku S. Tayeb, also a doctor, who was among four sons of Shamsuddin, who also had six daughters. Dr. Tayeb moved to the U.S. in the 1980s.
They said that Dr. Sarah met EI-Sayed in the University of Michigan and they got married in 2006. Reports said that their family has still maintained relations with family members in India.

articles.title: Buyers want bang for the buck as green crackers fail to deliver
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Traders say delayed licences have squeezed the window of sale, while confusion over green crackers persists as buyers continue to expect the familiar loud bangs of conventional fireworks.

Light travels faster than sound. Across Hyderabad, brightly lit firecracker stalls have sprung up ahead of Deepavali, their colourful displays drawing attention in several pockets of the city. Large makeshift tents lined with rows of fireworks have come up at designated locations, with fire extinguishers and other safety measures in place. Traders are preparing for the festive rush, but some say business has been slower than in previous years, even as the market undergoes a gradual shift towards green crackers.

Green crackers, developed as a less polluting alternative to conventional fireworks, are intended to reduce emissions and noise. Their adoption has gathered pace over the past few years, with several established brands moving towards greener variants. However, the transition has also brought a change in the sound and performance that customers have traditionally associated with firecrackers.

Sanjay Kumar Gupta of Ramamurthy Trading Company, which has been in the business since 1975, said many customers were still unaware of the distinction between green and conventional crackers. Some mistake the comparatively lower sound levels of green crackers for a decline in quality, he said.

“For customers, Deepavali is synonymous with crackers, blasts and bangs. They expect that familiar sound. When green crackers do not make a loud bang like traditional ones, they assume that the quality of established brands has gone down,” he said. Another trader said some customers even returned to complain about the sound, believing that the crackers were not performing as expected.

Myakala Venugopal of Shivashakti Agency, who has been in the business for 30 years, said the range of green crackers had expanded considerably. Even fancy fireworks, which were earlier not available in green variants, were now being manufactured as green crackers. Customers who are more conscious of environmental concerns specifically ask for them, he said.

Raghavendra of Hyderabad Crackers in Kukatpally said the shift towards green crackers began around 2021, with popular brands gradually moving to green variants. Their packaging now carries the green symbol, he said. While some fancy fireworks have stopped being produced, even the classic mirchi bombs now produce less sound and smoke.

He said the quality and packaging of green crackers had improved this year, with a majority of customers asking for them. However, a lack of awareness about the green crackers initiative continued to result in complaints from some buyers.

Several customers are also opting to place bulk orders directly with manufacturers in Sivakasi, including Standard Fireworks, at wholesale rates. “I have two children, and every Deepavali we invite my nieces, nephews and other relatives home to celebrate together. It has become a family tradition, so we need a large quantity of crackers. Buying directly from manufacturers in Sivakasi works out cheaper than purchasing them in smaller quantities from retail stalls,” said Ravi Kumar, a resident of Kowkoor.

For traders, the challenges this season have extended beyond changing customer preferences. Gupta said he applied for a licence around 20 days ago but received it only on November 5, four days before the festival. He said receiving licences at least 10 days before the festival would make a considerable difference to businesses.

“We are now hoping to break even, not even make a profit. Earlier, we did not have even a minute of free time. Now it is 8.30 p.m. and I am sitting idle and talking to you, with just four or five customers looking around the stall. Families involved in this business struggle throughout the year to deal with the losses during this season,” he said.

fullParagraphs: The decision, taken at a meeting of MSRTC officials on Wednesday (November 4, 2026), also includes an advance payment of ₹12,500 for eligible employees and an increase in Dearness Allowance (DA) from 58% to 60%
Maharashtra Transport Minister Pratap Sarnaik has announced a ₹10,000 ex-gratia grant for each of the 83,000 officers and employees of the Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation (MSRTC).

The decision, taken at a meeting of MSRTC officials on Wednesday (November 4, 2026), also includes an advance payment of ₹12,500 for eligible employees and an increase in Dearness Allowance (DA) from 58% to 60%.

“Despite the financial difficulties faced by the MSRTC, employees should not be deprived of the joy of Diwali,” Mr. Sarnaik said. He added that the measures would impose an additional financial burden of around ₹160 crore on the Corporation. However, he said, employees’ efforts to provide safe transport services to lakhs of passengers needed to be rewarded.
Mr. Sarnaik also appealed to ST employees not to resort to agitation or a strike, saying that their grievances could be resolved through dialogue.

articles.title: The war that defeated ‘America First’
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The central question now is whether Washington can recover the capacity to distinguish supporting an ally from subordinating its own interests

U.S. Vice-President J.D. Vance has supplied the most politically damaging explanation of the Republican mid-term debacle: “The reason we lost is the war.” His assessment deserves attention because it identifies a contradiction at the heart of Donald Trump’s presidency. An administration elected in large part on promises to avoid costly foreign entanglements made the U.S. a participant in another West Asian war without evidence that it advanced American interests. Republicans have now paid a huge electoral price for that reversal.

Mr. Vance’s explanation goes beyond the familiar claim that disappointed supporters stayed home. He argues that former Trump voters crossed over to the Democrats. He identified four demands among these defectors: ending the war, addressing living costs, putting American interests first, and changing Washington’s relationship with Israel. The political significance of his diagnosis is unmistakable. The administration’s own second-in-command has connected Republican losses to the collision between its nationalist promises and its foreign policy.
Global & Diplomatic Brief: The war that defeated ‘America First’. This development underscores India's strategic autonomy and pragmatic engagement in bilateral and multilateral diplomacy.

articles.title: A noisy Anthropocene is imposing fatal stress on wildlife
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Researchers analysed over 200 experimental studies on 177 aquatic and terrestrial species across six continents and found that noise altered specific traits in 80% of the animals studied

The Anthropocene , the epoch of sweeping human-dominated planetary change, has ushered in an understudied phenomenon: extreme noise pollution. And the polluted soundscape is not just a human health hazard, but impacts the dynamics of wildlife too, physiologically, developmentally and behaviourally, found a new study published in Science.

The din of traffic, industrial activity, offshore construction, petroleum exploration, sonar operations and multiple other sources of noise, which has consistently increased during the past 50 years, affects over a 100 aquatic and terrestrial species, said the paper.

Science, Space & Environment Report: A noisy Anthropocene is imposing fatal stress on wildlife. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

articles.title: Anti-dam activist rejects Arunachal government’s invitation for talks, says time for negotiations is over
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Katon Moyong, a prominent voice against the proposed 11,200-MW Siang project, called the national security argument an attempt to overcome public resistance

Katon Moyong, popularly known as ‘Abor Man’ and a prominent voice opposing the proposed 11,200-MW hydropower project in the Siang valley of Arunachal Pradesh, has rejected the State government’s offer of talks, saying the time for negotiations has passed.

The engineer-turned-activist, whom the Delhi Police detained recently for protesting the project in the national capital, dismissed the government’s national security argument for building the dam on the Siang river as an attempt to overcome public resistance.

The Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP), one of the biggest hydropower projects planned in the north-eastern State, envisages the construction of a large dam across the Siang. It will be executed by the National Hydroelectric Power Corporation.

The project has been facing stiff resistance from the Adi community, particularly in the Siang region, over concerns about the displacement of people, the submergence of ancestral lands and forests, and the impact on their cultural and ecological heritage.

The Arunachal Pradesh government has said the project is primarily aimed at storing and managing water in the Siang basin, particularly in view of concerns over China’s proposed mega dam on the river upstream.

Mr. Moyong said the Adi community’s position against the dam remained unchanged, alleging that the government’s push for the project was politically motivated, with an eye on the 2029 Assembly elections. He appealed to the indigenous communities of Arunachal Pradesh to remain united against the project, and cautioned them against “attempts to divide” different tribes over the issue.

“The time for discussion on the SUMP has passed,” he told a press conference at the Arunachal Press Club in Itanagar on Thursday (November 5, 2026). “Let there be dams on smaller rivers, but not on the Siang. Either the entire Adi community will have to be exterminated to build the Siang dam, or there will be no Siang dam.”

Mr. Moyong claimed the first proposal for a dam on the Siang was introduced in 1979 under the banner of Brahmaputra flood control, but was rejected by the Adi community. He blamed the government of the late Chief Minister Dorjee Khandu for signing 145 memoranda of understanding (MoUs) with power developers and private companies, which he alleged had pushed the State into a huge debt burden.

Successive governments changed the justification for the project over the years, describing it as a flood mitigation initiative, a project of national interest and a national project, before the present government began promoting it as a national security imperative, he claimed.

Protesters have been demanding an immediate stop to the continuing Pre-Feasibility Report (PFR) activities and survey work for the project. They have also sought the withdrawal of security forces deployed in areas likely to be affected.

articles.title: Hyderabad Metro-RTC Bus common pass charges dropped from ₹8,500 to ₹4,000 for monthly pass
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Revised charges effective from November 8, 2026

Telangana government has slashed charges for Hyderabad Metro-RTC common pass by more than half for the monthly pass and by 31% for the daily. While the number of trips using the passes was unlimited earlier, there is a cap now. The revised prices will come into effect from Sunday (November 8, 2026).

The earlier prices were ₹8,500 for the monthly pass and ₹400 for the daily. The steep prices were criticised soon after the launch. The maximum charges to travel between Miyapur and L.B. Nagar (red line), and Nagole to Raidurg (blue line) is ₹69.

Transport Minister Ponnam Prabhakar announced on Friday (November 6, 2026) that the monthly pass charges are reduced to ₹4,000, with ₹3,000 for commuting in Metro and ₹1,000 for RTC services. A maximum of 50 round trips in a month can be availed using the pass.
The charges of daily pass were reduced from ₹400 to ₹275, with ₹200 for Metro services and ₹75 for RTC. A maximum of four ‘single journeys’ in a day are permitted.

The Transport Minister said that the decision was taken to reduce travel costs for people and make public transport services accessible. He said it is a gift for people on the occasion of Deepavali. Officials were directed to take measures for implementation of the revised prices from November 8.

articles.title: ‘Vested interests trying to turn Kannada Sahitya Parishat into a political organisation’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Former chairman of the Kannada Development Authority S.G. Siddaramaiah campaigns for Janagere Venkataramaiah

“Some vested interests are trying to turn the Kannada Sahitya Parishat (KSP) into a political organisation. It is the responsibility of every Kannadiga to fight against it and try to retain it as a non-political advocacy group that fights for the language and culture of the land,” former chairman of Kannada Development Authority S.G. Siddaramaiah said in Belagavi on November 4.

“KSP is a symbol of the cultural identity of the Kannada language, the Kannada people, and the state of Karnataka. It must function autonomously, free from the control of any political party or faction,” Professor Siddaramaiah told reporters after meeting writers and Kannada activists to campaign for Janagere Venkataramaiah , a candidate in the upcoming KSP election. He said that like-minded writers and activists had chosen Mr. Venkataramaiah as it was essential to preserve the Parishat’s core vision and dignity.

“Some developments over the past few decades had run counter to the KSP’s foundational objectives. This is a matter of grave concern over the increasing interference of political parties in the elections. Some parties have succeeded in taking over cultural institutions like the Mythic Society in Bengaluru. We should not let that happen with KSP,” he said.

“Mahesh Joshi, the outgoing president of KSP, has acted in a non-democratic manner. He has taken several decisions that were against the spirit of Kannada. He unilaterally amended the bylaws to extend the term of the president to six years and gave himself unhinged powers. He threatened the other office-bearers and district unit KSP presidents with legal challenges. He faces allegations of misusing around ₹8 crore of KSP funds. A case has been filed in a court. Mr. Joshi conducted meetings in a way that undermined democratic principles,” he said.

“Mr. Joshi removed a quote embodying adi kavi Pampa’s message of humanism from the Parishat premises, and relocated the statue of the founder Nalwadi Krishnaraja Wodeyar. articles.title: SC clarifies its March 2026 verdict on OBC creamy layer policy will not apply retrospectively
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: As far as the operation of the 2025 batch was concerned, the Court said the service allocation would be in compliance with the March 2026 judgment

The Supreme Court on Friday (November 6, 2026) clarified that the the ratio of the March 11, 2026 judgment, to re-assess OBC non-creamy layer status as per a 1993 Office Memorandum by excluding parental salary income and agricultural income from the income/wealth test, will not apply retrospectively.

The Court, in its judgment, however, did not agree with the government’s plea for a “reasonable time” of two years to undertake the necessary exercise of establishing equivalence of posts, after consulting stakeholders and formulating an appropriate and uniform policy/mechanism for determination of OBC creamy layer status.
As far as the operation of the 2025 batch was concerned, the Court said the service allocation would be in compliance with the March 2026 judgment.

The government had said a retrospective implementation of the Supreme Court verdict would have significant consequences for recruitment, service allocation, cadre allocation, seniority, admissions and the administration of OBC reservation generally, affecting lakhs.

“The Court has power under Article 142 of the Constitution to declare its judgment prospective. If the judgment is not given prospective effect, it will entail several harsh and unjust unintended consequences on employees/ appointees who were not even parties to the litigation and complete administrative chaos. It is therefore prayed that the judgment (Union of India versus Rohith Nathan) be given prospective effect so that ongoing and past recruitment processes are not affected,” the Centre had urged.

Ms. Bhati had submitted that an implementation of the March 11 judgment, particularly with retrospective effect, may affect allocation of services since 2012. Retrospective re -allocation would impact existing seniority and gradation and affect recruitments undertaken by major employers like the railways, banks, Department of Posts and paramilitary services.

The implementation of the judgment currently would not only affect admissions in higher educational institutions and but also candidates involved in ongoing examinations/recruitment processes post the judgment. Ms. Bhati said an immediate move would have consequences on OBC reservation policy across the country.
She had said the government required sufficient time for determination of a new policy to correct hostile discrimination as pointed out by the court in the judgment.

Senior advocate P. Wilson, who represents the candidates, objected while contending that the Centre was merely trying to delay, even undo a final judgment of the apex court. He criticised that the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) had failed to comply with court directions, Parliamentary Committee recommendations, and its own 1993 rules. He said the government could very well create supernumerary posts to accommodate eligible OBC candidates.

In its judgment, the court had directed the DoPT to create supernumerary posts within six months to accommodate eligible Other Backward Castes-Non-Creamy Layer (OBC-NCL) candidates who were wrongfully denied service allocations due to improper creamy layer classification.

articles.title: Perpetrators of attacks against Blue Helmets must be held accountable: India at UN
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: India is among the largest troop-contributing countries to UN peacekeeping, having deployed more than 3,00,000 troops across 50 missions to date
India has called for holding perpetrators of attacks against UN peacekeepers accountable, underlining that Blue Helmets face asymmetric and technologically enabled threats.
India is among the largest troop-contributing countries to UN peacekeeping , having deployed more than 3,00,000 troops across 50 missions to date.

“India upholds the safety and security of peacekeepers as one of the most important aspects of peacekeeping," Military Advisor at the Permanent Mission of India to the UN, Colonel Tarunendra Pratap Singh, said on Thursday (November 5, 2026).

"Personnel today face asymmetric and technologically-enabled threats, and those who attack peacekeepers must be held accountable,” Colonel Singh said while addressing the annual debate on comprehensive review of the whole question of peacekeeping operations in all their aspects.

He said India's continued leadership on UN Security Council resolution 2589 on accountability of crimes against peacekeepers, adopted under Delhi’s presidency of the 15-nation body in August 2021, reflects the same conviction.

He further said that because India regards peacekeeping as “irreplaceable" to the UN’s core purpose, New Delhi has identified it as a priority for its candidacy for the Security Council term 2028-29 as a non-permanent member.
“We reaffirm our unwavering commitment to UN peacekeeping and to a peacekeeping architecture that is better resourced, better protected, and more representative of the world itself,” Mr. Singh said.
He also paid homage to the 184 Indian peacekeepers who have made the supreme sacrifice in their duty as Blue Helmets.

“India's commitment to this indispensable cause is not just philosophical; it is foundational, rooted in seven decades of operational engagement, and is shaped by the sweat and blood of our peacekeepers,” he said.

India is among the largest troop-contributing countries to UN peacekeeping, having deployed more than 3,00,000 troops across 50 missions to date

India has called for holding perpetrators of attacks against UN peacekeepers accountable, underlining that Blue Helmets face asymmetric and technologically enabled threats.

India is among the largest troop-contributing countries to UN peacekeeping , having deployed more than 3,00,000 troops across 50 missions to date.

“India upholds the safety and security of peacekeepers as one of the most important aspects of peacekeeping," Military Advisor at the Permanent Mission of India to the UN, Colonel Tarunendra Pratap Singh, said on Thursday (November 5, 2026).

"Personnel today face asymmetric and technologically-enabled threats, and those who attack peacekeepers must be held accountable,” Colonel Singh said while addressing the annual debate on comprehensive review of the whole question of peacekeeping operations in all their aspects.

He said India's continued leadership on UN Security Council resolution 2589 on accountability of crimes against peacekeepers, adopted under Delhi’s presidency of the 15-nation body in August 2021, reflects the same conviction.

He further said that because India regards peacekeeping as “irreplaceable" to the UN’s core purpose, New Delhi has identified it as a priority for its candidacy for the Security Council term 2028-29 as a non-permanent member.

“We reaffirm our unwavering commitment to UN peacekeeping and to a peacekeeping architecture that is better resourced, better protected, and more representative of the world itself,” Mr. Singh said.

He also paid homage to the 184 Indian peacekeepers who have made the supreme sacrifice in their duty as Blue Helmets.

“India's commitment to this indispensable cause is not just philosophical; it is foundational, rooted in seven decades of operational engagement, and is shaped by the sweat and blood of our peacekeepers,” he said.

Mr. Singh told the debate that peace operations are most likely to succeed when they are accompanied by a broader political process, with a clearly envisaged political outcome and commensurate resources for peacekeepers.

articles.title: Elephant calf with genetic bone disorder to be flown from Keralam to Gujarat’s Vantara for specialised treatment
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 18-month-old calf, which is unable to stand or walk, has been shifted from Kodanad elephant centre to a specially arranged animal ambulance with the help of a crane and 10-12 people, before being taken to Kochi airport for a chartered flight to Jamnagar, accompanied by veterinary experts, say officials

An 18-month-old elephant calf suffering from a genetic bone disorder and unable to stand or walk will be flown to Jamnagar in Gujarat on Friday (November 6, 2026) for specialised treatment at Vantara, the Kerala Forest Department said.
The calf, weighing around 125 to 130 kg, was shifted from its treatment facility at Kodanad elephant centre in Kochi to an animal ambulance with the help of 10 to 12 people and a crane.

The calf was subsequently loaded onto a specially arranged animal ambulance and taken to the Nedumbassery airport in Kochi, from where a chartered flight, accompanied by veterinary experts, was scheduled to depart for Jamnagar by noon, officials said.
Chief Wildlife Warden P. Pugazhendi told reporters that the calf had been brought to Kodanad soon after its birth and was being provided treatment there.
“Unfortunately, it fell once, following which we realised that it had certain genetic disorders. It was found to have osteopenia, a bone-related disorder,” he said.

Mr. Pugazhendi said Keralam did not have the facilities required to provide the calf with specialised treatment and the department had held discussions with experts, including veterinary specialists at Vantara.

“We are sending our calf to another State with great hope for specialised treatment. We are hopeful that it will recover and we will certainly bring it back to Keralam once it regains its health,” he said.
He said the initial treatment period was expected to last four to six months, depending on the calf’s progress.

A treatment plan involving hormonal therapy and hydrotherapy had been prepared by the specialists at Vantara, he said, adding that the outcome could not be predicted with certainty as the calf was suffering from a genetic disorder.
A team comprising a veterinary officer from Keralam, Forest department officials and the mahout who had cared for the calf since its early days would accompany it and assist in its treatment.

articles.title: VISTAR: India’s shift towards a real-time, technology-driven statistical system | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: For an economy aspiring to become a developed nation by 2047, the statistical blind spots could translate into costly policy mistakes, misdirected investments and ineffective welfare schemes

India’s statistical requirements have outgrown the conventional survey-based architecture, requiring a more scientific and technological architecture to better capture key performance indicators of economy, even as it should avoid the growing risks of synthetic data.

Seeking to move official data collection beyond periodic surveys and administrative records, the VISTAR or Viksit Bharat Initiative for Statistical Transformation, Analytics & Research is a major overhaul of India’s official statistical system at the centre and state levels using interoperable datasets, bridging data gaps and generating timely, reliable socioeconomic indicators for evidence-based policymaking.

articles.title: China's Macau jails ex-lawmaker in first national security trial
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Au Kam San, who co-organised annual vigils for victims of the 1989 Tiananmen Square crackdown in Beijing, is the first person convicted under national security laws widened in 2023 in Macau
A Court in the Chinese territory Macau sentenced on Friday (November 6, 2026), ex-lawmaker and democracy campaigner Au Kam San to 12 years and six months in prison for subversion and other offences.
Au, 69, is the first person convicted under national security laws widened in 2023 in Macau, the former Portuguese colony and casino hub which reverted to China in 1999.
He co-organised annual vigils for victims of the 1989 Tiananmen Square crackdown in Beijing, something previously tolerated only in Macau and neighbouring Hong Kong.

Au, detained in July 2025 and whose closed-door trial concluded in September in three days, was found guilty of "subversion against the political power of the State" among other offences, a Court statement said.

Au "personally provided, over a long period of time, assistance and collaboration to external hostile organisations in the collection, preparation, and public dissemination of various images and information that were manifestly filled with political claims of a subversive nature against the political authority of the State," it said.

He also sought to "incite hatred among Macau residents against the Central People's Government, with the intent to overthrow and undermine the fundamental system of the State enshrined in the Constitution of the People's Republic of China," it added.
The European Union last year condemned his arrest, saying it only heightened concerns about the "erosion of political pluralism" in Macau.
The organisation Justice Abroad said in July that Au's family, including his wife and three daughters, have not been permitted to see or speak with him since shortly after his detention.
The family received only one telephone call from him, lasting less than one minute, on the day after his arrest, Justice Abroad said.

"My father dedicated more than 30 years of his life serving the people of Macau. Nearly a year has passed, and we are still unable to communicate with him," his daughter was quoted as saying in the statement.

articles.title: US midterm election results 2026: Key Indian-origin winners
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Indian-Americans Nithya Raman won the Los Angeles mayoral race, while Vivek ‌Ramaswamy‌ was defeated in ⁠the ⁠race to become Ohio’s ‌next governor

Many Indian-origin candidates too notched up victories as Democrats captured majorities in both the Senate and House, sweeping victories that reached deep into Republican strongholds as tens of millions of voters delivered a scathing rebuke to ​President Donald Trump.

Indian-American candidates Suhas Subramanyam and Pia Dandiya won their seats in the US House of Representatives from Virginia and Florida, respectively. India-born Nithya Raman too has won the Los Angeles mayoral race. On the other hand, Republican ‌Vivek ‌Ramaswamy ‌was defeated in ⁠the ⁠race to become Ohio’s ‌next governor.

Kerala-born Nithya Raman has won the Los Angeles mayoral race, becoming the first Indian-American elected to lead the city, as incumbent Karen Bass conceded defeat and pledged a smooth transition. The most recent Los Angeles County electoral updates, refreshed at 4:34 pm local time, recorded Raman holding 460,772 ballots, equivalent to 52.70 per cent, compared with Bass’s 413,519 votes, representing 47.30 per cent.

Her lead expanded to 47,253 votes, marking a significant increase from the 34,654-vote advantage reported during the morning count, though these figures remain provisional while electoral staff continue processing votes cast on Tuesday.

Suhas Subramanyam, who served as an advisor to former president Barack Obama, has been re-elected as a member of the US House of Representatives. The 40-year-old won from Virginia’s 10th congressional district , polling over 61.5% of the vote against Republican Dave Beckwith, who managed to win 36.4 per cent of the ballots cast.

Ro Khanna has won re-election from California’s 17th Congressional District, located in the heart of Silicon Valley. The 50-year-old is completing his fifth term and will begin his sixth in January. Khanna was born in Philadelphia to a middle-class family. Both his parents immigrated to the United States from India in the 1970s.

Pramila Jayapal, who represents Washington’s 7th Congressional District, has secured a sixth term in the House of Representatives. Last month, her criticism of India’s Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls drew a public rebuke from India’s ambassador to the US. Jayapal, who was first elected to Congress in 2016, has been a prominent voice on immigration reform and healthcare issues.

A former high school principal, Pia Dandiya became the newest Indian-American to be elected to the US House , defeating Republican Casey Askar in Florida’s 22nd Congressional district. Dandiya bagged 51.9% of the votes, while her opponent Askar polled 49.1% of the votes.

Indian-American Democratic lawmaker Ami Bera has won the re-election to the U.S. House in California’s 3rd Congressional District, defeating Republican Robb Tucker. The 61-year-old won his eighth term in the US House of Representatives. Physician-turned-politician Amerish Babulal ‘Ami’ Bera is the longest-serving Indian American in the US Congress and is considered a strong voice on healthcare and diplomacy, as per PTI.
Amish Shah , an Indian-American physician, has been elected to the U.S. House of Representatives in Arizona’s First Congressional District.

🌐 International & Geopolitics 📅 06 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 4 Min Read

📰 US midterm election results 2026: Key Indian-origin winners

🎯 Exam Relevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy

Indian-Americans Nithya Raman won the Los Angeles mayoral race, while Vivek ‌Ramaswamy‌ was defeated in ⁠the ⁠race to become Ohio’s ‌next governor

Many Indian-origin candidates too notched up victories as Democrats captured majorities in both the Senate and House, sweeping victories that reached deep into Republican strongholds as tens of millions of voters delivered a scathing rebuke to ​President Donald Trump.

Indian-American candidates Suhas Subramanyam and Pia Dandiya won their seats in the US House of Representatives from Virginia and Florida, respectively. India-born Nithya Raman too has won the Los Angeles mayoral race. On the other hand, Republican ‌Vivek ‌Ramaswamy ‌was defeated in ⁠the ⁠race to become Ohio’s ‌next governor.

Kerala-born Nithya Raman has won the Los Angeles mayoral race, becoming the first Indian-American elected to lead the city, as incumbent Karen Bass conceded defeat and pledged a smooth transition. The most recent Los Angeles County electoral updates, refreshed at 4:34 pm local time, recorded Raman holding 460,772 ballots, equivalent to 52.70 per cent, compared with Bass’s 413,519 votes, representing 47.30 per cent.

Her lead expanded to 47,253 votes, marking a significant increase from the 34,654-vote advantage reported during the morning count, though these figures remain provisional while electoral staff continue processing votes cast on Tuesday.

Suhas Subramanyam, who served as an advisor to former president Barack Obama, has been re-elected as a member of the US House of Representatives. The 40-year-old won from Virginia’s 10th congressional district , polling over 61.5% of the vote against Republican Dave Beckwith, who managed to win 36.4 per cent of the ballots cast.

Ro Khanna has won re-election from California’s 17th Congressional District, located in the heart of Silicon Valley. The 50-year-old is completing his fifth term and will begin his sixth in January. Khanna was born in Philadelphia to a middle-class family. Both his parents immigrated to the United States from India in the 1970s.

Pramila Jayapal, who represents Washington’s 7th Congressional District, has secured a sixth term in the House of Representatives. Last month, her criticism of India’s Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls drew a public rebuke from India’s ambassador to the US. Jayapal, who was first elected to Congress in 2016, has been a prominent voice on immigration reform and healthcare issues.

A former high school principal, Pia Dandiya became the newest Indian-American to be elected to the US House , defeating Republican Casey Askar in Florida’s 22nd Congressional district. Dandiya bagged 51.9% of the votes, while her opponent Askar polled 49.1% of the votes.

Indian-American Democratic lawmaker Ami Bera has won the re-election to the U.S. House in California’s 3rd Congressional District, defeating Republican Robb Tucker. The 61-year-old won his eighth term in the US House of Representatives. Physician-turned-politician Amerish Babulal ‘Ami’ Bera is the longest-serving Indian American in the US Congress and is considered a strong voice on healthcare and diplomacy, as per PTI.

Amish Shah , an Indian-American physician, has been elected to the U.S. House of Representatives in Arizona’s First Congressional District.

articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Abdul El-Sayed’s describes himself as ‘just a capitalist who understands how capitalism works’ and identifies as a progressive; his candidacy was backed by leading figures such as Bernie Sanders and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez

In a country where, for more than a quarter of a century, the word “Muslim” has been used as an accusation in politics, Abdul El-Sayed’s election as the first Muslim member of the U.S. Senate breaks perhaps the thickest of glass ceilings in American public life. Dr. El-Sayed, a physician and epidemiologist, defeated the Republican former Congressman Mike Rogers with 52.5% of the vote, seven percentage points ahead of his rival.

It would be easy to dismiss this victory as merely a byproduct of the “blue wave” in the U.S. midterms, which carried Democratic candidates to wins even in Republican strongholds such as South Carolina, Texas, and Kansas. But that would be a reductive reading. The odds Dr. El-Sayed faced make the win remarkable in its own right.
Global & Diplomatic Brief: Abdul El-Sayed: The progressive’s progress. This development underscores India's strategic autonomy and pragmatic engagement in bilateral and multilateral diplomacy.

articles.title: Deepavali with pets: Why pet parents are choosing quieter holiday getaways
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: As fireworks unsettle dogs and cats, pet owners are trading noisy city celebrations for countryside retreats, pet hostels and quieter holidays

As Deepavali approaches, pets often become anxious at the sound of firecrackers. Dogs and cats may hide under beds or in dark corners, while some lose interest in playtime, walks and even pee breaks. For pet owners, finding ways to ease their distress is an ongoing challenge. Some who love celebrating Deepavali but cannot bear to see their pets shivering and panting are now choosing quieter destinations to spend the festival.
Frodo from Bengaluru | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

Pet parent JP Daisy boards her cat at a hostel in Hyderabad’s Kokapet with soundproof rooms during Deepavali. Watching her usually docile Siamese, Sharpay, run helter-skelter as firecracker noise peaks in the evening makes Daisy anxious. “She is a lightweight cat and usually eats very little. During Deepavali, she stops eating. One of our friends suggested a place to board her. Sharpay is not clingy, so boarding her is easy,” she says.

Pet boarding facilities also see a surge in demand during festivals, and not just from people travelling. With diyas lit in homes, unattended flames can pose a safety risk. At Pet Cafe Hyderabad, a boarding facility and restaurant in Banjara Hills, founder Deven Baheti says regulars book slots weeks, sometimes months, ahead of Deepavali.

“The open space and location make it comfortable for pets. Ours is a quiet locality, with few homes bursting firecrackers. To further drown out the noise, we play calming music, use vet-approved anti-anxiety drops and essential oils, and apply calming sprays to help them relax,” says Deven.

With boarding (charges of ₹1000 per day) slots fully booked, Deven and his team are preparing to keep the pets occupied with play and grooming sessions. “We do it for the love of animals. Even reactive pets are managed by a few of us and kept in separate enclosures, away from the friendly ones.”

Voicing use of vet-approved calming drops Bengaluru based Neeta Sharma said “That is the only way to calm our pet rescued Indie Frodo. The other two a labrador and a Beagle don’t care much about the sound.”
A boarder at Pet Cafe Hyd | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

Not all pet parents can board their pets, or are comfortable with the idea. Many instead look for pet-friendly homestays and resorts away from the city. With several properties now welcoming pets, finding the right one is the only challenge. In Chevella, about 50 kilometres from Hyderabad, homestays have become a welcome respite for pet owners. Ramya R, a pet parent, says the search for a suitable getaway begins soon after Ganesh Chaturthi. “The crackers on visarjan days are a reminder that we need to start looking.”

Pollam Gattu, a farmhouse in Chevella surrounded by carrot and flower fields, has become their regular Deepavali escape. The area sees fewer firecrackers than the city, making it a quieter retreat. “In villages, it is relatively quieter than in the city. I can’t say it is absolutely silent, but it is not as noisy with firecrackers as the city is,” she says.

With boarding (charges of ₹1000 per day) slots fully booked, Deven and his team are preparing to keep the pets occupied with play and grooming sessions. “We do it for the love of animals. Even reactive pets are managed by a few of us and kept in separate enclosures, away from the friendly ones.”

Voicing use of vet-approved calming drops Bengaluru based Neeta Sharma said “That is the only way to calm our pet rescued Indie Frodo. The other two a labrador and a Beagle don’t care much about the sound.”

A boarder at Pet Cafe Hyd | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

Not all pet parents can board their pets, or are comfortable with the idea. Many instead look for pet-friendly homestays and resorts away from the city. With several properties now welcoming pets, finding the right one is the only challenge. In Chevella, about 50 kilometres from Hyderabad, homestays have become a welcome respite for pet owners. Ramya R, a pet parent, says the search for a suitable getaway begins soon after Ganesh Chaturthi. “The crackers on visarjan days are a reminder that we need to start looking.”

Pollam Gattu, a farmhouse in Chevella surrounded by carrot and flower fields, has become their regular Deepavali escape. The area sees fewer firecrackers than the city, making it a quieter retreat. “In villages, it is relatively quieter than in the city. I can’t say it is absolutely silent, but it is not as noisy with firecrackers as the city is,” she says.

articles.title: Google sued over suicide-related AI chats on school computer
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The teenager was not able to access Google's Gemini app, nor OpenAI's ChatGPT, because they were blocked by her school
The parents of a 13-year-old girl have sued Google claiming she planned a potential suicide and funeral using its AI technology on a school-issued computer.

Filed Monday in a California court, the complaint is the first known case accusing Google of negligence related to AI integrations on Chromebooks, the tech giant's low-cost laptops used by millions of students in the United States and around the world.

The teenager was not able to access Google's Gemini app, nor OpenAI's ChatGPT, because they were blocked by her school. She was nonetheless still able to use Google's search engine, which contains AI-powered tools.
Those features were notably not among the tools that Google announced this week will be disabled by default for students.

"Schools should turn search off and keep it off until Google removes AI mode from search or ensures that every single student is always safe when they're interacting with AI," Andrew Liddell, one of the family's attorneys, told AFP on Thursday.
The complaint alleges that the child had been a "happy 13-year-old girl" in North Carolina who received great grades, played music and participated in Girl Scouts.

Despite "no history" of mental illness, within months of using Google's AI-powered search on her school laptop, she began a "quiet spiral into a severe psychological crisis" according to the complaint.
On March 17, the school's monitoring software flagged a document titled "Funeral," and the school notified her parents.
Her mother then saw the child writing a farewell letter in real-time after logging into her daughter's account, and her father intervened.
"We are reviewing the claims in the lawsuit and we take this very seriously," Google spokesperson Jose Castaneda told AFP.

articles.title: Air quality of Delhi worsens, many parts reel under ‘severe’ level air pollution
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Many parts of the national capital, including IIT Delhi, ITO, Dwarka, Rohini, Punjabi Bagh, Alipur, Bawana, and Jahangirpuri, witnessed “severe” level air pollution

The overall air quality of Delhi worsened and continued to be in the “very poor” category on Friday (November 6, 2026) morning, while many parts of the city reeled under “severe” level of air pollution, according to official data.
Many parts of the national capital, including IIT Delhi, ITO, Dwarka, Rohini, Punjabi Bagh, Alipur, Bawana, and Jahangirpuri, witnessed “severe” level air pollution.
Other cities and towns in north India, including Noida, Gurugram, and Faridabad also witnessed overall “very poor” air quality, on Friday (November 6, 2026) morning.
The 24-hour average Air Quality Index (AQI) of Delhi was 391 (very poor) at 9 a.m. on Friday, as per Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) data.
“Severe” level air pollution affects healthy people and seriously impacts those with existing diseases, as per the CPCB.
The overall air quality of Delhi is likely to be in the “severe” category for three days, as per the Central government’s ‘Air Quality Early Warning System for Delhi’.

The 24-hour average overall Air Quality Index (AQI) of Delhi stood at 369 (very poor) on Thursday at 4 p.m. on Thursday, slightly down from 377 (very poor) a day earlier, as per the Central Pollution Control Board’s daily bulletin, which is treated as the day’s AQI. A higher AQI means worsening of air quality.

Every winter, air pollution spikes in Delhi-NCR and many parts of the larger Indo-Gangetic Plains, mainly due to meteorological factors such as lower wind speeds and a drop in temperature. Also, pollution from stubble burning during October and November and bursting of firecrackers during the festive season add to existing pollution from vehicles and dust, worsening the air quality.

articles.title: Cancer care: Long battle for affordable treatment
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Advances in oncology have improved treatment options, but their benefits remain out of reach for many patients who cannot afford to complete the prescribed course. This is despite the recent decision to cap trade margins on 137 identified non-scheduled anti-cancer medicines, providing some relief, writes Afshan Yasmeen...

A 45-year-old garment factory worker from Bengaluru Rural diagnosed with stage IV-A cancer of the mouth faces an arduous course of treatment: chemotherapy to shrink the tumour, extensive surgery involving reconstruction, followed by radiation and chemotherapy. The cost of medicines and supportive drugs of around ₹93,000 alone, besides treatment costs, are staggering for her family with a modest monthly income of ₹28,000. With funds running out, she is facing the risk of discontinuing the final stages of treatment.

Likewise, a 56-year-old shopkeeper from Mysuru district, diagnosed with recurrent, inoperable hypopharyngeal cancer involving the oesophagus, has a different but equally difficult challenge. After three cycles of chemotherapy, the disease has shown partial response. Immunotherapy could offer another treatment option, but its cost remains prohibitive. Spending another ₹2.4 lakh to ₹8 lakh over the next 2 to 3 months for bi-weekly immunotherapy is virtually impossible on a ₹45,000/month income.
Science, Space & Environment Report: Cancer care: Long battle for affordable treatment. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

articles.title: No split in party, genuine issues will be addressed in steps: NC president Dr. Farooq Abdullah
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: ‘The baseless news of the National Conference (NC) splitting into groups is totally wrong. The party stands together. Those who think the party could be split: it was never, and it will never be split,’ says Dr. Farooq Abdullah

Ruling National Conference (NC) president Dr. Farooq Abdullah on Friday (November 6, 2026) ruled out any split in the party and assured a step-by-step approach to address the “genuine issues” raised by the 17 disgruntled legislators during a two-hour meeting with the top leadership in Srinagar.

“The baseless news of the National Conference (NC) splitting into groups is totally wrong. The party stands together. Those who think the party could be split: it was never, and it will never be split. We spoke to them [disgruntled legislators], and their issues were genuine. We heard all of them and assured them that some steps will be taken immediately and some slowly,” National Conference president Dr. Farooq Abdullah, after meeting disgruntled 17 party legislators in Srinagar.
Mr. Abdullah, who was accompanied by NC vice president Omar Abdullah and disgruntled leaders Mubarak Gul and Nazir Gurezi, said, “Our struggle for Statehood, Article 370 and 35A will continue.”

The meeting of the party in the wake of growing criticism from 17 legislators who held a separate meeting in Srinagar on October 27 and forwarded a joint resolution over a slew of issues, including removing CM Omar Abdullah’s adviser Nasir Aslam Wani and reassigning the portfolio of Roads and Buildings (R&B) currently with Deputy Chief Minister Surinder Choudhary.

The political upheaval was sparked hours after CM Abdullah expanded and reshuffled the Cabinet on October 27. Three senior leaders, Mr. Gul, Mr. Gurezi and Abdul Majeed Bhat Larmi showed heartburn publicly over not being inducted into the Cabinet.

“We have been raising issues with the party. We sat at a place recently, and the media blew it out of proportion and claimed a split [in the party]. There is no separate party. We placed the issues, both political and others, before the leadership, and there are assurances they will be addressed in step-by-step approach,” said Mr. Gurezi.

Earlier, a 10-point memorandum was submitted to the party leadership, which included a time-bound implementation of the election manifesto and an intensification of the struggle for the restoration of Statehood and special status. It also called for cabinet restructuring and ministerial accountability, and for the replacement of the Advisor. The memorandum also advocated a consultative advisory group of legislators and the constitution of a high-powered disciplinary committee.

‘The baseless news of the National Conference (NC) splitting into groups is totally wrong. The party stands together. Those who think the party could be split: it was never, and it will never be split,’ says Dr. Farooq Abdullah

Ruling National Conference (NC) president Dr. Farooq Abdullah on Friday (November 6, 2026) ruled out any split in the party and assured a step-by-step approach to address the “genuine issues” raised by the 17 disgruntled legislators during a two-hour meeting with the top leadership in Srinagar.

“The baseless news of the National Conference (NC) splitting into groups is totally wrong. The party stands together. Those who think the party could be split: it was never, and it will never be split. We spoke to them [disgruntled legislators], and their issues were genuine. We heard all of them and assured them that some steps will be taken immediately and some slowly,” National Conference president Dr. Farooq Abdullah, after meeting disgruntled 17 party legislators in Srinagar.

Mr. Abdullah, who was accompanied by NC vice president Omar Abdullah and disgruntled leaders Mubarak Gul and Nazir Gurezi, said, “Our struggle for Statehood, Article 370 and 35A will continue.”

The meeting of the party in the wake of growing criticism from 17 legislators who held a separate meeting in Srinagar on October 27 and forwarded a joint resolution over a slew of issues, including removing CM Omar Abdullah’s adviser Nasir Aslam Wani and reassigning the portfolio of Roads and Buildings (R&B) currently with Deputy Chief Minister Surinder Choudhary.

The political upheaval was sparked hours after CM Abdullah expanded and reshuffled the Cabinet on October 27. Three senior leaders, Mr. Gul, Mr. Gurezi and Abdul Majeed Bhat Larmi showed heartburn publicly over not being inducted into the Cabinet.

“We have been raising issues with the party. We sat at a place recently, and the media blew it out of proportion and claimed a split [in the party]. There is no separate party. We placed the issues, both political and others, before the leadership, and there are assurances they will be addressed in step-by-step approach,” said Mr. Gurezi.
