articles.title: Nedumbassery luxury car crash: Kerala HC grants bail to all four accused
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Justice Kauser Edappagath allows bail applications of four accused considering that all are in their early twenties, lack of criminal history, and the time already spent in custody
The Kerala High Court on Friday (November 6, 2026) granted bail to the four youths who were accused in the Nedumbassery luxury car accident that led to the death of three young two-wheeler riders.

Justice Kauser Edappagath allowed the bail applications of the four accused, considering that all accused were in their early twenties, the lack of criminal history, and the time already spent in custody. Suhail Sajeev, the first accused would be released on November 16, as the State had sought more time pertaining to the investigation. The other three would be released at the earliest.
The court held that it could not jump to the conclusion that the accused had prior knowledge of the alleged offences owing to mere alcohol consumption or speeding.

The accused had contended that as students, their continued detention would negatively affect their education and that they would fulfil any bail conditions necessary to ensure their continued cooperation.

Around 1.45 a.m. on October 11, the car driven by Sajeev crashed into a two-wheeler on Airport Road near Athani, claiming the lives of Gopika, Devika and Iyas. The other accused – Ninav, Joyal S. Anto and Ameen Shah – were in the car with Sajeev during the incident. All four were charged under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for rash and negligent driving, culpable homicide not amounting to murder, and abetment with a common intention.

articles.title: Kochi IT fraternity launches campaign for road safety as speeding bus kills colleague
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Fraternity of professionals based at Infopark, Kochi, have launched a multi-pronged campaign to ensure traffic safety in the vicinity of the campus following a recent accident in which a young IT professional was killed.

A digital signature campaign launched by Progressive Techies, a collective of IT professionals in the State, has already garnered over 4,000 signatures within a day. The group is also exploring legal remedies to address the frequent traffic woes in the area, which pose a serious safety threat to commuters and pedestrians alike.

The fresh round of campaigning was triggered by the death of Akshara A., 28, a senior consultant with EY. She was fatally knocked down by an allegedly speeding bus while walking home after a gym session at IMG Junction, Kakkanad, on Wednesday.
Employees of various companies held a candlelit vigil at Infopark on Thursday evening to honour Akshara’s memory.

“The major demand of our campaign is to evict encroachments along the stretch of road from IMG Junction to Infopark Road and make it safe for motorists and pedestrians. The stretch often remains so congested that there is not enough space for pedestrians. We are targeting at least 20,000 signatures for our campaign, and once we achieve this, we will forward our complaint to the authorities, including the District Collector, Chief Minister and Public Works Minister,” Anish Panthalani, co-founder of Progressive Techies, said.

He said the situation was similar on most of the arterial roads around Infopark, covering areas such as Pallikkara and Edachira, which are frequently used by tech professionals. “The possibility of filing a public interest litigation seeking a permanent solution is also being explored,” he said.
Mr. Panthalani said IT professionals had frequently met with accidents on roads around the tech campus due to various factors, including the stray dog menace.

The All India Professionals’ Congress (AIPC) Infopark chapter has also launched a campaign following Akshara’s death. The chapter will hold a ‘Listening Circle’ on the campus on Friday evening, allowing employees to share their traffic safety concerns.

“AIPC has brought the safety concerns to the attention of the Home Minister and Transport Minister and sought strict action against the erring driver in the fatal accident,” Eldho Chirackalchalil, district president of AIPC, said.

articles.title: Nithya Raman and her journey from Keralam to Los Angeles
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Nithya Raman defeated incumbent Mayor Karen Bass to take charge of the second most populous city in the U.S. after New York.

Nithya Raman, newly-elected Mayor of Los Angeles city in the U.S., has her roots in Keralam and a record of piloting effective civic activism in multiple Indian cities. Among the many Indian origin candidates making waves in this election season in the US, Ms. Raman defeated incumbent Mayor Karen Bass to take charge of the second most populous city in the U.S. after New York. The 45-year old is a member of the Democratic Socialists of America.

Born in Keralam, Nithya Raman spent the early years of her life between Thiruvananthapuram, her father Venkataraman’s native city, and Thrissur, her mother Sudha’s native place. Her father, who used to work for Keltron, and mother, a former employee of Indian Overseas Bank, migrated to the U.S. for better opportunities when Nithya was six years old.
She graduated in Social Studies from Harvard University in 2003, followed by a master’s degree in urban planning from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT).

Ms. Raman, who got her U.S. citizenship at the age of 22 later spent a few years in India, especially in Chennai, where she helmed Transparent Chennai which pushed the government to ensure better sanitation in slum areas through data-driven programmes. She was also part of protests against eviction of slum dwellers in Delhi.

After returning to the U.S. in 2013, she worked in the city administrative office as well as took part in activism to address homelessness. In 2019, she took the political plunge by announcing her candidacy to the Los Angeles City Council.

The grassroots campaign centering on homelessness and environmental issues, using a wide network of volunteers, paid off as she got elected to the City Council in 2020. Her Mayoral campaign focused on making more affordable homes in Los Angeles, improving city services and fixing Los Angeles’s movie business.

In a closely fought race for Los Angeles mayor, Ms Raman defeated incumbent ⁠Karen Bass. Ms Raman, a onetime ally of Bass, ‌stunned the political establishment in the second-largest US city when she challenged ‌the ⁠mayor. She is the first Los Angeles mayoral candidate to defeat ⁠an incumbent since 2005.

In a video statement thanking voters and campaign volunteers, Raman vowed to “build housing that people can afford, parks for ‌our children to play in, a transit system that can get people where they need to go, a city that is safe for its working people and its families.” The issue of homelessness played a major role in the campaign.

Democrats seized control of U.S. Congress after the midterm election on Tuesday (November 3, 2026), winning the Senate and House in a nationwide rebuke of President Donald Trump, likely limiting the rest of his term.

In a massive blue wave across the country, Trump’s Republican Party faced stunning defeats in its strongholds Texas, Georgia, Iowa and Ohio, where it lost the Governor’s posts to the Democrats. The Grand Old Party (GOP) also faced a drubbing in Senate races in Texas, Maine, South Carolina, North Carolina, Kansas, Iowa and Ohio, where Trump campaigned with a simple message, urging voters to pretend that he was on the ballot.

In a historic turn of events in U.S. political history, Texas Democrat James Talarico, a former teacher who ran on a “politics of love”, defeated Attorney General Ken Paxton to win a Senate seat—the first Democrat statewide winner since 1994. Separately, Democrat Gina Hinojosa defeated Republican Governor Greg Abbott, ending decades of Republican rule. Abdul El-Sayed defeated former Republican lawmaker Mike Rogers in Michigan to become the first Muslim elected to the upper chamber of Congress.

articles.title: Key federal panel approves Trump’s arch while it is being challenged in court
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The National Capital Planning Commission voted 8-4 to approve the 76-metre memorial arch near Washington, as three lawsuits challenge it and a judge is expected to rule soon on whether to block construction.
A federal judge late on Thursday (November 5, 2026) blocked the Trump administration from breaking ground on a towering memorial arch for 14 days.

The temporary restraining order by U.S. District Judge Tanya Chutkan, halting the work, represents a major setback for one of President Donald Trump’s most prominent projects in his vision to remake Washington.

The decision followed a series of steps taken earlier on Thursday by the government, including the final approval of the arch by the National Capital Planning Commission in an 8-4 vote after a hearing of nine and a half hours, where dozens of witnesses opposed the construction.

The administration said the work could begin as soon as the approval was in place, the Interior Department issued a final decision authorising construction and the National Park Service published the proper notification.
In issuing the temporary stop, Judge Chutkan said Virginia and the District of Columbia had shown that the immediacy of the construction would cause real harm to the plaintiffs.

“The harm is certain,” she wrote. “Defendants initially notified the court that construction could begin as early as November 5, 2026, if the NCPC approves the project at its meeting that day and the Department of the Interior authorizes construction.” In their filing, Virginia and the District of Columbia warned of traffic pattern distortions, as well as concerns about the impact on mutual aid emergency calls if the arch were to proceed.

“Second, the District and Virginia will incur significant unrecoverable costs. As soon as construction begins, DDOT [District Department of Transportation] will need to expend staff time and operating resources to affirmatively and proactively manage temporary detours, crashes or disabled vehicles,” Judge Chutkan wrote.

The judge’s decision came just over an hour after the commission’s hearing ended. The final vote came after nine and a half hours and scores of people opposing it. The vote broke along federal and local lines. Those in favour work for the administration or are connected to the President, who was pushing for the immediate construction. Opponents represented the city of Washington.
The panel’s Trump-appointed chairman launched the meeting with a gushing appraisal of the towering monument and lauded Mr. Trump for wanting to build it.

“President Trump understands as president and a superb builder that it’s important to our national identity to display who we are through grand monuments,” said Mark Paoletta, the commission’s chairman.

The decision followed a series of steps taken earlier on Thursday by the government, including the final approval of the arch by the National Capital Planning Commission in an 8-4 vote after a hearing of nine and a half hours, where dozens of witnesses opposed the construction.

The administration said the work could begin as soon as the approval was in place, the Interior Department issued a final decision authorising construction and the National Park Service published the proper notification.

In issuing the temporary stop, Judge Chutkan said Virginia and the District of Columbia had shown that the immediacy of the construction would cause real harm to the plaintiffs.

“The harm is certain,” she wrote. “Defendants initially notified the court that construction could begin as early as November 5, 2026, if the NCPC approves the project at its meeting that day and the Department of the Interior authorizes construction.” In their filing, Virginia and the District of Columbia warned of traffic pattern distortions, as well as concerns about the impact on mutual aid emergency calls if the arch were to proceed.

“Second, the District and Virginia will incur significant unrecoverable costs. As soon as construction begins, DDOT [District Department of Transportation] will need to expend staff time and operating resources to affirmatively and proactively manage temporary detours, crashes or disabled vehicles,” Judge Chutkan wrote.

The judge’s decision came just over an hour after the commission’s hearing ended. The final vote came after nine and a half hours and scores of people opposing it. The vote broke along federal and local lines. Those in favour work for the administration or are connected to the President, who was pushing for the immediate construction. Opponents represented the city of Washington.

The panel’s Trump-appointed chairman launched the meeting with a gushing appraisal of the towering monument and lauded Mr. Trump for wanting to build it.

“President Trump understands as president and a superb builder that it’s important to our national identity to display who we are through grand monuments,” said Mark Paoletta, the commission’s chairman.

Manuscripts of the epic Mahabharata, Kalhana’s 12th-century historical chronicle Rajatarangini, and Kautilya’s Arthashastra, a work on governance and statecraft, have been inscribed on UNESCO’s Memory of the World Asia-Pacific Regional Register, officials said on Thursday (November 5, 2026).
PIB Culture made the announcement on X and shared photos of UNESCO certificates.

“A moment of immense pride for India! The Rajatarangini, Mahabharata and Arthashastra have been inscribed in @UNESCO’s Memory of the World Asia-Pacific Regional Register, marking a historic milestone in the global recognition of India’s rich civilisational heritage!” it said.

The decision was taken at the 11th Session of the Memory of the World Asia-Pacific Regional Register held in Jakarta, Indonesia, the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA) said.

Union Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat hailed the inscriptions as a landmark recognition of India’s extraordinary documentary and civilisational heritage.

Under the visionary leadership of Hon’ble PM Shri @narendramodi Ji, India’s civilisational legacy is receiving unprecedented global recognition and its rightful place on the world stage,” the minister added.

With the recognition, India’s historical, literary, philosophical and political thought receives wider international acknowledgement, taking the country’s total number of inscriptions in the Regional Register to six, officials said.

articles.title: Trump to participate in Deepavali celebration at White House

fullParagraphs: The celebrations are scheduled to be held at the Oval Office, continuing a tradition started by President George W Bush
President Donald Trump will participate in a Deepavali celebration at the White House on Friday.
The celebrations are scheduled to be held at the Oval Office, continuing a tradition started by President George W Bush.
Earlier, the ceremonies were mostly held in the Eisenhower Executive Office Building in the presence of Indian-American community members and Indian diplomats.
In 2009, President Barack Obama became the first president to light a lamp (diya) at the White House, during a ceremony in the East Room.
Since then, lamp lighting ceremonies have been held in various locations in the White House, including the Oval Office and the Roosevelt Room.
Last year, India’s Ambassador to the U.S. Vinay Kwatra joined Mr. Trump in the Oval Office to celebrate Deepavali with the traditional lighting of the lamp.

articles.title: Indian NGO REACH receives Kochon Prize 2026
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Presented by the Kochon Foundation, an independent Korean non-profit foundation, in partnership with the Stop TB Partnership, the Kochon Prize recognises individuals and organisations that have made significant contributions to the fight against TB

Resource group for Education and Advocacy for Community Health (REACH), a not-for-profit organisation working to strengthen the tuberculosis (TB) response in India, has been awarded the Kochon Prize 2026, becoming the first civil society, non-profit organisation from India to receive this prestigious global recognition for its contributions to combating TB, a press release said.

Presented by the Kochon Foundation, an independent Korean non-profit foundation, in partnership with the Stop TB Partnership, the Kochon Prize recognises individuals and organisations that have made significant contributions to the fight against TB. The 2026 Kochon Prize is shared by REACH, the Centre for Health Solutions, Kenya, and the Marshall Islands TB Control Program. Previous winners from India include L.S. Chauhan (2006), head of the Revised National TB Control Programme, the Indian Council of Medical Research (2017) and Molbio Diagnostics (2024). The award was presented at the Stop TB Partnership Board Meeting held in Indonesia on November 5, 2026.

“Treat the person, not the disease - our journey with TB communities has been just that. We realised early on that overcoming barriers to care means addressing more than clinical needs - it means recognising social, community, family, mental health and situational challenges. That is the essence of integrated care: seeing the whole person, understanding their realities, and doing whatever it takes to ensure that no one is left behind,” said Nalini Krishnan, chairperson and co-founder, REACH.

“REACH is a remarkable and rare organisation that has been consistently ahead of the curve in terms of public health action, and particularly in the field of TB. A women-led organisation, they genuinely care about the people they’re supporting, beyond the numbers, data and reports to donor. However, they combine this with a robust scientific and technical approach and a shrewd understanding of the public health landscape in the country,” said Soumya Swaminathan, chairperson, M. S. Swaminathan Research Foundation and former chief scientist, WHO, who nominated REACH for the award.

“This recognition is testimony to the dedication of the community health workers, TB Nanbans and TB Champions who work alongside us, and to the families affected by TB and non-communicable diseases (NCDs) who have placed their trust in us. We are deeply grateful to their unwavering commitment and fortitude, and are energised to do more to help facilitate equitable access to health,” said Ramya Ananthakrishnan, director, REACH.

articles.title: Documentary highlights role of family physicians in strengthening primary healthcare
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The documentary intends to initiate wider conversations on reviving primary healthcare networks in urban and rural communities, and recognising neighbourhood doctors as an integral part of the healthcare system

The role of family physicians in ensuring accessible, affordable and patient-centred healthcare came into focus at the premiere of the documentary The Doctor Next Door: A Legacy of Care , screened at the Indian Heritage Academy in Bengaluru earlier this week.

Through accounts of veteran physicians, patients and young medical professionals, the film examines the decline of neighbourhood family practices and the growing fragmentation of healthcare. It highlights how long-standing doctor-patient relationships, built on trust, familiarity and personal attention, remain central to effective primary care.

The documentary draws attention to the rising dependence on specialised and corporate hospital-based treatment, making a case for strengthening family medicine as the foundation of India’s healthcare system.

Swetha Reddy Pitchela, project manager for the documentary, said the film features perspectives from young medical students and practitioners considering careers in general practice, highlighting the need for changes in medical education and healthcare policy to encourage family medicine.

Directed by Ganesh Shankar Raj of Mindia Films and produced in collaboration with the Academy of Family Physicians of India (AFPI), the non-profit documentary explores the enduring relationship between family doctors and patients and the importance of continuity of care in an increasingly specialised healthcare system.

The screening was followed by a panel discussion featuring scientists, medical professionals, senior family physicians and community health advocates. The discussion centred on the challenges facing primary healthcare, the need to strengthen family medicine, and the importance of human relationships in medical practice.
Veteran family physician B.C. Rao was among the contributors to the initiative, alongside representatives of AFPI and other healthcare professionals.

The organisers said the documentary was intended to initiate wider conversations on reviving primary healthcare networks in urban and rural communities and recognising neighbourhood doctors as an integral part of the healthcare system.

articles.title: We lost the elections to the Supreme Court, not to the BJP: Mamata-Trinamool’s Abhishek Banerjee
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: “Let the government of India or ECI take suo motu cognisance and file a case against me. I will represent myself and fight it at the Supreme Court,” Mr. Banerjee said.

Diamond Harbour MP and Mamata All India Trinamool Congress leader Abhishek Banerjee on Thursday (November 5, 2026) claimed that his party lost the 2026 West Bengal Assembly elections to the Supreme Court of India and not to the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

“I have no qualms in saying this that we lost the Bengal elections to the Supreme Court of India and not to the BJP because we took a leap of faith on the highest court of the country,” Mr. Banerjee said on Thursday (November 6, 2026) evening.

The Mamata AITC leader said that the Supreme Court had assured that names will be included in the voter list three days before polling which was not allowed and randomisation of counting staff was not followed by (Chief Electoral Officer) Manoj Agarwal. “Let the government of India or ECI take suo motu cognisance and file a case against me. I will represent myself and fight it at the Supreme Court,” Mr. Banerjee said.

The remarks by the Mamata AITC leader come at a time when protests are raging across the country over allegations of “vote-theft” and demands of scrapping Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. In West Bengal 91 lakh electors were removed from the voter list during SIR which preceeded before assembly polls . Mamata Banerjee and her party had challenged SIR before the Supreme Court and Ms. Banerjee had also appeared in person before the Supreme Court. In the Assembly polls, the BJP came to power winning 207 of the 294 seats in the West Bengal Legislative Assembly.

Abhishek Banerjee also made allegations that the police are threatening the accused in police custody with an encounter. Mr. Banerjee’s personal assistant Sumit Roy is in police custody and the Trinamool leader has been named as accused in more than 20 FIRs since the Bharatiya Janata Party government came to power in May 2026.

The remarks come after Mamata AITC leadership has also raised allegations of planted evidence at their vacated party office after ₹1 crore cash was recovered from the premises. The party office in question is a part of Mr. Banerjee’s constituency Diamond Harbour. Abhishek Banerjee alleged that his personal assistant Sumit Roy was being pressurised and forced under threat to testify about the recovered cash.
“Money was brought between 1 a.m. and 3 a.m. in the night from the Black XUV that Diamond Harbour SP uses,” Mr. Banerjee alleged.

articles.title: 10 smaller Gulf carriers denied airport slots at Mumbai
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The development comes as Mumbai airport plans to suspend flights to 14 international destinations, which will be served from Navi Mumbai.

Atleast 10 smaller Gulf carriers have had their requests for slots at Mumbai airport rejected, with the Adani-operated airport requiring airlines to shift to Navi Mumbai on the pretext of renovation work, according to airline sources.

The airlines include Oman Air, Bahrain’s Gulf Air, Sharjah-based Air Arabia, Kuwait Airways and Jazeera Airways from Kuwait, Doha-based Qatar Airways, and four carriers from Saudi Arabia — Flyadeal, Flynas, Riyadh Air and Saudia — it is reliably learnt.

This comes as Mumbai airport plans to suspend flights to 14 international destinations, which will be served from Navi Mumbai. The destinations are Bahrain, Dammam, Dhaka, Doha, Fujairah, Jakarta, Jeddah, Kathmandu, Kuwait City, Madinah, Muscat, Ras Al Khaimah, Riyadh and Sharjah.
Shift to Navi Mumbai or stop flying to Mumbai: Adani Airports CEO tells foreign airlines
Foreign airlines grouping urges for alternatives to flight cuts at Mumbai airport
Centre intervenes to buy airlines more time at Adani’s Mumbai airport

A representative of an airline denied slots for some flights at Mumbai said the carrier had protested and asked the airport to reconsider, questioning how a low-cost carrier could split its operations between the two airports. The representative raised concerns about staffing, ground handling and cargo, as well as the airline’s catchment market, and called for a gradual, phased shift. The representative said the airport had taken a hardline approach and could have been more “congenial rather than thrust the decision upon us”.

The dispute stems from Mumbai International Airport Ltd’s plan to redevelop Terminal 1 and shift some of its domestic operations to Terminal 2. To make room, the airport operator proposed reducing international operations at Terminal 2, with some flights expected to move to Navi Mumbai International Airport. articles.title: Supreme Court terms vehicular emissions major contributor to air pollution in Delhi-NCR
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Bench highlighted the large number of vehicles plying on roads connecting Delhi with neighbouring areas, including Ghaziabad, Greater Noida, Gurugram and Faridabad

The Supreme Court on Friday (November 6, 2026) termed vehicular emissions a major contributor to air pollution in Delhi-NCR and said immediate, medium- and long-term measures were needed to curb the rising air quality index.

Hearing a suo motu case examining the regulatory framework governing air pollution, a Bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana also expressed concern over “bumper-to-bumper” traffic in Delhi-NCR.
“We keep talking and sometimes make statements and suggestions, but the point is that AQI is already touching 400,” the CJI said.
The Bench highlighted the large number of vehicles plying on roads connecting Delhi with neighbouring areas, including Ghaziabad, Greater Noida, Gurugram and Faridabad.
“Look at the roads in Delhi and the roads connecting Delhi with the NCR. Take a look at any road and the kind of vehicles moving on it. That is the major problem,” the CJI said.
The Bench said the poor people are the real sufferers, as they are on the roads, and moreover, the festival time is the only period when they earn a livelihood.

articles.title: UPSC Mains Result 2026 declared: Here’s how to check
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Civil Services exam is conducted annually in three stages - preliminary, main, and interview - to select candidates for the Indian Administrative Services (IAS), Indian Foreign Service (IFS), and Indian Police Service (IPS) and other services.

The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) has declared the results of the Civil Services (Main) Examination 2026, on November 5, 2026, with successful candidates qualifying for the personality test of the highly coveted examination.

The civil services exam is conducted annually in three stages — preliminary, main, and interview — to select candidates for the Indian Administrative Services (IAS), Indian Foreign Service (IFS), and Indian Police Service (IPS) and other services.
Long UPSC prep cycles take heavy toll on aspirants’ mental health
Candidates can follow these steps to check their UPSC results

A candidate who clears the written examination (Main) will proceed to the personality test, also referred to as the UPSC interview. The interview carries 275 marks, while the written Mains examination carries 1,750 marks. The final merit list is prepared using the combined scores of both the main and interview stages of the UPSC examination.
Candidates who qualify for the Mains examination will receive e-summon letters of personality tests (Interviews), which can be downloaded from the commission’s website.
Candidates who may not be able to download their e-Summon letters, should immediately contact the office of the Commission through letter or through the following means
No paper/physical summon letters will be issued for the personality tests (interviews) by the commission.

Dates of personality tests (interviews) of the candidates will be notified in due course, as per the official communication. The interviews will be held at the Office of the Union Public Service Commission at Dholpur House, Shahjahan Road, New Delhi.

articles.title: Five acquitted in 2013 Muzaffarnagar riots case over mosque arson, vandalism
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: According to Mr. Sharma, the Special Investigation Team (SIT) had filed a chargesheet against the five accused after investigating an incident that took place on September 8, 2013, in Muthbhar village under the Bhorakala police station limits

A local court has acquitted five people in a 13-year-old case related to the vandalism and arson at a mosque and a house during the 2013 Muzaffarnagar riots , citing lack of evidence, a case lawyer said on Friday (November 6, 2026).

Additional District and Sessions Judge Vijay Kumar acquitted Anuj, Arvind, Nitu, Ankit and Ramkumar on Thursday (November 5), observing that the prosecution had failed to prove the charges against them, government counsel Narendra Sharma said.

According to Mr. Sharma, the Special Investigation Team (SIT) had filed a chargesheet against the five accused after investigating an incident that took place on September 8, 2013, in Muthbhar village under the Bhorakala police station limits.
The accused were charged with vandalising and setting a mosque on fire, besides looting around ₹1 lakh in cash collected at the religious place during the riots.

According to the complaint lodged by the victim, Shahbuddin, more than 50 people had allegedly vandalised the mosque and set it ablaze. They also allegedly looted cash from the mosque, ransacked his house, and set it on fire.
The SIT subsequently filed a chargesheet against five people in connection with the incident.

articles.title: T.N. government constitutes Tamil Nadu Investment Promotion Commission
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Chief Secretary will be the chairperson of the Commission while the Secretary, Industries, Investment Promotion and Commerce will be the member-convener.

The Tamil Nadu government has issued an order constituting a 20-member Tamil Nadu Investment Promotion Commission headed by Chief Secretary with an objective to facilitate and promote investments linked to Free Trade Agreements, investments by persons of Tamil origin outside India and such other investments.
According to a Government Order, the Chief Secretary will be the chairperson of the Commission while the Secretary, Industries, Investment Promotion and Commerce will be the member-convener.

Secretaries to various departments such as Municipal Administration and Water Supply; Home, Prohibition and Excise; Artificial Intelligence, Information Technology and Digital Services; Environment, Climate Change and Forests; Finance, Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises; Housing and Urban Development; Natural Resources; Rural Development and Panchayat Raj; Energy; Labour Welfare and Skill Development; Revenue and Disaster Management; Commercial Taxes and Registration; and Water Resources will be the ex-officio members.

Apart from them, the Commissioner of Land Reforms, Commissioner of Land Administration, the Member-Secretary of Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board, and Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Guidance Tamil Nadu will also be ex-officio members of the Commission.

The order said the goal of the State government was to transform Tamil Nadu into a $1.5 trillion economy by 2036 and achieving this objective will require not only attracting investment commitments, but also ensuring their timely conversion into grounded projects, commercial operations and employment opportunities within predictable timelines.

The constitution of Tamil Nadu Investment Promotion Commission was announced by the newly formed TVK-led government during the inaugural address of the Governor to the Legislative Assembly on June 18, 2026.

Following this, the State government, during the Budget session of the Tamil Nadu Assembly introduced an amendment to the Tamil Nadu Business Facilitation Act, 2018, to strengthen the institutional framework for promoting ease of doing business in Tamil Nadu and constitute the Tamil Nadu Investment Promotion Commission to facilitate, coordinate, and monitor high-value and strategic investments. The Bill was later passed.
The Amended Act reduced the time limit for obtaining clearances under 22 State Acts and other subordinate legislations to 21 days, excluding public and local holidays, to promote investments.

The Commission would review the pipeline and progress of large, strategic, and high-impact investments involving proposed capital investments of ₹200 crore or more, investments expected to generate employment for 5,000 persons or more, investments linked to Free Trade Agreements, investments by persons of Tamil origin outside India, and other investments specified by the government.

The Commission would function as a dedicated high-level body to advise, oversee, and review all investment promotion and facilitation activities, the grounding of projects, employment generation, and promotion of exports in the State. It would review the progress of investments up to the stage of grounding and commencement of operation and to issue directions to the competent authorities, departments concerned, or nodal agencies for timely grant of clearances, incentives, and other prerequisite approvals. The directions of the Commission would be binding.

articles.title: JSP keen on Deputy Mayor post of Vizianagaram city
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Despite stiff TDP competition, JSP hopes to win the coveted post for backing a major alliance partner. According to sources, BJP, which won three divisions, is also in the race
The Jana Sena Party is keen to obtain the Deputy Mayor post of the Vizianagaram Municipal Corporation after winning six of the ten contested segments in the city.

In spite of the tough competition within the TDP, JSP is hopeful of securing the coveted post as a reward for its support of a major alliance partner. According to sources, the BJP, which won three divisions, is also in the race for the post.

articles.title: Form 8 must be decided during SIR; deletion without hearing denies vote: Bombay HC
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Bench also ordered the Election Commission of India to restore the six names, and to set aside the rejection of their Form 8 applications
The Goa bench of The Bombay High Court held that removal of an elector’s name from the roll without a hearing denies the citizen the right to vote.

The Bench delivered the judgment on a petition by six members of the Salgaonkar family that an Electoral Registration Officer must decide a Form 8 application while Special Intensive Revision is underway. The Bench also ordered the Election Commission of India to restore the six names, and to set aside the rejection of their Form 8 applications.

The judgment, delivered by a Bench of Justice Valmiki Menezes and Justice Amit Jamsandekar, records that Section 22 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 and Rule 13 of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 continue to operate during a revision, whether Intensive or Summary, and that an ERO who receives Form 8 is bound to decide the application rather than refuse it because the revision is underway. The Bench rejected the contention of the ECI that an ERO may refuse Form 8 while revision is underway.

The Bench cited Rule 21A of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 and said that the Rule reflects the proviso to Section 22 of the Act, which requires an ERO to give a person whose name is on the roll and is required to be deleted, an opportunity to show cause before deletion. The Court added that an ERO must make an endeavour to give a voter who does not reside in the constituency an opportunity to show cause why the action proposed should not be taken.

The Court examined Sections 22 and 23 of the Act with Rules 13 and 25 of the Rules and drew a line between Form 6 and Form 8 by holding that Form 6 is for a person who seeks inclusion for the first time and requires a declaration that the name is not on any Assembly or Parliamentary roll, while Form 8 is for a voter on the roll who seeks shift of residence or correction of entries, so a voter who shifts within the constituency can file only Form 8 and cannot be directed to file Form 6 during SIR .

The Bench held that a direction to file Form 6 would require the voter to declare that the name was not on a roll and that the application was for inclusion for the first time, which would conflict with the record and expose the applicant to Section 31 of the Act. It also held that removal of a name from the roll after revision, and without a hearing, when the elector has submitted Form 8 for shift of residence within that constituency, denies the right to vote.

The petitioners had their names on the electoral roll in Part 29 of the Santa Cruz constituency in Goa since 1995 and moved to Part 25 before the SIR began in November 2025. When a Booth Level Officer visited the address on the roll the landlord said they had moved, after which the petitioners approached the BLO at the address to which they moved on November 12, 2025 and were directed to submit Form 8.

The BLO uploaded Form 8 on December 8, 2025, verification took place, and the ECI told the petitioners that the verification report had been submitted and the applications forwarded to the ERO, but when the roll was published on December 16, 2025 the names were absent from Part 29 and Part 25. Subsequently, on January 21, 2026 the ERO rejected Form 8 and told them the EPIC numbers had been deleted and that they should submit Form 6.

The petitioners challenged the rejection before the District Election Officer and the Chief Electoral Officer, both of whom upheld it, and they then moved the High Court contending that rejection of Form 8 was not in accordance with the Act and the Rules and that the names had been deleted without notice or hearing.
Mumbai / Goa / Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls

articles.title: From fictitious Chief Minister to Naladiyar as ‘poet’: Tamil writer Perumal Murugan flags ‘literary scam’ in Periyar Arivulagam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Rajmohan, State Minister for Tamil Development, Information and Publicity, said an inquiry would be initiated immediately into the alleged scam in procurement of books at the newly inaugurated library and science centre in Tamil Nadu’s Coimbatore.

Who was the first Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, then known as Premier of the Madras Province, in 1947, the year India attained Independence? According to a book titled Tamil Nadu Oru Paarvai , it was Muthuvelu Subbaiah Iyer, an unheard of personality.

The book, authored by Dhanalakshmi Arjun, is among the titles now on the shelves of Periyar Arivulagam, a dream project of the erstwhile DMK government , inaugurated recently in Coimbatore by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay .
Tamil Nadu CM Vijay inaugurates ₹301.71-crore Periyar Arivulagam in Coimbatore
Periyar Arivulagam books row: People of Tamil Nadu will never forgive DMK for corruption, says CM Vijay
Award-winning Tamil writer Perumal Murugan , who visited the library and browsed through its collection, has flagged what he says are serious irregularities in the purchase of books.

The book states: “Muthuvelu Subbaiah Iyer made a great impact on the principal leadership and the Assembly. Subsequently, Mu. Ka. Ramasamy, an important figure in Dravidian Kizhakku Arasiyal, emerged as a prominent political leader. Later, Kamaraj took over from him (1954–1963)” (page 108).
Periyar Arivulagam at Gandhipuram in Coimbatore. File | Photo Credit: S. Siva Saravanan

Mr. Perumal Murugan, who wrote a lengthy article — Periyar Arivulagathil Periya Oozhal (Major Scam in Periyar Arivulagam)— in the online portal Sindhai detailing his observations, said he did not know when the books had been purchased. “It is for the government to come out with a clarification,” he told The Hindu on Friday (November 6, 2026).
School Education Minister Rajmohan, who is also in charge of Tamil Development, Information and Publicity, said an inquiry would be initiated immediately.

“There is a scam. I can forgive anything. But a scam in a library bearing the name of Periyar is unacceptable. To borrow the words of my leader and Chief Minister, we will not spare anyone,” he said while participating in a government function at Chennai.

Rajmohan, State Minister for Tamil Development, Information and Publicity, said an inquiry would be initiated immediately into the alleged scam in procurement of books at the newly inaugurated library and science centre in Tamil Nadu’s Coimbatore.

Who was the first Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, then known as Premier of the Madras Province, in 1947, the year India attained Independence? According to a book titled Tamil Nadu Oru Paarvai , it was Muthuvelu Subbaiah Iyer, an unheard of personality.

Award-winning Tamil writer Perumal Murugan , who visited the library and browsed through its collection, has flagged what he says are serious irregularities in the purchase of books.

The book states: “Muthuvelu Subbaiah Iyer made a great impact on the principal leadership and the Assembly. Subsequently, Mu. Ka. Ramasamy, an important figure in Dravidian Kizhakku Arasiyal, emerged as a prominent political leader. Later, Kamaraj took over from him (1954–1963)” (page 108).

Periyar Arivulagam at Gandhipuram in Coimbatore. File | Photo Credit: S. Siva Saravanan

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The court has ordered the reinstatement of the candidates selected under advertisement number 10/2023, directing that their service be treated as continuous, without any interruption.
The Jharkhand High Court on Friday (November 6, 2026) quashed State government decision to cancel the Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission Combined Graduate Level (JSSC-CGL) exam.

A single-Judge bench of Justice Deepak Roshan, set aside the State government’s decision to cancel the appointments made under the JSSC-CGL examination. The court has also ordered the reinstatement of the candidates selected under advertisement number 10/2023, directing that their service be treated as continuous, without any interruption.

Based on the Jharkhand State Crime Investigation Department (CID) investigation report and widespread protests by candidates, the State government had decided to cancel the examination process and the appointments made based on it on August 17, 2026.

The decision was made public through a notification issued late in the evening on August 18, 2026. On the same day, the Hemant Soren cabinet decided to cancel a total of 22 examinations, including the 11th to 13th Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC), Child Development Programme Officer (CDPO), and JSSC-CGL exams.

Additionally, six other examinations were postponed. The investigation into these examinations was handed over to the CID. Furthermore, it was decided that 17 other examinations would also be investigated by the CID.
The court directed that that candidates will not be deprived of any other service benefits due to the notification cancelling the recruitment.

“It is not impossible to identify the suspect and guilty candidates in this matter. Therefore, instead of cancelling the entire examination and the appointments made on its basis, those involved in the irregularities can be identified through an investigation,”the court observed.
The court also pointed out that the State government failed to present any concrete, fact-based inquiry or evidence to prove that the entire selection process was marred by systematic irregularities.
“The appointments of all selected candidates cannot be terminated merely on the grounds that allegations exist or investigations are pending against a few individual candidates,” the court said.

Advocate Amritansh Vats, representing the petitioners that court also refereed to earlier orders passed by the High Court and the Supreme Court, the court stated that the State government cannot take action contrary to those judicial directives

articles.title: Profit-sharing formula in sugarcane pricing introduced in Belagavi district of Karnataka farmers
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: This initiative succeeded in breaking the deadlock between sugarcane farmers and factories, allowing commencement of operations in sugar factories
The Belagavi district administration managed to introduce a profit-sharing formula in the pricing of sugarcane for this crushing season. Most farmers’ leaders welcomed the formula.
This has succeeded in breaking the deadlock between sugarcane farmers and factories , allowing commencement of operations in sugar factories.

District In-charge minister Satish Jarkiholi has claimed that this was the first in the country where the profit sharing formula was introduced according to the C Rangarajan committee recommendations.

Most of the farmers leaders have accepted this formula and suspended their protest . On Friday, eight out of the 29 factories in Belagavi district issued notices, saying they were starting crushing operations and would abide by the formula.

Some leaders, like Shashikant Padasalagi Guruji have expressed their displeasure at the formula, saying it was speculative and dependent heavily on the union government’s efforts at revising the Minimum Selling Price of sugar.

The agreement was hammered out between Satish Jarkiholi, former minister Shashikant Nayak, Rahul Shindhe, in charge Deputy Commissioner, sugar factory representatives and some farmers leaders. The minister clarified that the issues of Minimum Selling Price of sugar, Fair and Remunerative Price of sugarcane and the State Advised Price to be decided by the state government were all issues that could be discussed at a later date.

The formula is based on the understanding that farmers are both raw material suppliers and share holders of factories. It involves an agreement that farmers will be paid a base price, that is above the Fair and Remunerative Price fixed by the union government and an additional amount that is given out as profit. It is not mandatory and could be irregular.
The profits will be calculated in such a way that 75 percent shall go to farmers and 25 percent to the factory.
Mr Shindhe said that the ₹ 3650 per tonne offered by the factories as the base price, was around ₹ 350 higher than the prices paid last year.

The details regarding the sugarcane payment are as follows: According to the agreement, ₹3,500 per tonne will be paid as the first instalment. Once the crushing season concludes, an additional ₹100 will be provided as a second instalment.

articles.title: Periyar Arivulagam books row: People of Tamil Nadu will never forgive DMK for corruption, says CM Vijay
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: “For those familiar with the DMK’s history, this is hardly shocking. However, what makes us deeply distressed is that all this involves public money,” Mr. Vijay said in a social media post after renowned writer Perumal Murugan flagged irregularities in the procurement of books for Periyar Arivulagam in Coimbatore.

Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam president and Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on Friday (November 6, 2026) said the people of Tamil Nadu would never forgive the DMK, which had made a history of “looting and indulging in corruption” in the name of Periyar E.V. Ramasamy and Tamil.

Coming down heavily on the DMK following serious irregularities surfacing in the purchase of books for the newly inaugurated Periyar Arivulagam in Coimbatore , Mr. Vijay, in a post on X, alleged “The DMK, the root cause of corruption, has now been exposed as an example of how those who loudly proclaim that they alone represent Tamil and deceive the people have always been corrupt.”
From fictitious Chief Minister to Naladiyar as ‘poet’: Tamil writer Perumal Murugan flags ‘literary scam’ in Periyar Arivulagam
DMK chief Stalin visits Periyar Arivulagam in Coimbatore

A book recommendation committee was constituted for the Periyar Arivulagam and other new libraries, and a Government Order was issued on November 5, 2025 during the previous DMK regime, Mr. Vijay said.

He hailed author Perumal Murugan, who was a member of the committee tasked with recommending modern literary works and books on literary criticism, for flagging the irregularities in the procurement of books for the Periyar Arivulagam.

“The DMK has resorted to corruption in a somewhat different way, turning the Periyar Arivulagam in Coimbatore itself into a world of corruption. The DMK leadership, which had repeatedly boasted that it had meticulously built the Periyar Arivulagam, has now been exposed for recommending substandard books and indulging in corruption in their procurement. The entire world is watching and laughing at this,” Mr. Vijay said.

“How many instances of corruption took place during the previous DMK regime? Corruption in the Municipal Administration Department , TASMAC , tenders. The DMK created a world of corruption for itself, with corruption in every department, and one after another is now coming to light,” he alleged.

“Among these, it is widely known that corruption also took place in the School Education department, which is concerned with the welfare of our children, and those involved were arrested . But now, is there corruption even in the library built as a knowledge centre for our children and students to use?” he asked.

“For those familiar with the DMK’s history, this is hardly shocking. However, what makes us deeply distressed is that all this involves public money,” Mr. Vijay said, accusing the DMK of being involved in corruption that directly affects people’s lives.

fullParagraphs: Just a day after a blue wave swept across the U.S. in midterms election shaking President Donald Trump’s administration, the fall of Santiago Pena carries significance beyond the borders of the country of seven million people

On Wednesday (November 4, 2026), rising tensions in Asuncion, the capital of Paraguay, turned violent as hundreds of thousands stormed the streets to protest locking out of their accounts in the country’s biggest bank. As fires burned and people anxiously queued outside the collapsed bank, President Santiago Pena, a former shareholder in the bank, announced his resignation.

But as Congress moved to impeach him, Mr. Pena disappeared amid rumours that he had fled to Argentina — just as Brazilian far-right leader Flávio Bolsonaro did last week before fleeing to U.S. after losing the election to President Lula da Silva. “We have information that he left the country without telling anyone. I think he went to Argentina and sought asylum,” said Paraguayan Senator Antonio Velázquez on Thursday (November 5, 2026).

Global & Diplomatic Brief: After Donald Trump’s midterm poll rout, South America breathes easy as far-right feels the heat. This development underscores India's strategic autonomy and pragmatic engagement in bilateral and multilateral diplomacy.

articles.title: Swift grievance redressal system for entrepreneurs and investors put in place on K-SWIFT portal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Every query or grievance registered through the system will be automatically routed to the department and officer concerned.

A ticket-based query and grievance redressal system has been put in place under the ‘Invest Kerala Helpdesk’ on the K-SWIFT Portal as the centralised mechanism for the registration, tracking, escalation and resolution of queries, complaints and grievances raised by entrepreneurs and investors. Every query or grievance registered through the system will be automatically routed to the department and officer concerned.

The helpdesk, implemented by the Kerala State Industrial Development Corporation (KSIDC), will serve as the single point of intake for all queries and grievances relating to the single window system. The government has mandated that the high priority queries and grievances have to be addressed by the respective departments within three days, while the medium ones need to be addressed in five days and low priority grievances within seven days.

Any ticket, especially department or service-level grievances remaining unresolved beyond the applicable timelines shall be automatically escalated to the Managing Director, KSIDC, and thereafter to the Secretary (Industries), who will be the final escalation authority.

As per the single window guidebook approved by the government, no department or agency processing an application through K-SWIFT can mark an application as ‘rejected’, unless the reason for rejection, detailed rejection remarks, the legal or procedural basis for rejection, details of missing or deficient documents are recorded in the system, along with the name, designation, date and time of the officer rejecting the application.

Applicants can file an appeal through K-SWIFT against an eligible rejected application, along with the relevant application and rejection details, grounds of appeal and supporting documents. Every department and agency integrated with K-SWIFT will designate an officer as the Appellate Authority for applications relating to the services under its jurisdiction.

articles.title: Punjab farm fire cases reach 2,787, with 586 incidents from Tarn Taran
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: So far, the authorities have imposed fines totalling more than ₹46 lakh as environmental compensation in 914 cases of stubble burning, with more than ₹24 lakh already recovered

“The number of farm fire incidents in Punjab between September 15 and November 5, 2026 this year has reached 2,787, with Tarn Taran recording 586 cases and Ferozepur 361,” official data said on Friday (November 6, 2026).

On November 4, 2026, stubble burning cases stood at 2,347, the data showed. Till Thursday (November 5, 2026), there were 221 farm fire incidents in Amritsar, 216 in Bathinda, 240 in Sangrur and 156 in Patiala.

So far, the authorities have imposed fines totalling more than ₹46 lakh as environmental compensation in 914 cases of stubble burning, with more than ₹24 lakh already recovered. Officials registered 710 FIRs related to stubble burning incidents, including 294 in Tarn Taran under Section 223 (disobedience of orders promulgated by a public servant) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.

The annual farm fire monitoring period begins on September 15, two weeks before paddy procurement starts on October 1. Taking a serious view of the "very high" number of farm fires in Punjab, the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) met with senior bureaucrats and police officers from 12 districts to review steps to prevent stubble burning.

Rajesh Verma, the chairperson of CAQM in NCR and adjoining areas, presided over the meeting via video conferencing with the State's Secretary, Environment; Secretary, Agriculture and Deputy Commissioners (DCs) and Senior Superintendents of Police (SSPs) from 12 districts.
The Commission directed that the monitoring and enforcement drive be intensified and that nodal officers be held accountable for failing to monitor and prevent farm fires.

articles.title: Lab tests show ethanol blend in E20 petrol as high as 31% in Karnataka
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Minister for Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs of Karnataka demands penalising OMCs, an E20 spoilage fund to compensate consumers

Petrol sold by several major oil companies in Karnataka contained ethanol far above the prescribed 20% level, in some cases as high as 31.2%, the State government has alleged, raising questions about transparency in the controversial ethanol blend petrol being sold to consumers across the country.

The samples in question were taken recently by the Department of Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs from Bengaluru Urban, Bengaluru Rural, Kolar, Chikkaballapura, Tumakuru, and Dakshina Kannada districts in Karnataka, said Rizwan Arshad, Minister of Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs, Karnataka, on November 6.

Petrol samples from major Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL) and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL) recorded ethanol blend percentage of 31.2% and 30.5%, respectively. Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL), Nayara, and Shell petrol samples revealed 26.5%, 26.1%, and 25.5% ethanol blend, respectively, he said.

Mr. Arshad said the samples were initially submitted to the in-house laboratories of IOCL and BPCL. But. he claimed, the test reports issued by these laboratories did not disclose the ethanol content in the fuel, despite it being one of the prescribed testing parameters. “This raises serious concerns on transparency from the oil majors and what they are hiding from the consumers,” he said.

“The Department of Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs, Karnataka, later got the same samples tested at labs recognised by National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL), and International Organisation for Standardisation (ISO). These reports have revealed higher ethanol blends,” Mr. Arshad said.

The Modi Government has already forced E20 petrol on the people, despite serious concerns over reduced mileage, additional fuel expenses and compatibility with older vehicles. Now, what we have uncovered in Karnataka is even more alarming. Our Government's independent laboratory tests have found ethanol content as high as 31.2% in petrol sold by major oil companies, with samples from seven districts exceeding the prescribed 20% limit. Even the Centre has acknowledged that E20 can reduce fuel efficiency in certain vehicles. What happens when the ethanol content goes beyond 30%? Who will bear the additional fuel costs and the risk to vehicle performance? Why should ordinary motorists pay the price for such failures? And look at the Modi Government's double standards: It claims ethanol blending benefits farmers, yet it has now excluded ethanol made from sugarcane juice, sugar syrup and B-heavy molasses from its latest procurement tender. At a time when Karnataka's farmers are already suffering from severe drought, the Centre is restricting an important market for sugarcane-based ethanol while allowing petrol to be sold with ethanol levels far beyond the prescribed limit. Where is the promised benefit to farmers? Where is the protection for motorists? Is this not deceiving both farmers and consumers? Prime Minister @narendramodi and Union Minister @nitin_gadkari owe the people an explanation. When the Union Government itself has prescribed a 20% blending standard, how is petrol containing over 30% ethanol reaching consumers? Who is monitoring these oil companies? Where is the accountability? We will place Karnataka's findings before the Union Government. I demand an immediate investigation, strict action against those responsible, transparent disclosure of ethanol content at every petrol pump and necessary safeguards for consumers.
ALSO WATCH SC refuses plea seeking mandatory E20 ethanol disclosure

Mr. Arshad said 99% of India’s over 35 crore vehicles are not built for ethanol blend of more than 20%, and the risk is not just limited to old vehicles. “Vehicles sold after April 2023 have been certified only up to E20. With lower-ethanol blend petrol withdrawn from nearly one lakh fuel stations, the consumer has been left with no alternative,” he said.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity 📅 06 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 5 Min Read

📰 Lab tests show ethanol blend in E20 petrol as high as 31% in Karnataka

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

Minister for Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs of Karnataka demands penalising OMCs, an E20 spoilage fund to compensate consumers

Petrol sold by several major oil companies in Karnataka contained ethanol far above the prescribed 20% level, in some cases as high as 31.2%, the State government has alleged, raising questions about transparency in the controversial ethanol blend petrol being sold to consumers across the country.

The samples in question were taken recently by the Department of Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs from Bengaluru Urban, Bengaluru Rural, Kolar, Chikkaballapura, Tumakuru, and Dakshina Kannada districts in Karnataka, said Rizwan Arshad, Minister of Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs, Karnataka, on November 6.

Petrol samples from major Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL) and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL) recorded ethanol blend percentage of 31.2% and 30.5%, respectively. Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL), Nayara, and Shell petrol samples revealed 26.5%, 26.1%, and 25.5% ethanol blend, respectively, he said.

Mr. Arshad said the samples were initially submitted to the in-house laboratories of IOCL and BPCL. But. he claimed, the test reports issued by these laboratories did not disclose the ethanol content in the fuel, despite it being one of the prescribed testing parameters. “This raises serious concerns on transparency from the oil majors and what they are hiding from the consumers,” he said.

“The Department of Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs, Karnataka, later got the same samples tested at labs recognised by National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL), and International Organisation for Standardisation (ISO). These reports have revealed higher ethanol blends,” Mr. Arshad said.

The Modi Government has already forced E20 petrol on the people, despite serious concerns over reduced mileage, additional fuel expenses and compatibility with older vehicles. Now, what we have uncovered in Karnataka is even more alarming. Our Government's independent laboratory tests have found ethanol content as high as 31.2% in petrol sold by major oil companies, with samples from seven districts exceeding the prescribed 20% limit. Even the Centre has acknowledged that E20 can reduce fuel efficiency in certain vehicles. What happens when the ethanol content goes beyond 30%? Who will bear the additional fuel costs and the risk to vehicle performance? Why should ordinary motorists pay the price for such failures? And look at the Modi Government's double standards: It claims ethanol blending benefits farmers, yet it has now excluded ethanol made from sugarcane juice, sugar syrup and B-heavy molasses from its latest procurement tender. At a time when Karnataka's farmers are already suffering from severe drought, the Centre is restricting an important market for sugarcane-based ethanol while allowing petrol to be sold with ethanol levels far beyond the prescribed limit. Where is the promised benefit to farmers? Where is the protection for motorists? Is this not deceiving both farmers and consumers? Prime Minister @narendramodi and Union Minister @nitin_gadkari owe the people an explanation. When the Union Government itself has prescribed a 20% blending standard, how is petrol containing over 30% ethanol reaching consumers? Who is monitoring these oil companies? Where is the accountability? We will place Karnataka's findings before the Union Government. I demand an immediate investigation, strict action against those responsible, transparent disclosure of ethanol content at every petrol pump and necessary safeguards for consumers.

ALSO WATCH SC refuses plea seeking mandatory E20 ethanol disclosure

Mr. Arshad said 99% of India’s over 35 crore vehicles are not built for ethanol blend of more than 20%, and the risk is not just limited to old vehicles. “Vehicles sold after April 2023 have been certified only up to E20. With lower-ethanol blend petrol withdrawn from nearly one lakh fuel stations, the consumer has been left with no alternative,” he said.

Assuming a 10% mileage loss at ₹100/litre, he said the hidden loss to consumers would add up to around ₹62,000 crore, on the basis of India’s consumption of 6,200 crore litres of fuel every year.

The Minister claimed that adding damage and repair costs due to higher blends, the loss would be around ₹1 lakh crore, but did not elaborate on how he arrived at this figure.

articles.title: Bengaluru cab driver kills wife, six members of her family
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The murders are believed to have been carried out between October 16 and November 3, with the bodies dumped at multiple locations on Bengaluru’s outskirts, including one near the foothills of Nandi Hills in Chickballapur.
In a shocking murder spree in Bengaluru, a 52-year-old man allegedly killed his wife and six members of her family over a family dispute, according to senior police officers.
The accused, identified as Indushekar, a cab driver, has been arrested by the Rajajinagar police.

The murders are believed to have been carried out between October 16 and November 3, with the bodies dumped at multiple locations on the city’s outskirts, including one near the foothills of Nandi Hills in Chickballapur.

The incident came to light after a family member of one of the deceased lodged a missing complaint at the Srirampura police station. Subsequent investigations led to Indushekhar being detained, and his statements unravelled a series of horrific murders that allegedly took place at his house near Bhashyam Circle in Rajajinagar, north Bengaluru.

The deceased have been identified as Indushekhar’s wife, Sunita (40); his mother-in-law, Roopavathi (65); his two brothers-in-law Shivakumar (30) and Shankar (44); their wives Divya (30) and Nalini (29), and Shivakumar’s son, Puneeth (7). The murders were reportedly carried out on different occasions after inviting family members to his house on separate days. The police are verifying these claims.

According to the preliminary investigation, Indushekhar allegedly used a grinding stone to kill the victims. The killings reportedly began with the murder of his wife and mother-in-law. The accused then invited other victims to his house, where he reportedly carried out the murders. He has stated that he had been planning the murders for several months and decided to execute them after his mother-in-law visited their house in mid-September, according to a police source.

“He maintained that his mother-in-law and her family used to abuse him and frequently intervene in family matters. Even during the September visit, his mother-in-law allegedly abused him repeatedly, which angered the accused,” the source told The Hindu .
Meanwhile, the police are investigating where the bodies were dumped and what assistance the accused received.

articles.title: Asian parties reject ‘unilateral actions’, call for respect for international law
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The declaration was unanimously adopted at the 13th General Assembly of ICAPP, held in Seoul from November 4 to 6, with representatives of 83 political parties from across Asia participating

The International Conference of Asian Political Parties (ICAPP) on Friday (November 6, 2026) adopted the Seoul Declaration, expressing concern over unilateral actions and reaffirming state sovereignty and territorial integrity, while also calling for strict adherence to the principles of the UN Charter amid growing geopolitical tensions.

The declaration was unanimously adopted at the 13th General Assembly of ICAPP, held in Seoul from November 4 to 6, with representatives of 83 political parties from across Asia participating. The summit was jointly hosted by South Korea’s governing Democratic Party and the Opposition People Power Party.

The plenary sessions of the Assembly, attended by representatives from Palestine, Iran, China, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh and others, saw discussions on contemporary conflicts, including in Palestine and Iran. Though there is no reference to these conflicts in the declaration, members expressed “great concern” on unilateral actions, intensifying geopolitical rivalry and weakening international cooperation. It said non-interference in the internal affairs of states, the peaceful settlement of international disputes, and the equal status of all nations were essential to maintaining peace, stability and reconciliation.

“We were particularly concerned that in international relations, unilateral actions, the use of the threat of force, and selective observance of international obligations can erode confidence in the international legal order,” reads the declaration.

Rejecting the use or threat of force as instruments of diplomacy, the participating parties called on all countries to respect international law consistently, irrespective of their size or geopolitical influence. They also stressed the need to keep diplomatic channels open, including between adversaries.
The declaration sought to place the principles of the UN Charter at the centre of efforts to rebuild trust among nations.

Answering a question from The Hindu on whether ICAPP can be a platform for mediation and conflict resolution in Asia, Chung Eui-yong, Chairperson of the ICAPP Standing Committee and former Minister of Foreign Affairs of South Korea, said ICAPP is a platform for dialogue between political parties and that parties can influence governments in moving towards peaceful settlement of disputes.

“We are not governments. Political parties represent people. What we can do is influence our governments. The governing as well as Opposition parties should put in their best effort to influence government policies and promote peace,” said Mr. Chung.
He added that in the Seoul declaration, “we agreed to reject war as an instrument of coercion. This demonstrates our strong commitment to peaceful settlement of conflicts.”

Beyond geopolitical security, the declaration addressed challenges to democratic governance, climate change and the rapid development of artificial intelligence. It highlighted a growing deficit of trust between nations, citizens, and institutions, and called for responsible, human-centred oversight of AI technologies, equitable climate finance for developing countries facing climate-related disasters, and stronger democratic accountability.

The declaration was unanimously adopted at the 13th General Assembly of ICAPP, held in Seoul from November 4 to 6, with representatives of 83 political parties from across Asia participating

The International Conference of Asian Political Parties (ICAPP) on Friday (November 6, 2026) adopted the Seoul Declaration, expressing concern over unilateral actions and reaffirming state sovereignty and territorial integrity, while also calling for strict adherence to the principles of the UN Charter amid growing geopolitical tensions.

The declaration was unanimously adopted at the 13th General Assembly of ICAPP, held in Seoul from November 4 to 6, with representatives of 83 political parties from across Asia participating. The summit was jointly hosted by South Korea’s governing Democratic Party and the Opposition People Power Party.

The plenary sessions of the Assembly, attended by representatives from Palestine, Iran, China, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh and others, saw discussions on contemporary conflicts, including in Palestine and Iran. Though there is no reference to these conflicts in the declaration, members expressed “great concern” on unilateral actions, intensifying geopolitical rivalry and weakening international cooperation. It said non-interference in the internal affairs of states, the peaceful settlement of international disputes, and the equal status of all nations were essential to maintaining peace, stability and reconciliation.

“We were particularly concerned that in international relations, unilateral actions, the use of the threat of force, and selective observance of international obligations can erode confidence in the international legal order,” reads the declaration.

Rejecting the use or threat of force as instruments of diplomacy, the participating parties called on all countries to respect international law consistently, irrespective of their size or geopolitical influence. They also stressed the need to keep diplomatic channels open, including between adversaries.

The declaration sought to place the principles of the UN Charter at the centre of efforts to rebuild trust among nations.

Answering a question from The Hindu on whether ICAPP can be a platform for mediation and conflict resolution in Asia, Chung Eui-yong, Chairperson of the ICAPP Standing Committee and former Minister of Foreign Affairs of South Korea, said ICAPP is a platform for dialogue between political parties and that parties can influence governments in moving towards peaceful settlement of disputes.

“We are not governments. Political parties represent people. What we can do is influence our governments. The governing as well as Opposition parties should put in their best effort to influence government policies and promote peace,” said Mr. Chung.

He added that in the Seoul declaration, “we agreed to reject war as an instrument of coercion. This demonstrates our strong commitment to peaceful settlement of conflicts.”

Beyond geopolitical security, the declaration addressed challenges to democratic governance, climate change and the rapid development of artificial intelligence. It highlighted a growing deficit of trust between nations, citizens, and institutions, and called for responsible, human-centred oversight of AI technologies, equitable climate finance for developing countries facing climate-related disasters, and stronger democratic accountability.
