articles.title: Federal judge orders 14-day delay on any work beginning on Trump’s monumental arch
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Judge Tanya Chutkan’s temporary restraining order came just over an hour after the National Capital Planning Commission approved the memorial arch in an 8-4 vote
A federal judge late on Thursday (November 5, 2026) blocked the Trump administration from breaking ground on a towering memorial arch for 14 days.

The temporary restraining order by U.S. District Judge Tanya Chutkan, halting the work, represents a major setback for one of President Donald Trump’s most prominent projects in his vision to remake Washington.

The decision followed a series of steps taken earlier on Thursday by the government, including the final approval of the arch by the National Capital Planning Commission in an 8-4 vote after a hearing of nine and a half hours, where dozens of witnesses opposed the construction.

The administration said the work could begin as soon as the approval was in place, the Interior Department issued a final decision authorising construction and the National Park Service published the proper notification.
In issuing the temporary stop, Judge Chutkan said Virginia and the District of Columbia had shown that the immediacy of the construction would cause real harm to the plaintiffs.

“The harm is certain,” she wrote. “Defendants initially notified the court that construction could begin as early as November 5, 2026, if the NCPC approves the project at its meeting that day and the Department of the Interior authorizes construction.” In their filing, Virginia and the District of Columbia warned of traffic pattern distortions, as well as concerns about the impact on mutual aid emergency calls if the arch were to proceed.

“Second, the District and Virginia will incur significant unrecoverable costs. As soon as construction begins, DDOT [District Department of Transportation] will need to expend staff time and operating resources to affirmatively and proactively manage temporary detours, crashes or disabled vehicles,” Judge Chutkan wrote.

The judge’s decision came just over an hour after the commission’s hearing ended. The final vote came after nine and a half hours and scores of people opposing it. The vote broke along federal and local lines. Those in favour work for the administration or are connected to the President, who was pushing for the immediate construction. Opponents represented the city of Washington.
The panel’s Trump-appointed chairman launched the meeting with a gushing appraisal of the towering monument and lauded Mr. Trump for wanting to build it.

“President Trump understands as president and a superb builder that it’s important to our national identity to display who we are through grand monuments,” said Mark Paoletta, the commission’s chairman.

articles.title: Keralam’s mangrove cover expanded in past decade despite prior decline, finds study
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Study by ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute based in Kochi compared satellite images from 2017 and 2026 to map changes in mangrove vegetation across Keralam’s coastal districts
Mangrove cover in Keralam registered an overall increase over the past decade, a new study by ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute (CMFRI) has found.

The study, presented at the international symposium on fisheries and remote sensing hosted at CMFRI, compared satellite images from 2017 and 2026 to map changes in mangrove vegetation across Keralam’s coastal districts. It found an overall rise in mangrove cover during the period, despite the State having lost nearly 90% of its mangroves over the past five decades, a statement issued by CMFRI in Kochi said.

Mangroves serve as vital breeding and nursery grounds for fish, protect coastlines from cyclones and storm surges, and help absorb atmospheric carbon. The findings highlight the potential of satellite-based monitoring to track mangrove recovery and support conservation efforts along Keralam’s coast.

The three-day international symposium is being jointly organised by Trevor Platt Science Foundation, Department of Chemical Oceanography of the Cochin University of Science and Technology (CUSAT), CMFRI and Marine Biological Association of India.

Another study presented at the symposium highlighted the increasing incidence of marine heatwaves in the Bay of Bengal. The region experienced more than 100 marine heatwave events between 1982 and 2023, with both their frequency and cumulative intensity showing an increasing trend.
The study was presented by the Department of Oceanography of Shahjalal University of Science and Technology, Bangladesh.

articles.title: Ravichandra takes charge as TTD Specified Authority chief, prioritises pilgrim amenities
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Muddada Ravichandra, Executive Officer of Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD), assumed charge as Chairman of the TTD Specified Authority on Friday.
TTD Additional Executive Officer Ch. Venkaiah Chowdary administered the oath of office to Mr. Ravichandra at the Bangaru Vakili of the Srivari Temple in Tirumala.

Speaking to the media after the ceremony, Mr. Ravichandra thanked the State government and Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu for entrusting him with the responsibility. He said his priorities included improving pilgrim amenities, strengthening educational institutions and upgrading healthcare facilities.

He said efforts would be made to ensure that devotees visiting Tirumala had access to better facilities for a smooth darshan. Attention would also be given to improving amenities at all 64 temples administered by TTD.

On the education front, Mr. Ravichandra said the focus would be on providing quality education in TTD-run institutions, along with opportunities for the overall development of students and their preparation for future challenges.
He also stressed the need to strengthen healthcare infrastructure and improve medical services at TTD-run hospitals by providing modern facilities.
He said TTD would continue to expand its pilgrim welfare, education and healthcare initiatives while carrying forward its religious and spiritual activities.

1. Core Context & Background: Muddada Ravichandra, Executive Officer of Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD), assumed charge as Chairman of the TTD Specified Authority on Friday.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: TTD Additional Executive Officer Ch. Venkaiah Chowdary administered the oath of office to Mr. Ravichandra at the Bangaru Vakili of the Srivari Temple in Tirumala.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: He said TTD would continue to expand its pilgrim welfare, education and healthcare initiatives while carrying forward its religious and spiritual activities.

articles.title: Official residences need timely repairs, says Pinarayi Vijayan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Many of the official residences are in a pathetic state due to poor maintenance and the media tend to depict any effort to launch repairs as ‘beautification,’ implying that it is unnecessary spending, says Keralam Leader of the Opposition

Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan has underscored the need for carrying out timely repairs on the official residences allotted to the Chief Minister, Leader of the Opposition, and the Ministers.

Reacting to a recent controversy over repairs planned at the Cliff House, the official residence of the Keralam Chief Minister, Mr. Vijayan said many of these official residences were in a pathetic state due to the absence of proper maintenance and the media tended to depict any effort to launch repairs as ‘beautification,’ implying that it was unnecessary spending.

Repairs were planned at the Cliff House when he was a resident there as Chief Minister in the previous LDF government, Mr. Vijayan said. Government departments wanted the repairs done as part of security arrangements, but they were not taken forward as the government’s term came to an end, he said.

Later, he had rented a house instead of moving into Cantonment House, the official residence of the Leader of the Opposition, as it was also in need of repairs, Mr. Vijayan. “I had moved into the rented house under the impression that it would be only for two weeks. I’m surprised how the previous Leader of the Opposition (Mr. Satheesan) lived there,” he said. Ideally, the government departments concerned should have a firm policy on repairs and carry them out once a year without waiting for the occupants’ clearance, but without inconveniencing them, he said.
Many of the official residences, situated on sprawling grounds in different parts of the capital city, are Travancore-era bungalows.

articles.title: Karnataka Lokayukta calls for improvement in administrative functioning
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Karnataka Lokayukta B.S. Patil has called upon government officials to improve their administrative functioning, develop a problem-solving approach and ensure that government welfare schemes reach eligible beneficiaries effectively.

Chairing a meeting with district-level officers at the J.H. Patel Hall in the Zilla Panchayat in Koppal on Friday, Mr. Patil said the government had introduced several schemes for the welfare of the common people and allocated substantial funds for their implementation. It was the responsibility of every government official to ensure that these schemes and funds reached the intended beneficiaries in an efficient and honest manner, he said.
Warning officials against corruption, he said strict disciplinary action would be taken without any leniency if any officer or staff member was found indulging in corrupt practices.

“Although the government provided its employees with several facilities and sufficient opportunities to lead a decent life, some officials were reportedly resorting to corruption out of greed. Such conduct would not be tolerated,” he cautioned.

Mr. Patil said that a people-oriented approach and administrative efficiency at the district level could make a significant contribution to the overall development of the State. Proper utilisation of government funds and their honest delivery to eligible beneficiaries would help improve people’s standard of living, he said.

Pointing to the duties and responsibilities assigned to every government employee and the supervisory officers appointed to monitor their performance, Mr. Patil said the delivery of government services was not always smooth. “If a person had to visit a government office repeatedly for the same work, it indicated that the system was not functioning properly. Officials should discharge their duties honestly and conscientiously, keeping in mind the values instilled in them by their parents and the principles on which they had been brought up,” he said.

Holding that government employees could truly become public servants only by performing their duties honestly and in accordance with the law, Mr. Patil said that such honest performance would give real meaning to the principle that government service is service to God. “Every person working in public service should be familiar with the provisions of the Lokayukta Act, as any violation, whether minor or serious, would attract punishment under the law,” he warned.

Referring to hostels and residential schools functioning under the Social Welfare and Backward Classes Welfare departments, he instructed the officials not to admit students beyond their sanctioned capacity, as overcrowding would lead to a shortage of basic amenities and adversely affect their academic progress. He directed the authorities to shift students from overcrowded hostels to rented buildings and ensure that they were provided with the necessary infrastructure. “Cleanliness and discipline should also be given priority in all hostels and residential schools,” he said.

Lokayukta secretary Srinath, additional registrar Krishnayya, Deputy Commissioner Suresh B. Itnal, Zilla Panchayat Chief Executive Officer Varnit Negi, Superintendent of Police Sahil Bagla, Raichur Lokayukta Superintendent of Police Siddaraju and other officials were present at the meeting.

articles.title: When feed prices crack the egg market
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Rising maize and soybean prices, the mainstays of poultry feed, are squeezing farmers even as El Niño threatens to disrupt grain supplies; with feed accounting for nearly 80% of production costs, the pressure is building on Telangana’s poultry sector, raising concerns over egg output and prices

An unusual warming of the Pacific Ocean, nearly 12,000 km from Telangana, is casting a shadow over the State’s poultry industry. El Niño may seem far removed from the price of an egg, but its ripple effects are being felt in the cost of maize and soybean, the two principal ingredients of poultry feed. For farmers, the question of what came first, the egg or the chicken, has a clear answer: feed comes first.

Prices of maize and soybean have surged even as the harvest is under way. Against the Minimum Support Prices of ₹2,410 and ₹5,708 a quintal, respectively, open-market rates are around ₹3,200 and ₹6,000, up from ₹2,000 and ₹3,500 six months ago. Poultry associations also allege deliberate hoarding.

“We are all worried. What will we be able to feed them in the coming months,” asks a representative of the Telangana Poultry Breeders’ Association which recently approached Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy for urgent measures. They sought broken rice and rice unfit for human consumption from Food Corporation of India and Markfed godowns at a marginal subsidy. “We don’t want it for free,” he adds.

But rice cannot simply replace maize and soybean. Poultry feed is scientifically formulated to meet birds’ nutritional requirements at different growth stages. A commercial chicken needs about 1.5 kg of feed to gain 1 kg in body weight, enabling it to reach 2 kg in 36 days. This is its feed conversion ratio (FCR).

The ICAR-Directorate of Poultry Research (ICAR-DPR) has developed feed formulations, while the Bureau of Indian Standards specifies 15 types according to birds’ age and purpose. In 2022, ICAR-DPR published over 1,100 region-specific formulations. A typical 100-kg mix for breeder and layer birds contains 50% maize, 30% soybean, 15-18% de-oiled rice bran, and 1 kg each of mineral mixture and probiotics.

Former Animal Husbandry Department director V. Lakshma Reddy says standardised feed ensures balanced nutrition, digestibility and feed efficiency, helping reduce FCR and costs. “The present feed composition is a remarkable achievement by our scientists, animal nutritionists and geneticists,” he says, adding that a commercial layer chicken in Telangana produces about 320 eggs a year, comparable to output in the United States and Europe.

Research institutions such as ICAR-DPR in Hyderabad, Central Avian Research Institute-Bareilly, National Institute of Animal Nutrition and Physiology-Bengaluru and Indian Veterinary Research Institute-Bareilly are exploring alternatives such as Azolla, seaweed, oilseed meals, distillers dried grains with solubles (DDGS), gluten meal and tapioca. The Kerala Veterinary and Animal Sciences University has also tested Black Soldier Fly larvae as feed; processing units now produce it for poultry and fish.

Telangana, the country’s third-largest egg producer after Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, produces 3.80 crore eggs daily, according to the National Egg Coordination Committee (NECC). More than 2,000 farmers manage 5.5 crore layer birds, with 1.80 crore eggs shipped daily to Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh.

On November 6, a dozen eggs at an egg syndicate in Netaji Nagar at Kapra, Hyderabad, cost ₹94, while a tray of 30 was priced at ₹210. The NECC’s suggested farm-gate price was ₹660 per 100 eggs. “Prices usually rise in November and peak in December because of cooler weather and Christmas and New Year demand. But the increase has come early,” says Raju, who sources eggs from farms in Medchal and Keesara.

The average NECC price in Hyderabad was ₹570 per 100 eggs in November last year and ₹655 in December. On November 6 this year, Chennai and Kolkata were already quoting ₹730, the highest in the country.

articles.title: U.S. midterm results add to global AI-linked stock sell-off, $2.5 trillion wiped off Nasdaq 100
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Democrats’ victories raise prospect of tighter scrutiny of data-centre projects as investors reassess AI spending; Indian equities buck global market weakness

Global technology stocks tumbled on fears that the massive infrastructure investments underpinning the artificial intelligence (AI) boom may take longer to build, finance and monetise, even as Indian equities bucked the worldwide sell-off with a sharp rally on November 6.

The sell-off, fuelled by concerns over mounting AI-related capital expenditure and uncertain returns, gathered momentum following the U.S. midterm election results. Democrats’ victories have heightened the prospect of tighter scrutiny of data-centre projects and possible restrictions on new developments, adding to investor anxiety.

The Nasdaq-100 plunged 6.36% on November 5, erasing approximately $2.53 trillion from its aggregate adjusted market value, according to Nasdaq index data. The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.52%, while the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 4.36% and 3.44%, respectively.
Semiconductor stocks bore the brunt, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index slumping 12.2%. Nvidia lost about 9%, while AMD and Micron Technology shed more than 17% each.
The weakness spilled over into Asian markets on Friday. South Korea’s KOSPI fell 6.02%, after plunging more than 8% intraday. Japan’s Nikkei 225 declined 5.96%, while Taiwan’s TAIEX lost 4.51%.
Indian equities, however, bucked the trend. The Sensex surged 1,718 points, or 2.17%, to close at 81,028.02, while the Nifty 50 advanced 2.01% to 25,030.35.

Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) were net buyers of Indian equities worth ₹14,974.68 crore on November 5, against net sales of ₹10,444.54 crore by domestic institutional investors (DIIs), provisional exchange data across the NSE, BSE and MSEI showed.

A Macquarie Research note flagged potential regulatory headwinds for data-centre development following election outcomes in Texas, Georgia and Ohio, where proposals to impose moratoriums or restrictions on new projects could affect the industry.

Greater scrutiny of power connections, backup-generator emissions, water consumption, zoning and taxation could prolong approvals and raise project costs. The impact may be more pronounced for projects in the pipeline than for facilities that have already secured approvals and power capacity.

Macquarie said approved but unleased data-centre capacity could gain value if fresh supply faces delays, benefiting well-capitalised operators with access to power and approved sites. It remained positive on the digital infrastructure sector.

articles.title: EU says 'a lot of work' still needed to reach Ukraine peace deal
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Earlier, a NATO spokeswoman said Ukraine's allies are working for a "just and sustainable" end to the war ahead of U.S.-mediated talks next week in Abu Dhabi

The EU said on Friday (November 6, 2026) that "a lot of work" was still needed to reach peace in Ukraine, and the bloc would decide on its own security matters, after U.S. President Donald Trump touted a deal with Russia involving "all of Europe".

Mr. Trump on Thursday (November 5, 2026) predicted a "very big" deal with Russia involving not only the Ukraine war but "all of Europe", in remarks likely to fuel fresh fears on the continent of a pivot towards the Kremlin.
"We all wish that we will have a peace deal soon. We are all working in that regard," said EU spokeswoman Paula Pinho.
"But there is a lot of work that needs to go into it, and above all, there needs to be a willingness on the side of the one who first started the war."
Ms. Pinho added, "It's obviously up to the European Union to decide on matters which affect its security."
Earlier, a NATO spokeswoman said Ukraine's allies are working for a "just and sustainable" end to the war ahead of U.S.-mediated talks next week in Abu Dhabi.

On Thursday (November 5, 2026), talks in Brussels involving U.S., Ukrainian, European, and NATO officials "built on productive discussions in Miami and Oslo and sought to advance a just and sustainable end to the war in Ukraine", she said.

After participating by video link in the talks, Jared Kushner, the President's envoy and son-in-law, wrote that the United States was working on "a broader European security architecture that can help establish the conditions for lasting peace".
Mr. Kushner said Washington's "objective is to develop practical arrangements that address the security concerns of all sides".

He insisted that "any arrangements must fully respect the sovereignty, territorial integrity, and independent decision-making of every nation" and said NATO would "remain central to European collective defence".

articles.title: India-born Saba Haider wins Illinois State Representative election
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: An alumnus of Aligarh Muslim University (AMU), Saba Haider earned an MSc in Wildlife Science from the institution; the AMU Network congratulated her on her victory, describing it as a "proud moment for the university community"
India-born Democrat Saba Haider has won election to the Illinois House of Representatives, becoming the first South Asian woman to be elected to the state's General Assembly.

Ms. Haider won the November 3 U.S. mid-term elections from the 84th District with 70.9% of the votes, securing 20,756 ballots against her Republican rival Brian Scopa, who received 8,520 votes, or 29.1%.
The 84th District covers parts of Will, DuPage, Kane and Kendall counties, including Aurora, Naperville, Oswego, Montgomery and Boulder Hill.

“We did it! We worked hard for the last 15 months talking to voters in every corner of District 84 to learn what they care about, what they want to see change, and how we can work together to build stronger, more prosperous, and more inclusive communities,” Ms. Haider said in a social media post on Thursday (November 5, 2026).
She thanked voters, family members, friends, campaign team members and volunteers, describing the campaign as a "grassroots, people-powered movement".
"Ultimately this election was about the people who call this community home. It was about building the future we all deserve," she said.
Ms. Haider said her victory was for everyone who believes in an Illinois that is "a fair, just, and welcoming place for all".
Before entering the Illinois legislature, Ms. Haider served as a DuPage County Board member and community advocate.
Born in India, her family hails from Bulandshahr district in Uttar Pradesh. She immigrated to the United States about 20 years ago.
“Since then, I’ve dedicated my life towards giving back to the community that helped me and my family make Illinois our home," Haider said during her campaign.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes

Cyclones Arnab and Murasu have caused preliminary losses of over ₹500 crore to the Andhra Pradesh Energy Department, with more than 7,500 electricity poles damaged by Cyclone Murasu alone, Energy Minister Gottipati Ravi Kumar said.

articles.title: Karnataka CM and Dy. CM question BJP-led Union government on higher ethanol blends
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Pointing to findings from petrol samples tested across the State showing ethanol blends higher than the prescribed 20% on the social media platform X, Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar said the Union government cannot turn a blind eye to the violation of E20 norms and blend more ethanol, thereby imposing a financial burden on ordinary citizens. “Reduced mileage, potential vehicle damage and rising maintenance costs are concerns that deserve serious attention. It is unacceptable that consumers bear the cost while oil companies continue to report substantial profits,” he said.

Deputy Chief Minister G. Parameshwara said the “Modi-led government had already forced E20 petrol on the people, despite serious concerns over reduced mileage, additional fuel expenses and compatibility with older vehicles,” and the findings by the Department of Legal Metrology, Karnataka, were even more alarming.

He called the BJP-led Union government’s claim that an ethanol blend of petrol would help farmers a “double standard”. “It [the BJP-led Union government] claims that ethanol blending benefits farmers, yet it has now excluded ethanol made from sugarcane juice, sugar syrup and B-heavy molasses from its latest procurement tender. At a time when Karnataka’s farmers are already suffering from severe drought, the Centre is restricting an important market for sugarcane-based ethanol while allowing petrol to be sold with ethanol levels far beyond the prescribed limit. Where is the promised benefit to farmers? Where is the protection for motorists? Is this not deceiving both farmers and consumers?” he asked.

Mr. Parameshwara said Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways Nitin Gadkari owe the people an explanation. He demanded “an immediate investigation, strict action against those responsible, transparent disclosure of ethanol content at every petrol pump and necessary safeguards for consumers”.

articles.title: BJP MLA asserts TDP-Jana Sena-BJP alliance will remain intact
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Adinarayana Reddy dismisses YSRCP’s hopes of a split; says alliance will address organisational shortcomings and emerge stronger

The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) Legislative Assembly Chief Whip and MLA C. Adinarayana Reddy on Friday asserted that the TDP-Jana Sena-BJP alliance would remain intact and emerge stronger, dismissing the YSR Congress Party’s hopes of a split in the coalition.

Addressing a press conference at the BJP State office, he said the alliance had secured public support in the recent local body elections and would strive to improve its performance in future elections by addressing organisational shortcomings.

He cautioned against comparing local body election results with those of general elections, pointing out that candidates’ personal influence, local grievances and lack of coordination among leaders could affect electoral outcomes. The alliance would identify and address these shortcomings, he said.

Targeting YSR Congress Party president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy, he alleged that the former Chief Minister was criticising the coalition to remain politically relevant and obstructing development instead of respecting the people’s mandate. He asked Mr. Jagan to explain the CBI and Enforcement Directorate cases against him and demanded that the facts surrounding the murder of former MP Y.S. Vivekananda Reddy be brought to light.

Mr. Adinarayana Reddy accused the previous YSRCP government of undermining the State’s development prospects by delaying the Amaravati capital and Polavaram irrigation projects. The coalition government was according priority to infrastructure development, investment promotion, renewable energy and industrial growth, he said.
Citing investment opportunities in aerospace and defence manufacturing at Puttaparthi, he said the sector could attract investments of around ₹15,000 crore.
Referring to the BJP’s performance in Jammalamadugu constituency, he said the party had won 19 councillor seats in Yerraguntla municipality and secured encouraging results in the MPTC elections.
The alliance aimed to put Andhra Pradesh on a stronger development path by 2029 and realise the vision of a developed State by 2047, he said.
BJP State spokesperson Shaik Baji and party leaders Sashi Bhushan Reddy and Rajesh Reddy were present.

Adinarayana Reddy dismisses YSRCP’s hopes of a split; says alliance will address organisational shortcomings and emerge stronger

The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) Legislative Assembly Chief Whip and MLA C. Adinarayana Reddy on Friday asserted that the TDP-Jana Sena-BJP alliance would remain intact and emerge stronger, dismissing the YSR Congress Party’s hopes of a split in the coalition.

Addressing a press conference at the BJP State office, he said the alliance had secured public support in the recent local body elections and would strive to improve its performance in future elections by addressing organisational shortcomings.

He cautioned against comparing local body election results with those of general elections, pointing out that candidates’ personal influence, local grievances and lack of coordination among leaders could affect electoral outcomes. The alliance would identify and address these shortcomings, he said.

Targeting YSR Congress Party president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy, he alleged that the former Chief Minister was criticising the coalition to remain politically relevant and obstructing development instead of respecting the people’s mandate. He asked Mr. Jagan to explain the CBI and Enforcement Directorate cases against him and demanded that the facts surrounding the murder of former MP Y.S. Vivekananda Reddy be brought to light.

Mr. Adinarayana Reddy accused the previous YSRCP government of undermining the State’s development prospects by delaying the Amaravati capital and Polavaram irrigation projects. The coalition government was according priority to infrastructure development, investment promotion, renewable energy and industrial growth, he said.

Citing investment opportunities in aerospace and defence manufacturing at Puttaparthi, he said the sector could attract investments of around ₹15,000 crore.

Referring to the BJP’s performance in Jammalamadugu constituency, he said the party had won 19 councillor seats in Yerraguntla municipality and secured encouraging results in the MPTC elections.

The alliance aimed to put Andhra Pradesh on a stronger development path by 2029 and realise the vision of a developed State by 2047, he said.

articles.title: Number of polling stations in Keralam increases by 216
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The total number has now gone up to 30,682, says Chief Electoral Officer D. Sajith Babu

The number of polling stations in Keralam has gone up by 216, taking the total number to 30,682, Chief Electoral Officer (Keralam) D. Sajith Babu said on Friday. The Election Commission of India (ECI) had given its approval for the rationalisation of polling stations. Before the exercise, Keralam had 30,471 stations, the same number it had for the 2026 Assembly elections.
While 216 new stations have been formed, five existing ones in Ernakulam district have been merged. Also, 178 polling station buildings/places have been changed.

After the rationalisation, Malappuram continues to have the highest number of polling stations (3,773), followed by Thiruvananthapuram (unchanged at 3,173) and Ernakulam (3,154). Wayanad has the lowest number (717).

The number of voters at each station, availability of amenities, accessibility and geographical peculiarities were taken into account for the exercise. “The new polling stations have been formed, and some of them have been changed based on the criteria prescribed by the ECI and the maximum number of voters allowed in each polling station,” the CEO said.

articles.title: AIDSO opposes move to bring government schools under private adoption
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The All India Democratic Students’ Organisation (AIDSO), Mysuru district committee, staged a protest near Ramaswamy Circle here on Friday, opposing the State government’s reported move to allow private educational institutions and corporate companies to adopt government schools.
Addressing the protesters, AIDSO district secretary Nitin alleged that the government was paving the way for the closure of 45,000 government schools through the KPS-Magnet policy.

He claimed that a meeting was held at Vidhana Soudha on November 4 to facilitate the adoption of government schools by corporate companies and private educational institutions. “In the first phase, 2,000 government schools would be taken up for adoption,” he alleged.

Criticising remarks by the Chief Minister and other government representatives questioning the quality of education in government schools despite teachers drawing salaries ranging from ₹70,000 to ₹1.5 lakh, he said such statements ignored the government’s responsibility to address policy-related shortcomings in the public education system.

Under the proposal, each private institution would adopt three government schools and be allowed to name the developed schools after itself, the AIDSO claimed in a statement. The government had also reportedly sought private institutions’ support in providing teachers, computers and laboratory equipment, besides making available old buses from private schools, he alleged.
He also claimed that 14 government schools had already been merged with the Hegganuru Karnataka Public School in Kanakapura taluk of Bengaluru South district.

The All India Democratic Students’ Organisation (AIDSO), Mysuru district committee, staged a protest near Ramaswamy Circle here on Friday, opposing the State government’s reported move to allow private educational institutions and corporate companies to adopt government schools.

Addressing the protesters, AIDSO district secretary Nitin alleged that the government was paving the way for the closure of 45,000 government schools through the KPS-Magnet policy.

He claimed that a meeting was held at Vidhana Soudha on November 4 to facilitate the adoption of government schools by corporate companies and private educational institutions. “In the first phase, 2,000 government schools would be taken up for adoption,” he alleged.

Criticising remarks by the Chief Minister and other government representatives questioning the quality of education in government schools despite teachers drawing salaries ranging from ₹70,000 to ₹1.5 lakh, he said such statements ignored the government’s responsibility to address policy-related shortcomings in the public education system.

Under the proposal, each private institution would adopt three government schools and be allowed to name the developed schools after itself, the AIDSO claimed in a statement. The government had also reportedly sought private institutions’ support in providing teachers, computers and laboratory equipment, besides making available old buses from private schools, he alleged.

He also claimed that 14 government schools had already been merged with the Hegganuru Karnataka Public School in Kanakapura taluk of Bengaluru South district.

Social activist Ugra Narasimhe Gowda termed the move to hand over government schools built with taxpayers’ money to private institutions as “anti-education”. He urged people to oppose the KPS-Magnet scheme, which he said went against the spirit of the Right to Education Act.

Retired Kannada professor Latha Mysuru criticised Kannada activists and writers for not opposing the policy. DSS leader Chornalli Shivanna also spoke.

Members of the Save Public Education Committee, farmers’ associations, social activists, AIDSO office-bearers and students participated in the protest.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: This would be ADNOC’s fifth long-term LNG supply agreement with India.

Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) on Friday signed a 10-year sales and purchase agreement with Gujarat Energy to supply up to four million tonnes of liquefied natural gas (LNG) from 2028, further strengthening its presence in India’s expanding gas market.
The agreement marks ADNOC’s fifth LNG supply deal with an Indian company, following similar arrangements with Bharat Petroleum, Indian Oil Corporation, GAIL and Hindustan Petroleum.
Under the agreement, XRG, ADNOC’s international investment arm, will supply LNG produced outside the Gulf and owned by it through ADNOC’s global LNG marketing and trading platform.

Rashid Al Mazrouei, Chief Marketing & Origination Officer (LNG) at ADNOC, said, “It represents the first sale of molecules from XRG’s international portfolio, reinforcing our commitment to delivering reliable, long-term LNG supplies.”

He added, “Through our integrated LNG marketing and trading platform, we are connecting our growing international portfolio with customers in key regions across global markets, while providing India with reliable, flexible and long-term LNG supplies.”

ADNOC’s global LNG marketing and trading platform also has supply agreements with Japan’s INPEX and Thailand’s Gulf Group. The platform aims to market 47 million tonnes per annum (mtpa) of LNG beyond 2030.
Avantika Singh Aulakh, Managing Director of Gujarat Energy, said, “Through this partnership, Gujarat Energy and ADNOC are joining forces to fully realize the power of our collaboration.”
Gujarat Energy operates a city gas distribution network spanning 44 districts across six states.

articles.title: $2.5 trillion wiped off Nasdaq 100 as U.S. midterm outcome adds to AI stock slump
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Democrats’ victories raise prospect of tighter scrutiny of data-centre projects as investors reassess AI spending; Indian equities buck global market weakness

Global technology stocks tumbled on fears that the massive infrastructure investments underpinning the artificial intelligence (AI) boom may take longer to build, finance and monetise, even as Indian equities bucked the worldwide sell-off with a sharp rally on November 6.

The sell-off, fuelled by concerns over mounting AI-related capital expenditure and uncertain returns, gathered momentum following the U.S. midterm election results. Democrats’ victories have heightened the prospect of tighter scrutiny of data-centre projects and possible restrictions on new developments, adding to investor anxiety.

The Nasdaq-100 plunged 6.36% on November 5, erasing approximately $2.53 trillion from its aggregate adjusted market value, according to Nasdaq index data. The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.52%, while the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 4.36% and 3.44%, respectively.
Semiconductor stocks bore the brunt, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index slumping 12.2%. Nvidia lost about 9%, while AMD and Micron Technology shed more than 17% each.
The weakness spilled over into Asian markets on Friday. South Korea’s KOSPI fell 6.02%, after plunging more than 8% intraday. Japan’s Nikkei 225 declined 5.96%, while Taiwan’s TAIEX lost 4.51%.
Indian equities, however, bucked the trend. The Sensex surged 1,718 points, or 2.17%, to close at 81,028.02, while the Nifty 50 advanced 2.01% to 25,030.35.

Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) were net buyers of Indian equities worth ₹14,974.68 crore on November 5, against net sales of ₹10,444.54 crore by domestic institutional investors (DIIs), provisional exchange data across the NSE, BSE and MSEI showed.

A Macquarie Research note flagged potential regulatory headwinds for data-centre development following election outcomes in Texas, Georgia and Ohio, where proposals to impose moratoriums or restrictions on new projects could affect the industry.

Greater scrutiny of power connections, backup-generator emissions, water consumption, zoning and taxation could prolong approvals and raise project costs. The impact may be more pronounced for projects in the pipeline than for facilities that have already secured approvals and power capacity.

Macquarie said approved but unleased data-centre capacity could gain value if fresh supply faces delays, benefiting well-capitalised operators with access to power and approved sites. It remained positive on the digital infrastructure sector.

articles.title: Trump discusses West Asia de-escalation with Qatar's Emir

fullParagraphs: The telephone call between Trump and Qatar's Emir Sheik Tamim bin Hamad al Thani centred on international efforts to end tensions, according to a statement from the Qatari ruler's media office

U.S. President Donald Trump has discussed efforts to de-escalate tensions in the West Asia in a telephone call with Qatar's Emir as the region remained on edge over the possibility of renewed U.S. military action against Iran.
The telephone call between Mr. Trump and Qatar's Emir Sheik Tamim bin Hamad al Thani centred on international efforts to end tensions, according to a statement from the Qatari ruler's media office.
The two discussed in particular Qatar's mediation efforts aimed at reaching “a comprehensive agreement that ends the crisis and achieves security and stability in the region.”

Qatar has been mediating between the United States and Iran to end the war. Qatar and other U.S.-allied Gulf Arab countries came under heavy fire from Iran earlier in the U.S.-Iran war and have been anxious to avoid a new escalation that could leave them vulnerable to attacks.

During the call, Sheik Tamim “stressed the importance of continuing dialogue and adopting diplomatic means to resolve disputes, sparing the region further escalation, and ensuring freedom of maritime navigation and the security of energy supplies,” according to the statement.

articles.title: Europe bomb threats 'likely co-ordinated campaign': Irish government
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The hoaxes in Dublin came as more European flights were also hit on November 6 by bomb threats, the latest this week forcing authorities to reroute some planes or escort civilian aircraft with fighter jets

Ireland's government said on Friday (November 6, 2026) that hoax bomb claims sent to Irish media outlets amid a spate of threats against Europe-wide flights were "likely" part of a "co-ordinated campaign of disruption".

The hoaxes in Dublin came as more European flights were also hit on Friday (November 6, 2026) by bomb threats, the latest this week forcing authorities to reroute some planes or escort civilian aircraft with fighter jets.

The Irish government confirmed police responded after national broadcaster RTE , Virgin Media , Newstalk radio, and The Irish Independent newspaper all received what turned out to be hoax bomb claims.
"It is not known yet who is responsible for these threats, whether it is individuals or a centralised or co-ordinated effort," it said in a statement.
"However, these threats come on the heels of the ongoing disruption to aviation around Europe caused by similar threats, and it seems likely that this is a co-ordinated campaign of disruption."
It added that "the threats made this morning against media organisations here are very serious".
"Hoax threats such as these cause fear, distress and disruption to people going about their daily lives and activities; they achieve no positive purpose whatsoever," the statement said.
It noted police were working alongside Ireland's military, cyber, and aviation authorities, as well as European counterparts, to find the culprits.
"Every effort will be made to identify those responsible and to hold them to account," the government vowed.
Police were promptly deployed to RTE's Dublin headquarters and the other targeted sites following the threats, the outlets reported.

articles.title: Jay Rockefeller, heir to famed dynasty and healthcare advocate in U.S. Senate, dies at 89
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Jay Rockefeller, a tall, soft-spoken Democrat with liberal views, was a great-grandson of oil tycoon John ‌D. Rockefeller and the scion of a family that formed a political dynasty

John D. “Jay” Rockefeller IV, the progeny of one of America’s most famous and wealthiest families, who during three decades in the U.S. Senate sought expanded healthcare for the poor and excoriated President George W. Bush’s handling of ​the Iraq War, died on Friday (November 6, 2026) at his home in Washington, the Washington Post reported. He was 89.
His family did not provide a cause, the ‌newspaper added.

Mr. Rockefeller, a tall, soft-spoken Democrat with liberal views, was elected in 1984 to the first of his ​five six-year terms representing West Virginia in the Senate after two terms as Governor of the poor coal-mining State.

Mr. Rockefeller voted ⁠in 2002 in favour of the Republican Bush’s measure authorising the Iraq war, which began with a U.S.-led invasion in 2003. He later expressed regret over that vote and, as head of the Senate intelligence committee, accused Mr. Bush of taking the nation to war on “false premises.”
He was a great-grandson of oil tycoon John ‌D. Rockefeller and the scion of a family that formed a political dynasty that included his uncle, New York Governor Nelson Rockefeller.
New York-born Jay Rockefeller’s life changed direction after he graduated from Harvard and served in a national service program in ‌impoverished rural West Virginia from 1964 to 1966.

When he was put in public office, he worked to increase healthcare access, ‌fight ⁠poverty, provide health benefits to coal miners and assist military veterans. As a senator, he had a role in shaping ⁠the programme created in 1997 under which the U.S. government helps States provide medical coverage for millions of uninsured children.

Mr. Rockefeller backed Democratic President Bill Clinton’s failed proposal for near-universal health insurance coverage in the 1990s and then fought for Democratic President Barack Obama’s successful quest for a healthcare overhaul law, signed in 2010.

In the debate over Mr. Obama’s measure, Mr. Rockefeller unsuccessfully ​sought to have the federal government offer a medical insurance ‌program to the general population — in addition to existing programs for the poor and elderly — as an alternative to private insurance plans that could be costly and exclusive.

“Championing those most in need has been my life’s calling and I will never stop fighting to make a difference for the people who mean so much to me,” Mr. Rockefeller said in 2013 when he announced at age 75 he would ‌not seek a sixth Senate term.

articles.title: Kerala Police downgrades Pinarayi Vijayan’s personal security from Z+ to Y category
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Governor and Chief Minister have been assigned the highest security category of Z+, while State Ministers, Speaker and Deputy Speaker will receive Y category security with escort
The Kerala Police has downgraded Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan’s personal security from Z+ to Y category.
The decision was made by the security review coordination committee that also reassessed the security arrangements for the protection of other VIPs, including politicians and judicial officers.
Mr. Vijayan will have a pilot vehicle instead of a convoy while travelling. His security details will also include two personal security guards (PSG).

The revised security classifications were issued to Inspector Generals, Deputy Inspectors Generals and District Police Chiefs a few days ago. The review was undertaken to assess the existing threat levels of various leaders, official sources said.
The Governor and Chief Minister have been assigned the highest security category of Z+, while State Ministers, Speaker and Deputy Speaker will receive Y category security with escort.

Among senior politicians, former Chief Minister A.K. Antony will receive Z category security. Union Home Minister of State for Petroleum and Tourism Suresh Gopi, Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] general secretary M.A. Baby and CPI(M) leader P. Jayarajan have been allotted a security category of Y. CPI(M) State secretary M.V. Govindan will receive X category security.

The police have also scaled down or withdrawn security provided earlier to various leaders. Hindu Aikya Vedi leader Valsan Thillankeri, who previously had two PSGs, will only have one as per the revised security arrangements. Besides, the security of BJP State general secretary M.T. Ramesh has been withdrawn.

articles.title: Shivamogga SP suggests students to build ‘fort of knowledge’ and become law-abiding citizens
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Shivamogga Superintendent of Police B. Nikhil on Friday appealed to students to build a “fort of knowledge” by acquiring knowledge through books and to become law-abiding citizens.
Mr. Nikhil was addressing students after inaugurating The Hindu In School Science Fest - Avishkar and Ramanujan Spark Quest, organised in association with Excellent Moodubidire in Shivamogga.

Recalling that kings once built forts to protect their territories from enemies, he said students today should build a strong fort of knowledge. “If you acquire any valuable material, someone can steal it from you. Build a fort of knowledge that nobody can take away from you,” he said.

Highlighting the importance of reading newspapers daily, Mr. Nikhil said he owed much of what he had achieved to The Hindu . He had picked up the habit of reading newspapers as a schoolboy, and it had helped him greatly. He pointed to the paper’s range of coverage, from local, State and national news to world affairs, opinion, business and sports. Its credibility, he said, had endured before and after Independence, withstanding every test in nearly 150 years.

The officer also stressed the importance of communicating in English. Many brilliant students from tier-2 and tier-3 cities fall behind because they lack communication skills, he observed, adding that interviews hinge on how candidates present themselves. “Start speaking in English and don’t worry about mistakes. Make mistakes now, so you can succeed tomorrow. Our biggest teachers are our mistakes,” he said.

Speaking as a police officer, Mr. Nikhil said the law treats everyone equally and must be respected equally by all. “There is always a lawful way to celebrate or protest. Students should not blindly follow individuals or fall prey to manipulation. They should use their own judgement,” he said.
He also warned students against falling into the trap of drugs and advised them to firmly say “beda, bro” to anything illegal.

Citing road accident figures, Mr. Nikhil said that of 358 deaths recorded, 150 were two-wheeler riders who could have survived had they worn helmets. He urged students to ensure that their parents and others around them wear helmets without fail.

Shivamogga Superintendent of Police B. Nikhil on Friday appealed to students to build a “fort of knowledge” by acquiring knowledge through books and to become law-abiding citizens.

Mr. Nikhil was addressing students after inaugurating The Hindu In School Science Fest - Avishkar and Ramanujan Spark Quest, organised in association with Excellent Moodubidire in Shivamogga.

Recalling that kings once built forts to protect their territories from enemies, he said students today should build a strong fort of knowledge. “If you acquire any valuable material, someone can steal it from you. Build a fort of knowledge that nobody can take away from you,” he said.

Highlighting the importance of reading newspapers daily, Mr. Nikhil said he owed much of what he had achieved to The Hindu . He had picked up the habit of reading newspapers as a schoolboy, and it had helped him greatly. He pointed to the paper’s range of coverage, from local, State and national news to world affairs, opinion, business and sports. Its credibility, he said, had endured before and after Independence, withstanding every test in nearly 150 years.

The officer also stressed the importance of communicating in English. Many brilliant students from tier-2 and tier-3 cities fall behind because they lack communication skills, he observed, adding that interviews hinge on how candidates present themselves. “Start speaking in English and don’t worry about mistakes. Make mistakes now, so you can succeed tomorrow. Our biggest teachers are our mistakes,” he said.

Speaking as a police officer, Mr. Nikhil said the law treats everyone equally and must be respected equally by all. “There is always a lawful way to celebrate or protest. Students should not blindly follow individuals or fall prey to manipulation. They should use their own judgement,” he said.

He also warned students against falling into the trap of drugs and advised them to firmly say “beda, bro” to anything illegal.

Citing road accident figures, Mr. Nikhil said that of 358 deaths recorded, 150 were two-wheeler riders who could have survived had they worn helmets. He urged students to ensure that their parents and others around them wear helmets without fail.

articles.title: Pendency of schemes for minorities’ welfare reviewed
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka convened a meeting with legislators and officials on Friday to discuss the status of several welfare schemes of the Minorities Welfare Department.

The meeting saw Minorities Welfare Minister Mohammed Azharuddin and All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen legislator Akbaruddin Owaisi interacting with the Deputy Chief Minister, who, according to Mr. Azharuddin’s office, respomded positively.

The non-receipt of pre-matric scholarships by minority students and a proposal to introduce a State-funded scholarship scheme were discussed. The long standing issue of pending dues of the Reimbursement of Tuition Fee (RTF) and Maintenance Fee (MTF) schemes, prioritisation of pending applications, and the status of the Chief Minister’s Overseas Scholarship scheme, were also reviewed.

The meeting also took up delays in the verification and clearance of pending applications under the Shaadi Mubarak scheme. The proposal to reappropriate surplus funds under Shaadi Mubarak for the RTF and MTF schemes was discussed, along with concerns over the reduction in the RTF budget allocation for the current financial year.

Also discussed were pending developmental works in Old City. Sources said that the Deputy Chief Minister assured that a detailed inspection of pending works in Old City will be conducted soon. He also said the foundation stone for the new Haj House will be laid shortly and assured reforms to improve the functioning of the Minority Welfare Department.

articles.title: Rajasthan police rescue six minors forced into sex work, five arrested
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The police acted after taking cognisance of a ‘Ground Zero’ report in August by The Hindu.

The Rajasthan police has rescued six minor girls of the Banchhada community in Jhalawar district and arrested five people – most of whom were related to the girls – for allegedly pushing them into sex work, officers said on Friday (November 6, 2026).

Speaking to The Hindu , Jhalawar Superintendent of Police (SP) Amit Kumar said that the girls, aged between 12 and 17, were rescued in raids conducted in the Bhawanimandi area on November 3 and that medical and forensic examinations have confirmed sexual exploitation of five of the girls.
Two of the girls have also tested positive for sexually transmitted diseases (STDs).

Mr. Kumar said that the action was taken after the police took cognisance of a ‘Ground Zero’ report by The Hindu , which had in August highlighted the problem of children being forced into the sex trade in Madhya Pradesh’s Mandsaur, Neemuch and Ratlam districts.

The Banchhada community, a de-notified tribe , is mainly spread across various districts of Madhya Pradesh’s Nimar region and Rajasthan’s Mewar region. The community has long been infamous for being involved in traditional sex work, often by forcing their daughters into sex work from an early age, with their family members and relatives working as pimps.
As per the Jhalawar police, the community has a significant population in about 5-6 villages in the district.

Mr. Kumar said that an SIT headed by Additional SP Ayush Shrotriya was formed for the operation, after which two officers were sent to localities where the community had a presence to gather digital evidence with the help of spy cameras.

“After verifying the digital evidence and intelligence inputs, raids were conducted in localities of the community with over 100 personnel – including women personnel in civil dress – and six girls were rescued,” the officer said.

Mr. Kumar said that an FIR under Sections 3, 4, and 5 of the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, and Sections 5, 6, 11, 12 and 17 of the The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act has been lodged at Bhawanimandi police station.
He said that a separate SIT under Additional SP Bhagchandra Meena has been formed for further investigation into the case.

articles.title: RPF seizes 6 kg of ganja worth ₹3 lakh at Thrissur railway station
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 19-year-old West Bengal native held; says he was promised ₹20,000 to deliver the consignment at Aluva

The Railway Protection Force (RPF) seized 6 kg of ganja, estimated to be worth ₹3 lakh, and arrested a 19-year-old native of West Bengal at the Thrissur railway station on Friday. The seizure was made by the RPF Crime Intelligence Branch, Thiruvananthapuram, during a special inspection to curb drug trafficking through trains.

The accused, identified as Ashik Sekh of Murshidabad district in West Bengal, was intercepted after he alighted from the general coach of Train No. 12660 (Shalimar–Nagercoil) with a bag. A search of the bag led to the recovery of the contraband.

According to officials, the accused had boarded the train at Bhubaneswar with a general ticket. During questioning, he reportedly told the authorities that he had been instructed to hand over the bag to someone at Aluva and was promised a commission of ₹20,000 for the delivery.

The operation was conducted under the supervision of Jipin A.J., Inspector, Crime Intelligence Branch, following directions from Mohammed Haneefa, Senior Divisional Security Commissioner, RPF, Thiruvananthapuram.

The accused and the seized ganja were handed over to the Railway Police in Thrissur for further legal action. A case has been registered under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act.
The RPF had also seized 37.5 kg of ganja wrapped in jaggery recently. Officials said inspections would be intensified in view of the Deepavali season.

articles.title: Iran Guards say two tankers caught fire in Hormuz
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Since the outbreak of the West Asia war on February 28, Tehran has sought to limit traffic through the strategic waterway, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said in a statement carried by state media on Friday (November 6, 2026) that two oil tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, a day after Tehran claimed five other tankers had similar fates.
Since the outbreak of the West Asia war on February 28, Tehran has sought to limit traffic through the strategic waterway, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption.
The United States has in response imposed a blockade on Iranian ports and escorted tankers through the strait.

U.S. Central Command said last month that it had helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil via Hormuz since the summer and has recently said that all mines have been cleared from the waterway.

"Two violating oil tankers — one east of the Strait of Hormuz and the other within the Strait itself — that attempted to transit via an unauthorised route struck mines," the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, the ideological arm of Iran's military, said in a statement carried by state TV.

"The two tankers had deactivated all of their navigation and identification systems and were attempting to exit the Strait of Hormuz... with the support of the aggressor and terrorist American military, but following the collision with mines, they caught fire and were brought to a stop," the statement added.
On Thursday (November 5, 2026), Iranian media reported that five oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz in similar incidents.
There has, however, been no confirmation of any of these incidents from maritime officials.

articles.title: Israel Opposition eases on ultra-Orthodox draft to oust Netanyahu
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Listing the most important goals as removing Netanyahu and avoiding new elections, Opposition partner Avigdor Liberman said it was time to compromise and "understand that trying to have everything risks getting nothing".

Israel's Opposition saw a new path on Friday (October 6, 2026) to oust Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as one of its leaders backtracked on demands that ultra-Orthodox Jews serve in the military, opening the door to a once improbable alliance with the community.
Neither Mr. Netanyahu nor Opposition chief Gadi Eisenkot reached a majority in the October 27 election, with Israeli society highly polarised over Mr. Netanyahu and worn down by three years of war.

Mr. Eisenkot, a former military commander whose campaign sought to appeal to secular and liberal Israelis, could form a government with Israeli-Arabs, whose seat count soared on anger over Mr. Netanyahu's far-right government.

But an alliance with Israeli-Arabs faces strong disagreement from Opposition partner Avigdor Liberman, a one-time aide to Mr. Netanyahu who now sharply criticises the Prime Minister but shares his hawkish views on the Palestinians.

Mr. Liberman said on Friday (November 6, 2026) he would not back down on refusing to work with Israeli-Arabs but called for talks with ultra-Orthodox Jews, even though he has berated the community for years and ran on promises to end its exemption from Israel's mandatory military service.

Listing the most important goals as removing Mr. Netanyahu and avoiding new elections, Mr. Liberman said it was time to compromise and "understand that trying to have everything risks getting nothing".
"This also includes the issue of the conscription law," he said in a social media statement.

"This pains me, and I know it pains many others as well. But given the full range of challenges we face today, the national interest of the State of Israel and the Jewish people must take precedence over all other considerations."

President Isaac Herzog plans on Sunday (November 8, 2026) to announce who will have the first chance to form a government — most logically Mr. Eisenkot, as he has received the most endorsements thanks to support from Israeli-Arabs.
Yair Golan, Israel's main left-wing leader and part of the Opposition bloc, said "serious work" was underway to form a coalition.

However, The search is still on for the remaining two fishermen using an aircraft. A team of scuba diving experts have also come from Visakhapatnam, along with local Marine Police officials and personnel from Chennai, to inspect the capsized boat.

According to Indian Coast Guard (ICG) officials, the two bodies were found near Vajjireddypalem and Singarayakonda villages of Prakasam district. After consulting with the officials from Tamil Nadu, they confirmed that the deceased were identified as Kuppan and Aravind.
The five bodies of fishermen, which were kept at the mortuary of RIMS Hospital in Ongole, have been identified as Mohan, Murugan, Vijayakanth, Pakkiri Samy and Kuppus.

articles.title: APPTD directs 161 DDOs to install QR code-based feedback posters
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Andhra Pradesh Public Transport Department (APPTD-APSRTC) has directed all its 161 Drawing and Disbursing Officers (DDOs) to install QR code-based visitor feedback posters at prominent locations in their respective offices to facilitate public feedback on government services and employee performance.

A statement issued on Friday said the initiative was aimed at providing visitors with a simple and convenient mechanism to share their experiences and opinions on the functioning of government offices, thereby improving transparency, accountability and service delivery.

The instructions follow a government directive issued on October 11, which noted that only 15,927 of the 35,926 government offices across Andhra Pradesh had displayed the prescribed QR code posters, leaving the exercise pending in several offices.
Against this backdrop, the APPTD has asked all its 161 DDOs to complete the installation on top priority.

The department expects the QR code-based feedback mechanism to encourage public participation and provide the government with valuable inputs on the quality of services delivered. The feedback is also expected to help identify areas requiring improvement and make government offices more responsive to citizens’ needs and expectations.

articles.title: Officials told to make fool proof arrangements for CII Partnership Summit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: CII Partnership Summit will be held on November 12 and 13 at the Andhra University Engineering College grounds in Visakhapatnam

Special Chief Secretary (Youth Advancement, Tourism and Culture) Shamsher Singh Rawat on Friday (November 6, 2026) directed officials of all departments to work in coordination and make elaborate arrangements for the CII Partnership Summit to be held on November 12 and 13, 2026, in Visakhapatnam.

Reviewing the preparations with State and district-level officials at the Collectorate, along with Collector M. Abhishikth Kishore, Mr. Rawat said all advance measures should be taken so that delegates from India and abroad face no inconvenience. A command and control room should coordinate with the departments, and liaison officers should be well versed in their duties, the needs of guests and the programme details.

Special tourism circuits and trained guides should be arranged to introduce local attractions to foreign guests, he said. Hop-on hop-off buses should be used, welcome and signage boards put up on routes to tourist sites, and the summit publicised across the city.

The Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) was told to speed up civil works, beautification and sanitation, and install CCTV cameras where needed. Structural, fire and electrical safety, and public address systems at the venues should be inspected and certified. All measures should be taken for the security of guests.

A reception desk and a welcome team should be set up at the airport to receive guests in keeping with Telugu traditions, including with traditional shawls. Accommodation, transport, protocol, and the welcome and gala dinners should be handled meticulously. Registration desks should be set up on the engineering college ground opposite the main venue, with parking, a traffic plan and mobile toilets, officials were instructed.

Mr. Kishore said that the control room would function from November 9. Registration and issue of passes would be monitored from the Collectorate, with officials of the departments concerned available at the control room.
Police Commissioner Shankhabrata Bagchi and GVMC Commissioner Ketan Garg were among those present.

articles.title: OBC creamy layer verdict not a blanket revision of service allocations, seniority: Supreme Court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: March 11 judgment determined only rights of candidates who approached the court; it held they fell within non-creamy layer of OBC category

The Supreme Court on Friday (November 6, 2026) clarified that its March 11, 2026 judgment, upholding a 1993 Office Memorandum which excluded parental salary and agricultural income from the income/wealth test for determining OBC non-creamy layer status, did not call for a sweeping revision of service allocations or seniority across successive recruitment years.

A Bench of Justices P.S. Narasimha and R. Mahadevan, in its order, said the Union government, represented by Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, had erred in assuming that a “retrospective implementation of the March 11 judgment would have far-reaching consequences for recruitment, service and cadre allocation, seniority and admissions to Higher Educational Institutions”.

In a series of applications, the Centre had expressed apprehensions that a retrospective application of the court’s verdict on the assessment of creamy-layer status would unsettle the completed selection process and prejudice candidates. Mr. Mehta had specifically taken the case of the Civil Service Examination (CSE) 2025, of which the results had been announced five days prior to the judgment on March 6.

The government had argued the “potential impact” of the judgment on more than 6.69 lakh reserved vacancies, including 3.7 lakh OBC vacancies, filled over the preceding ten years across various government departments and public institutions, as well as the consequential effects on seniority, pay, promotional prospects and the Foundation Course for CSE-2025 candidates.

Addressing these apprehensions, the court made it clear that the judgment “cannot be construed as directing a general revision of service allocations or seniority across successive recruitment years, nor does it confer individual relief upon persons who were not parties to the original proceedings”.

The court clarified that although the result of the Civil Service Examination 2025 was declared on March 6, services had still not been allocated to the successful candidates. It said that since the process of allocation was pending, there would be no reasonable justification to defer the implementation of the March 11 judgment. It said the creamy layer principle, as interpreted in the judgment, would govern the allocation of services of OBC candidates selected through the Civil Service Examination 2025.
Justice Mahadevan clarified that the March 11 judgment had determined only the rights of the parties (candidates) who approached the Supreme Court.

“We find no observation or direction [in the March 11 judgment] requiring the Union government to revisit appointments already made, revise the seniority of any person, or undertake any selection, appointment or service allocation exercise afresh. No direction was issued for the retrospective reopening of concluded selections, appointments or service allocations so as to affect the rights of persons who were not parties to the proceedings,” Justice Mahadevan, who authored the order, set the record straight.

The judgment had held that the candidates who approached the apex court, represented by advocate Shashank Ratnoo, fell within the non-creamy layer of the OBC category and were clearly entitled to the benefit of reservation together with consequential placement and allotment of posts in the selection processes in which they participated.

“The grant of such benefit shall not, by itself, operate to the detriment of the seniority of any other person or entail the reopening of selections or appointments already concluded… The ratio laid down in the judgment shall not, by itself, furnish a ground for reopening selections or appointments already concluded prior to the judgment dated March 11, 2026,” the court reiterated.

articles.title: Stakeholders oppose Karnataka govt.’s move to make private schools adopt govt. schools
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Educationalists, student organisations, academicians, teachers and other stakeholders have criticised the State government’s plan to link government schools with private schools through adoption.

Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar recently held a meeting with private schools and companies, where he proposed the adoption of government schools by private schools and other firms under Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) funds.
The Save Public Education Committee and the All India Democratic Students’ Organisation (AIDSO) termed the initiative an attempt by the State government to shut down government schools.

“We strongly condemn this anti-people move. The government has allowed private schools to even tag their names to adopted government schools. By doing this, the government is trying to escape its responsibility to address the deficiencies in the public education system,” the committee said.

The committee also condemned remarks allegedly made by representatives of private schools at the meeting against government school teachers, including by Aishwarya DKS Hegde, daughter of Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and Trustee Secretary of the National Education Foundation. “During the interaction, they said the quality of teachers in government schools is low. They shifted the entire blame onto teachers while ignoring the role of the government’s own policies in creating the situation,” the committee said.

Meanwhile, teachers have expressed displeasure over the remarks. “Teachers are burdened with non-academic work. For example, this year we were deputed for Special Intensive Revision (SIR) work. We have been stuck with non-academic work for a year now, and the national census is due next year. Private school teachers do not have to do such work,” a government school teacher said.

A.H. Ningegowda, president of the Karnataka State Pre-University Lecturers’ Association, urged the government to fill vacant posts first and allow teachers to do their work instead of criticising them.

articles.title: Bangladesh rescues Rohingya refugees in border gun battle
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: One soldier was killed in the clash on November 5 night, the military's Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said.

Bangladesh security forces rescued at least 57 people, including Rohingya refugees, during a gun battle with suspected human traffickers near the Myanmar border, the military said on Friday (November 6, 2026).
One soldier was killed in the clash on Thursday (November 5, 2026) night, the military's Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said.

ISPR said that security forces launched an operation in the hills of Rongikhali in Teknaf, close to the border with Myanmar, after receiving a tip-off that an armed gang of 15 to 16 suspected traffickers had abducted around 120 Rohingya refugees and Bangladeshis.
"During the exchange of fire, an army soldier, Md. Titash Sheikh, was shot. The bullet struck his left shoulder. He was bleeding profusely," the statement said.
Bangladesh hosts more than 1.2 million Rohingya refugees, most of whom fled a brutal military crackdown in neighbouring Myanmar in 2017.
Many live in sprawling camps around Cox's Bazar, near the border, where trafficking gangs prey on refugees seeking work or passage abroad.
The 2017 Myanmar crackdown, which saw Rohingya villages burned and civilians killed, is the subject of a genocide case at the UN's top court in The Hague.
